entries.odia: ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ହୋଇ ଦୀପରୁଖାରେ ଚଢ଼ିବା
entries.title: An ant climbing the lampstand
entries.literal_meaning: Being an ant and climbing onto the lampstand.
entries.explanation: The dictionary applies this small creature and high perch to a “small” person intervening in “big” matters. The wording does more than describe scale: it can dismiss someone’s right to take part by placing them below the subject under discussion. That ranking belongs to the source’s social judgment, not a fact about anyone’s worth or ability. Read critically, the analogy lets us hear how a vivid image can keep a person out of a conversation instead of answering what they said.
entries.meaning_odia: ଛୋଟ ପିମ୍ପୁଡ଼ି ଓ ଉଚ୍ଚ ଦୀପରୁଖାର ଛବିକୁ ଅଭିଧାନ ‘ଛୋଟ ଲୋକ’ ହୋଇ ‘ବଡ଼ କଥା’ରେ ହସ୍ତକ୍ଷେପ କରିବା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ିଛି। ଏହା କେବଳ ଆକାରର ତୁଳନା ନୁହେଁ; କାହାକୁ ତୁଚ୍ଛ କରି ତାଙ୍କ କଥା କହିବାର ଅଧିକାରକୁ ଅସ୍ୱୀକାର କରିବାର ସ୍ୱର ମଧ୍ୟ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି। ସେହି ଉଚ୍ଚନୀଚ ବିଚାର ସ୍ରୋତର ପ୍ରୟୋଗର ଅଂଶ, କାହାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ବା ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ। ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରି ପଢ଼ିଲେ ଦେଖାଯାଏ, ଉତ୍ତର ଦେବା ବଦଳରେ ଏକ ଚିତ୍ର କିପରି ଲୋକଟିକୁ ଆଲୋଚନାରୁ ବାହାରେ ରଖିପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: A historical analogy can dismiss a supposedly insignificant person’s participation in larger matters.
entries.odia_summary: କାହାକୁ ତୁଚ୍ଛ ଭାବି ବଡ଼ କଥାରେ ତାଙ୍କ ଅଂଶଗ୍ରହଣକୁ ଖାରଜ କରିବାର ଏକ ପୁରୁଣା ଉପମା।
entries.usage_example: At a residents’ meeting, a newcomer questions an expense. Someone dismisses the question with “ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ହୋଇ ଦୀପରୁଖାରେ ଚଢ଼ିବା.” Another resident replies that the question should be answered, whoever asked it. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
entries.cultural_context: An unnumbered analogy follows note3 and precedes5 in both witnesses; labelled fourth position for this audit only. Source’s ଛୋଟ ଲୋକ is not evidence of a named caste, innate inferiority or lack of ability. Critical reading preserves the dismissive register, not an endorsed lesson to stay in one’s place.

entries.odia: ହାତୀ ମୁହଁରୁ କଳେ ଖସି ପଡ଼ିଲେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିକୁ ଖାଇବାକୁ ଶହେ ବରଷ ନ୍ୟାୟ
entries.literal_meaning: If a mouthful falls from an elephant’s mouth, an ant has food for a hundred years.
entries.explanation: The joke makes the same scrap almost nothing to one creature and an enormous provision to another. The dictionary extends the contrast to an elephant-like person leaving a small amount that can sustain many ant-like lives. The hundred years is the saying’s extravagant measure of scale, not a feeding calculation. The comparison can make an overlooked remainder suddenly look substantial.
entries.meaning_odia: ହାତୀ ପାଇଁ କଳେ ମାତ୍ର ଖାଦ୍ୟ, ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ପାଇଁ ଶହେ ବରଷର ଖୋରାକ—ଏହି ମାପର ତଫାତରେ କଥାଟିର ମଜା। ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ହାତୀ ପରି ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଅଳ୍ପ କିଛି ଛାଡ଼ିଗଲେ ସେଥିରେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ପରି ଅନେକ ଜୀବ ପୋଷିହେବାର କଥା ଅଛି। ଶହେ ବରଷ ଏଠାରେ ଅତିଶୟୋକ୍ତି। ଜଣକ ପାଇଁ ତୁଚ୍ଛ ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣକ ପାଇଁ କେତେ ବଡ଼ ହୋଇପାରେ, ଚିତ୍ରଟି ସେହି ତଫାତ ଦେଖାଏ।
entries.english_summary: A tiny remainder to one can be a large provision to another.
entries.odia_summary: ଜଣକର କଳେ ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣକର ବହୁତ ଖୋରାକ।

entries.title: An elephant’s mouthful, an ant’s hundred years
entries.usage_example: A large printing shop offers its unused paper offcuts to a small drawing club. Seeing how many sketchbooks they can make, a member quotes the elephant-and-ant analogy. (Original imagined use.)
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary explicitly interprets unequal scale through elephant-like and ant-like figures. This records a comparison, not a claim that people have unequal worth or a historical account of patronage.

entries.odia: ହାତୀ ମୁତି ଦେଲେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ପହଁରାଏ ନ୍ୟାୟ
entries.literal_meaning: When an elephant urinates, the ants swim.
entries.explanation: The blunt bodily image makes scale impossible to miss: an ordinary discharge for the elephant becomes a flood for the ants. The dictionary’s gloss goes further than the heading’s swimming and says the smaller creatures drown. The contrast can picture how a large actor’s small action overwhelms those with much less room to absorb it; that application is editorial, rather than a separate use supplied by the dictionary.
entries.meaning_odia: ହାତୀ ମୁତିଦେବା ପରି ସାଧାରଣ କାମ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ପାଇଁ ପହଁରିବାର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି କରିଦିଏ। ବଡ଼ ଓ ସାନର ମାପକୁ ଏହି ଖୋଲା ଦେହଜ ଚିତ୍ର ତୀବ୍ର କରେ। ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ି ବୁଡ଼ିଯିବା କଥା ଅଛି। ବଡ଼ ପକ୍ଷର ଅଳ୍ପ କାମର ପ୍ରଭାବ ସାନ ପକ୍ଷ ପାଇଁ କେତେ ଭାରି ହୋଇପାରେ—ଏପରି ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ଚିତ୍ରଟିର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପାଠ; ଉତ୍ସରେ ଅଲଗା ସାମାଜିକ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: An ordinary act at one scale can overwhelm life at another.
entries.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ଜୀବର ସାଧାରଣ କାମ ସାନ ଜୀବ ପାଇଁ ବିପଦ।

entries.literal_meaning: The analogy of ants eating up the jaggery store.
entries.explanation: The sweet store is something the ants will keep returning to. The dictionary applies the image to work that must always be guarded carefully against an enemy. Its emphasis is continuing exposure, rather than a single finished loss. Unlike putting an ant in charge of the store, this analogy does not appoint the eater as guardian.
entries.meaning_odia: ଗୁଡ଼ଘରକୁ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିର ଆସିବା ଥରେ ଜଗିଦେଲେ ଶେଷ ହୋଇଯିବା ପରି ନୁହେଁ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରକୁ ଶତ୍ରୁଠାରୁ ସର୍ବଦା ସାବଧାନତା ସହ ରକ୍ଷା କରିବାକୁ ଥିବା କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଏଠାରେ ଜୋର ଲଗାତାର ସତର୍କତା ଉପରେ। ଗୁଡ଼ଘରେ ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିକୁ ଜଗୁଆଳି କରିବାର ଅନ୍ୟ ନ୍ୟାୟଠାରୁ ଏହା ଅଲଗା; ଏଠାରେ ଖାଦକକୁ ରକ୍ଷାର ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ଦେବା କଥା ନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: The source applies the sweet-store image to work needing continuing protection.

entries.explanation: This is a visual comparison rather than a rebuke. The dictionary describes a place where many people gather and compares their movement to a line of ants. The eye follows the continuing file of people. The source does not turn the image into a lesson about obedience, hard work or unquestioning conformity.

entries.literal_meaning: The analogy of ants being mad for jaggery.
entries.explanation: The ants’ pull towards sweetness supplies a picture of someone’s marked eagerness or greed. The dictionary allows both interest and greed, so the comparison need not carry the same accusation on every occasion. A playful comment about enthusiasm can turn sharp when the attraction is self-serving. The object of desire need not be food.
entries.meaning_odia: ଗୁଡ଼ ପ୍ରତି ପିମ୍ପୂଡ଼ିର ଆକର୍ଷଣକୁ ଧରି ଜଣକର ବିଶେଷ ଆଗ୍ରହ କିମ୍ବା ଲୋଭ ବୁଝାଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଦୁଇଟି ଅର୍ଥର ସୁଯୋଗ ରଖିଛି। ତେଣୁ ପ୍ରତିଥର ଏହାକୁ କଠୋର ଲୋଭର ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିଦେଲେ କଥାର ସ୍ୱର ବଦଳିଯିବ। ଅବସର ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହା ଆଗ୍ରହକୁ ନେଇ ହାଲୁକା ଥଟ୍ଟା ହୋଇପାରେ, କିମ୍ବା ଲାଭ ପାଇଁ ବ୍ୟାକୁଳତାକୁ ବିନ୍ଧିପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: An attraction can be playful eagerness or pointedly described greed.

entries.title: Still reaching for the pulse store
entries.literal_meaning: After eating so much, the belly is still not full; you are reaching into the stored black gram.
entries.explanation: The speaker points out a comic excess: even a substantial meal has not stopped the hand reaching for more. The dictionary places the line under having a full meal; the appetite and the reaching hand are its concrete scene. It can be read as a teasing complaint that someone has already had plenty yet still wants another share. That broader application is an editorial reading, not an additional dictionary gloss. Tone matters: the joke need not be turned into a judgment about a person’s body or genuine hunger.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏତେ ଖାଇସାରି ମଧ୍ୟ ପେଟ ପୂରିଲା ନାହିଁ, ହାତ ପୁଣି ବିରି ରଖାଥିବା ଓଳିଆ ଆଡ଼କୁ ଯାଉଛି—ଏହି ବଢ଼ିଚାଲିଥିବା ଚାହିଦାରେ କଥାଟିର ଖୋଚା। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଭୋଜନରେ ପେଟ ପୂରିବା ଅର୍ଥର ଉଦାହରଣ। ନିଜ ଭାଗରେ ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ପାଇସାରି ଆହୁରି ମାଗୁଥିବା ଜଣକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ଧରି ଥଟ୍ଟା କରାଯାଇପାରେ; ଏହା ଆମର ପ୍ରୟୋଗମୂଳକ ପାଠ। ହସରେ କୁହାଯାଇଥିବା କଥା ଯେପରି କାହାର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଭୋକ କିମ୍ବା ଶରୀରକୁ ଅପମାନ ନକରେ, ସେଥିରେ କହିବାର ସ୍ୱର ଓ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିର ଫରକ ଅଛି।
entries.english_summary: A reaching hand makes a teasing picture of wanting more after already having plenty.
entries.odia_summary: ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ପାଇସାରି ମଧ୍ୟ ଆହୁରି ଚାହିଁବାକୁ ଖୋଚା ଦିଏ ଏହି ଭୋଜନର ଚିତ୍ର।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: At a drawing club, everyone receives a packet of paper. One member has already taken two spare packets and now reaches for the last one. A friend laughs and quotes the saying, asking them to leave something for the others. The joke concerns their extra share, not their appetite or body.
entries.cultural_context: The food image is retained as a conversational tease. The source supplies the literal full-meal sense, not a general moral definition. The storage object is retained as ଓଳିଆ in Odia; its construction has not been independently established here.

entries.odia: ଯେବେ ପାଇଥାଏ ଘଇତାବୁକୁ, ସଜ ହେଉଥାଏ ବାପ ଘରକୁ
entries.title: An assurance, then preparations
entries.literal_meaning: When she receives encouragement or a promise from her husband, she gets ready to go to her father’s home.
entries.explanation: The local expression ଘଇତାବୁକୁ is defined as encouragement or a promise from a husband. The saying follows that assurance with the quick, visible response of getting ready to visit her parental home. The paired endings give the movement from words to preparations a light, teasing rhythm. The source does not tell us whether the promise concerns travel, money or something else, so none of those details is treated as fixed. Read as a conversational scene, it catches the eagerness with which a welcome assurance can become action.
entries.meaning_odia: ଘଇତାବୁକୁ ମାନେ ସ୍ୱାମୀଙ୍କଠାରୁ ମିଳିଥିବା ଉତ୍ସାହ ବା ଅଙ୍ଗୀକାର ବଚନ—ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ଅର୍ଥ ଦେଇଛି। ସେହି କଥା ପାଇବା ସାଙ୍ଗେ ସାଙ୍ଗେ ବାପଘରକୁ ଯିବାର ସଜବାଜ ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୋଇଯାଏ। ବୁକୁ ଓ ଘରକୁର ମିଳ ଏହି ତତ୍ପରତାକୁ ହାଲୁକା ଥଟ୍ଟାର ସ୍ୱର ଦିଏ। ଅଙ୍ଗୀକାରଟି ଯାତାୟାତ, ଟଙ୍କା କିମ୍ବା ଆଉ କେଉଁ ବିଷୟରେ, ଉତ୍ସ ତାହା କହେନାହିଁ। ମନକୁ ସୁହାଇଲା ଭଳି କଥାଟିଏ ମିଳିଲେ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି କେମିତି ଚଟାପଟ ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୁଏ, କଥାଟିକୁ ସେହି ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ିହୁଏ।
entries.english_summary: A welcome assurance is followed by eager preparations for a visit home.
entries.odia_summary: ମନକୁ ସୁହାଇଲା ଅଙ୍ଗୀକାର ମିଳିଲେ ବାପଘରକୁ ଯିବାର ସଜବାଜ ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୋଇଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A woman has been hoping to visit her parents. Her husband offers to take over their shared errands that weekend, and she immediately starts packing. Her sister smiles and quotes the saying at the speed of the preparations. The offered help is an invented detail of this example, not part of the historical wording.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary marks the headword as a rural figurative expression. The saying presents a husband-and-wife situation; it does not establish a rule that a woman needs permission to visit her family. No particular region, marriage custom or historical incident is inferred.

entries.odia: ଜହ୍ନିଫୁଲ ପରି ଆୟୁଷ ପା ସଞ୍ଜେ ଫୁଟି ସକାଳେ ଯା
entries.title: A blessing that lasts one night
entries.literal_meaning: Have a lifespan like the jahni flower: bloom at dusk and be gone by morning.
entries.explanation: The line opens like a blessing for someone’s life, then gives that life only the span from dusk to morning. The dictionary explicitly marks it as an ironic blessing and says it is spoken in jest. That reversal, rather than a gentle wish for longevity, is the point of the joke. The flower supplies the source’s image of brevity; this explanation is not a botanical lifespan claim. Depending on the relationship and occasion, such a mock blessing can sound playful or cruel.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆୟୁଷ ପା ବୋଲି କଥାଟି ଆଶୀର୍ବାଦ ଭଳି ଆରମ୍ଭ ହୁଏ, ହେଲେ ସେହି ଆୟୁଷ ସଞ୍ଜରୁ ସକାଳ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ମାତ୍ର। ଦୀର୍ଘ ଜୀବନର ଆଶାକୁ ଏମିତି ଓଲଟାଇ ଦେବାରେ ତାହାର ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହାକୁ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗୋକ୍ତିମୂଳକ ଆଶୀର୍ବଚନ କହିଛି ଓ ଥଟ୍ଟାରେ କୁହାଯାଏ ବୋଲି ଲେଖିଛି। ଫୁଲ ଏଠାରେ ଅଳ୍ପ ସମୟର ଚିତ୍ର ହୋଇ ଆସିଛି। କିଏ କାହାକୁ କେଉଁ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିରେ କହୁଛି, ସେହି ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହି ଓଲଟା ଆଶୀର୍ବାଦ ହସ ମଧ୍ୟ ଆଣିପାରେ, ଆଘାତ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: An apparent blessing turns into a sharp joke about a life lasting only from dusk to morning.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଶୀର୍ବାଦ ଭଳି ଶୁଣାଯାଉଥିବା କଥାଟି ସଞ୍ଜରୁ ସକାଳର ଆୟୁଷ ଦେଇ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A friend announces yet another promise to start a daily walk tomorrow. Remembering yesterday’s abandoned plan, another friend quotes the flower blessing about the new promise, and both laugh at how briefly the last resolve lasted. Applying the image to a promise rather than a person’s life is an editorial transfer in this example.
entries.cultural_context: This is a documented mock blessing, not an instruction to wish someone harm. The printed entry’s dusk/morning wording supports the irony; no particular ceremony, speaker, first author or origin event is established. Surrounding dictionary material on a flower-related observance is a separate entry and is not imported as this saying’s origin.
entries.origin_note: Earliest use and origin unverified. Printed dictionary attestation is not proof of first composition.

entries.odia: କେତେ ଅନଉଛୁ ମତେ, ତୋଠଉଁ ସୁନ୍ଦର ମୋର ବିନୋଦିଆ, ଚାକର ରଖିବ ତତେ
entries.title: A boast that puts the onlooker in place
entries.literal_meaning: Why keep looking at me? My charming one is more beautiful than you and could keep you as a servant.
entries.explanation: The line answers someone who keeps looking at the speaker by praising another person as more beautiful. The dictionary explains “keep as a servant” here as figurative superiority in wealth or qualities, so the comparison is not a report of employment. One possible performance is a proud rebuff to an admirer: the speaker boasts that a favoured person would far outshine this supposed rival. Neither admiration nor a romantic relationship is fixed by the source gloss, however. The repeated address gives the comparison a personal, theatrical edge. Its status hierarchy is part of the rhetoric, not a measure of anyone’s human worth.
entries.meaning_odia: କେହି ଚାହିଁରହିଥିବା ବେଳେ ଏହି କଥାର ବକ୍ତା ନିଜ ପ୍ରିୟଜଣଙ୍କ ସୁନ୍ଦରତାକୁ ବଢ଼ାଇ କହି ସେହି ଚାହାଣିର ଜବାବ ଦିଅନ୍ତି। ଚାକର ରଖିବାକୁ ଅଭିଧାନ ଏଠାରେ ଧନ ବା ଗୁଣରେ ଉତ୍କୃଷ୍ଟ ହେବାର ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥ ଦେଇଛି। ଯିଏ ନିଜକୁ ପ୍ରତିଦ୍ୱନ୍ଦ୍ୱୀ ଭାବୁଥାଇପାରେ, ତାକୁ ପ୍ରିୟଜଣଙ୍କଠାରୁ ବହୁତ ତଳେ ରଖିଦେବାରେ ଏହି ଉତ୍ତରର ଖୋଚା। ଏହା ନିଜ ପ୍ରିୟଜଣଙ୍କୁ ନେଇ ଗର୍ବ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ମିଶିଥିବା ଏକ ନାଟକୀୟ ଜବାବ ଭଳି ଶୁଣାଯାଏ; ପ୍ରେମର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଏହାର ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପାଠ। କାମ ବା ସାମାଜିକ ସ୍ଥିତି ଦେଇ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ମାପିବାକୁ ଏହି ପାଠ ସମର୍ଥନ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A pointed comparison answers an onlooker with a boast about someone else’s beauty.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଜ ପ୍ରିୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଗର୍ବ କରି ଚାହିଁରହିଥିବା ଜଣକୁ ଖୋଚା ଦେଉଥିବା ଉତ୍ତର।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: During a light-hearted drama rehearsal, one character keeps posing to catch another character’s eye. The other quotes this line, praising someone supposedly more beautiful. The performers choose to play it as a proud rebuff to an admirer; that relationship is invented for this scene, not established by the dictionary. They treat the employment comparison as exaggeration rather than a reason to mock an occupation.
entries.cultural_context: The source supplies a figurative status comparison, not a named romance or biographical episode. Charming one renders ବିନୋଦିଆ without fixing a romantic relationship; the speaker’s gender and any historical characters are not established. The employment hierarchy should remain visible as rhetoric without being endorsed.

entries.odia: ହାଣ୍ଡିରେ ଖାଏ, ଗୋଡ଼ରେ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ଗାଧୋଇ ଯାଏ
entries.title: Good enough to eat, too much to touch
entries.literal_meaning: One eats from the pot, but goes to bathe when its contents fall on the foot.
entries.explanation: The same food is welcome in the mouth and suddenly objectionable on the foot. That abrupt change is the comic hinge of the line: acceptance in one situation turns into an elaborate response in another. The dictionary supplies the bathing sense but no separate moral gloss. Our reading treats the contrast as a possible tease about selective fastidiousness or inconsistent standards. It does not establish that bathing is always excessive, or that a particular ritual or community is being described.
entries.meaning_odia: ହାଣ୍ଡିରୁ ଖାଇବା ବେଳେ ଯାହା ଗ୍ରହଣୀୟ, ସେହି ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଗୋଡ଼ରେ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ଗାଧୋଇବାକୁ ଯିବାର କଥା ଆସୁଛି। ଏକେ ଜିନିଷକୁ ଦୁଇ ପରିସ୍ଥିତିରେ ଏତେ ଅଲଗା ଭାବେ ନେବାରେ ଏହାର ହାସ୍ୟ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଗାଧୋଇବା କ୍ରିୟାର ଉଦାହରଣ ଭାବେ କଥାଟି ଅଛି; ଅଲଗା ନୀତିକଥା ଦିଆଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଏହି ବିପରୀତ ଆଚରଣକୁ ଧରି ଅତି ବାଛବିଚାର ବା ବଦଳୁଥିବା ମାପକାଠିକୁ ଥଟ୍ଟା କରିହୁଏ। ସ୍ୱରଟି ଘନିଷ୍ଠ ହସର ହୋଇପାରେ, ପୁଣି ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟର ମଧ୍ୟ ହୋଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: The contrast invites a teasing question about standards that change with the situation.
entries.odia_summary: ଏକେ ଜିନିଷ ପାଇଁ ଦୁଇ ମାପକାଠି ରଖିବାକୁ ଖୋଚା ଦେଉଥିବା ଚିତ୍ର।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A friend happily eats a sticky sweet with their fingers, then protests loudly when a little syrup touches their shoe. Another friend quotes the saying with a smile while offering a cloth. This harmless transfer is editorial, not a documented historical use.
entries.cultural_context: No named caste, purity rule or bathing custom is inferred. The interpretation of inconsistent standards is editorial close reading; the source attests the words and literal verb.

entries.odia: ଯେ ତବତ ଖାଇଛି ସେ ପଖାଳ ଖାଉ, ଯେ କିଛି ନ ଖାଇଛି ସେ ଗାଧୋଇ ଯାଉ
entries.title: More for the fed, nothing for the hungry
entries.literal_meaning: Let the one who has eaten hot rice have pakhala; let the one who has eaten nothing go off to bathe.
entries.explanation: The people already fed receive another dish, while those who have had nothing are sent away. The dictionary’s figurative sense of going to bathe—being deprived of an enjoyment—makes the exclusion explicit. The pairing sounds almost like an orderly instruction, but the distribution it describes is upside down. It can give a speaker a pointed way to expose favouritism: those already served are served again, and unmet need is dismissed. This is an editorial reading of the contrast, not a rule about who deserves food.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯିଏ ଗରମ ଭାତ ଖାଇସାରିଛି, ତାକୁ ପୁଣି ପଖାଳ; ଯିଏ କିଛି ଖାଇନାହିଁ, ତାକୁ ଗାଧୋଇ ଯିବାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି। ଗାଧୋଇ ଯିବାର ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥ ଅଭିଧାନରେ କୌଣସି ଲାଭ ବା ଉପଭୋଗରୁ ବଞ୍ଚିତ ହେବା। ଶୁଣିବାକୁ ବଣ୍ଟନର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ଭଳି, ହେଲେ ଭାଗବଣ୍ଟାଟି ପୂରା ଓଲଟା। ଯାହାର ମିଳିସାରିଛି ତାକୁ ଆହୁରି ମିଳୁଛି, ଯାହାର କିଛି ନାହିଁ ତାକୁ ଦୂରେଇ ଦିଆଯାଉଛି—ଏହି ଅନ୍ୟାୟକୁ ଦେଖାଇବାରେ କଥାଟିର କଟାକ୍ଷ ଲାଗିପାରେ। ଏଠାରେ ଆମେ ସେହି ବୈଷମ୍ୟକୁ ଚିହ୍ନଟ କରି ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ, ତାକୁ ଠିକ୍ ବୋଲି କହୁନାହୁଁ।
entries.english_summary: A seemingly orderly instruction exposes an unfair distribution: more for those already served.
entries.odia_summary: ଯାହାର ମିଳିସାରିଛି ତାକୁ ଆହୁରି, ବାକି ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ କିଛି ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଓଲଟା ବଣ୍ଟନର କଟାକ୍ଷ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A workshop gives extra notebooks to participants who already received supplies, while late arrivals are told there are none for them. One participant quotes the saying to question the arrangement and asks for the remaining notebooks to be shared fairly.
entries.cultural_context: The hot-rice sense of ତବତ is independently checked in a second entry of the same dictionary lineage (revision221175), not an independent witness to the saying. Pakhala is retained as the food name. Unlike existing166, this is about unequal allocation and exclusion, not deciding between dishes before asking.

entries.title: The king’s answer is a brinjal
entries.literal_meaning: Rana, forest and thatching grass—the king of Banki answers with “my dhudhua brinjal.”
entries.explanation: The opening piles up three resources with a quick rhyme; the reply sets one unassuming vegetable against them. The dictionary explains the joke through a comparison of revenues: it says Dampara’s river fish, forest products and thatching grass brought less than Banki’s tax on the silted land where these brinjals grew. That explanation gives the king’s answer its boastful force: what looks like a modest crop may be the more valuable resource. This is the dictionary’s account, not a revenue comparison independently established here. Its conversational appeal lies in the surprise of the small-looking answer to a grand list.
entries.meaning_odia: ରଣ, ବଣ, ଛଣ—ତିନୋଟି ସମ୍ପଦର ନାଁ ମିଳାଇ କହିବା ପରେ ଉତ୍ତରରେ ଆସୁଛି ମାତ୍ର ବାଇଗଣ। ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଅନୁସାରେ ଡାମ୍ପଡ଼ାର ନଦୀମାଛ, ଜଙ୍ଗଲଜାତ ଦ୍ରବ୍ୟ ଓ ଛଣର ଆୟଠାରୁ ବାଙ୍କିର ବାଇଗଣ ଫଳୁଥିବା ପଟୁଜମିର ଖଜଣା ଅଧିକ ଥିଲା। ଏହି ଉତ୍ସକଥା ଧରି ପଢ଼ିଲେ, ସାଧାରଣ ଦେଖାଯାଉଥିବା ଫସଲକୁ ନେଇ ଉତ୍ତରରେ ଗର୍ବ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ବଡ଼ ତାଲିକାକୁ ଛୋଟ ଦେଖାଯାଉଥିବା ଗୋଟିଏ ଜିନିଷ ଟପିଯିବାରେ କଥାଟିର ଚମକ। ସେହି ରାଜସ୍ୱ ତୁଳନାକୁ ଆମେ ଏଠାରେ ସ୍ୱତନ୍ତ୍ର ଐତିହାସିକ ତଥ୍ୟ ଭାବେ ଯାଞ୍ଚ କରିନାହୁଁ।
entries.english_summary: A modest-looking crop supplies the surprising answer to a grand list of resources.
entries.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ସମ୍ପଦତାଲିକାକୁ ସାଧାରଣ ବାଇଗଣର ଚମକପ୍ରଦ ଉତ୍ତର।

entries.odia: ବୁଢ଼ା ବଳଦକୁ ଜୂଆଁଣିଆ ଘାସ ଖାଉ କି ନ ଖାଉ ମେଲି ଦେଇ ଆସ
entries.title: Leaving care at the gate
entries.literal_meaning: Give the old bull coarse juannia grass; whether it eats or not, let it loose and come away.
entries.explanation: The food is offered, but whether the old animal can use it is treated as no concern of the giver. The dismissive ending is the revealing part: doing something that resembles care becomes an excuse to stop caring about the outcome. The source defines the grass as coarse and tough; it does not give a separate figurative gloss. Our reading hears a picture of perfunctory attention, especially when someone’s needs have changed. Quoting it critically can draw attention to neglect rather than recommend the conduct it describes.
entries.meaning_odia: ବୁଢ଼ା ବଳଦକୁ ମୋଟା କରଡ଼ା ଘାସ ଦେଇଦେଲେ, ହେଲେ ସେ ଖାଇପାରିଲା କି ନାହିଁ ସେଥିରେ ଆଉ ଧ୍ୟାନ ନାହିଁ। ମେଲି ଦେଇ ଚାଲିଆସିବାର ଶେଷକଥାରେ ଏହି ଅବହେଳା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ହୁଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଘାସକୁ ମୋଟା ଓ କରଡ଼ା ବୋଲି କହିଛି; ଅଲଗା ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥ ଦେଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଏହା କେବଳ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ସାରିଦେବା ଭଳି ଯତ୍ନର ଚିତ୍ର—ଯାହା ପାଇଁ ଦିଆଗଲା, ତାହାର କାମରେ ଲାଗିଲା କି ନାହିଁ ଦେଖାଗଲା ନାହିଁ। ଏହି ଅବହେଳାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରି କଥାଟି ବ୍ୟବହାର କରିହୁଏ, ତାହାର ଅନୁକରଣ କରିବା ପାଇଁ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: An offer of care means little when no one checks whether it meets the recipient’s needs.
entries.odia_summary: ଯତ୍ନ ନାଁରେ କିଛି ଦେଇଦେବା ଓ ତାହା କାମରେ ଲାଗୁଛି କି ନାହିଁ ଦେଖିବା ଏକ କଥା ନୁହେଁ।

entries.odia: କଣ୍ଟାଫିରିକି, ଏତେ ଗୁଣ ବୋଲି ଜାଣିଥିଲି କି ବେଳସୁଁ ନ କହିଲୁ ଫୁଲପରା କରି ଟେକି ଧରିଥିଲୁ କଚାଡ଼ି ପକେଇଲୁ
entries.title: Raised like a flower, then dropped
entries.literal_meaning: Thorny phiriki, did I know you had such qualities? Why did you not tell me in time? You held me up like a flower, then flung me down.
entries.explanation: The voice turns on someone who first treated the speaker tenderly and then hurtfully reversed that treatment. “Such qualities” can be heard as an ironic compliment: the ending reveals why the earlier admiration has soured. The linked dictionary entry identifies phiriki as a thorny plant; the flower and the thorn therefore offer a sharp contrast without requiring a story about a particular person. The main entry supplies the words but no separate account of their occasion. Our conversational reading is a reproach for praise or support followed by abrupt rejection, not proof of a named betrayal or romance.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆଗରୁ ଫୁଲ ପରି ଟେକି ଧରିଲ, ପରେ କଚାଡ଼ି ପକାଇଲ—ଏହି ଓଲଟା ଆଚରଣକୁ ଧରି ବକ୍ତା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରୁଛନ୍ତି। ଏତେ ଗୁଣ ଥିଲା ବୋଲି କହିବାଟି ଏଠାରେ ପ୍ରଶଂସାର ଓଲଟା ସ୍ୱରରେ ଶୁଣାଯାଇପାରେ। ଅଭିଧାନର ସଂଯୁକ୍ତ ପିରିକ ଶବ୍ଦରେ କଣ୍ଟାଯୁକ୍ତ ଗଛର କଥା ଅଛି; ଫୁଲ ପରି ଆଦର ଓ କଣ୍ଟାର ଖୋଚା ଏହି ପାଠରେ ପାଖାପାଖି ଆସେ। ପ୍ରଥମେ ଭରସା ବା ପ୍ରଶଂସା ଦେଇ ପରେ ହଠାତ୍ ଦୂରେଇଦେବାକୁ ଏହି କଥାରେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିହୁଏ। କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ପ୍ରେମକାହାଣୀ ବା ଘଟଣାକୁ ଏହାର ମୂଳ ବୋଲି ଉତ୍ସ କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A reproach turns earlier praise into irony when tender support ends in abrupt rejection.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଗରୁ ଆଦର କରି ପରେ ଦୂରେଇଦେଲେ ପ୍ରଶଂସାର ସ୍ୱର ଅଭିଯୋଗରେ ବଦଳିଯାଏ।

No species identification, medicinal property, actual physical assault or fixed romantic relationship is claimed. Flower/thorn contrast and the modern conversational application are editorial readings.

entries.odia: କାଣି କଉଡ଼ି ପିତା ତାଳ, ୟାକୁ ଦେଉଥିବ ରାତ୍ରିକାଳ
entries.title: Passing it on after dark
entries.literal_meaning: A worthless cowrie, a bitter palm fruit—give these at night.
entries.explanation: Two disappointing things are paired with a convenient hour for giving: darkness. The dictionary identifies the cowrie as tiny or broken and, in the latter sense, worthless shell money. The saying itself gives no explanatory story. One possible reading is a dry joke about passing on something poor when its defects may be harder to notice. The surface instruction need not become our advice: quoted critically, it can expose the attempt to make a bad offering pass for a good one. We do not infer who receives them, or a custom that required such giving.
entries.meaning_odia: କାଣି କଉଡ଼ି ଓ ପିତା ତାଳ—ଦୁଇଟି ଅପସନ୍ଦ ହେବା ଭଳି ଜିନିଷ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ଦେବାର ସମୟ ରଖାଯାଇଛି ରାତି। ଅଭିଧାନ କଉଡ଼ିଟିକୁ ଛୋଟ ବା ଭଙ୍ଗା, ଆଉ ଭଙ୍ଗା ଅର୍ଥରେ ମୂଲ୍ୟହୀନ ବୋଲି କହିଛି। ଅନ୍ଧାରରେ ଦୋଷ ଭଲକରି ଦେଖାନଯିବାର ସୁଯୋଗ ନେଇ ଖରାପ ଜିନିଷ ଚଳାଇଦେବାର ଶୁଖିଲା ଥଟ୍ଟା ଭାବେ ଏହାକୁ ପଢ଼ିହୁଏ। ଏହା ଆମର ପ୍ରୟୋଗମୂଳକ ପାଠ; ଉତ୍ସ ଅଲଗା ଘଟଣା ବା ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଦେଇନାହିଁ। କାହାର ଏମିତି ଚାଲାକିକୁ ଧରି କଥାଟି କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ, ସେହି ଚାଲାକି କରିବାକୁ ପରାମର୍ଶ ଦେବା ପାଇଁ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: One possible reading is a dry joke about passing on something poor under cover of darkness.
entries.odia_summary: ଖରାପ ଜିନିଷକୁ ଅନ୍ଧାରରେ ଚଳାଇଦେବାର ଚାଲାକି ଉପରେ ଏକ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A friend notices that a damaged second-hand lamp is being shown to a buyer only in a dim corner. They quote the saying and ask that the lamp be brought into the light before anyone decides. This modern scene is an editorial use, not a documented trading custom.
entries.cultural_context: The cowrie is a historical money image in the source gloss. The darkness/deception interpretation is not separately defined there and remains an editorial reading. No specific recipient, ritual, trade practice or origin is supplied. The fruit wording is retained without a botanical or dietary claim.

entries.odia: ଅଳଙ୍କାର ମଇଧେ ନିମକାଠି ଥାନେ
entries.title: A twig among ornaments
entries.literal_meaning: Among the ornaments, a neem twig has a place.
entries.explanation: The line puts a small ordinary twig among things normally valued for adornment. A separate dictionary entry explains that a piece of neem twig could occupy an ear or nose piercing when an ornament was absent. That historical description makes the juxtaposition less random: the twig stands in the place an ornament would otherwise occupy. It does not, by itself, settle whether every speaker intends affection, modest pride or a dismissive comparison. One editorial application is to notice an unassuming substitute that serves a purpose among more impressive things. The source’s old bodily practice is context, not a recommendation to reproduce it.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଳଙ୍କାରମାନଙ୍କ ଭିତରେ ସାଧାରଣ ନିମକାଠିର ମଧ୍ୟ ସ୍ଥାନ ଅଛି—ଏହି ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖିବାଟି କଥାର ଚମକ। ଅନ୍ୟ ଏକ ଅଭିଧାନ ଶବ୍ଦରେ ଅଳଙ୍କାର ନଥିଲେ କାନ ବା ନାକର ଫୋଡ଼ରେ ଛୋଟ ନିମକାଠି ରଖାଯିବାର ପୁରୁଣା ବ୍ୟବହାର ବର୍ଣ୍ଣିତ ଅଛି। ସେହି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ଧରିଲେ କାଠିଟି କାହିଁକି ଅଳଙ୍କାର ପାଖରେ ଆସିଲା, ବୁଝିହୁଏ। ତେବେ କଥାଟିରେ ଆଦର, ନିଜ ସାଧାରଣତାକୁ ନେଇ ହସ, ନା ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟ—ସବୁ ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ପାଇଁ ଏକ ସ୍ୱର ଉତ୍ସ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ କରେନାହିଁ। ଆଡ଼ମ୍ବର ଭିତରେ କାମରେ ଲାଗୁଥିବା ସାଧାରଣ ବଦଳି ଜିନିଷକୁ ଚିହ୍ନିବା ଏହାର ଗୋଟିଏ ପ୍ରୟୋଗମୂଳକ ପାଠ।
entries.english_summary: An ordinary twig beside ornaments suggests a place for an unassuming substitute, though tone depends on use.
entries.odia_summary: ଅଳଙ୍କାର ପାଖରେ ନିମକାଠି—ସାଧାରଣ ବଦଳି ଜିନିଷର ସ୍ଥାନ ଦେଖାଇବାର ଗୋଟିଏ ଚିତ୍ର।

This is an editorial application, not a sourced musical tradition.

entries.odia: କଅଁଳକହୀ ରାଧା, ଘରକୁ ଗଲେ କଥା ନ କହନ୍ତି ବାଟରେ ବଡ଼ ଶରଧା
entries.title: Warm words on the road
entries.literal_meaning: Sweet-speaking Radha: when one goes to the house, she does not speak; on the road, such affection.
entries.explanation: The praise in “sweet-speaking” is undercut by the change of setting. On the road there is a warm reception; at the house there is not even conversation. The linked dictionary definition includes flattering words that conceal a different intention, so the contrast is sharper than a simple difference between a busy and a free moment. The line can tease or reproach warmth that seems to depend on where it is displayed. It does not tell us who visits the house or what relationship the visitor has to Radha. Our present-day application concerns inconsistent welcome, not a rule about women or a story about a deity.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାଟରେ ଦେଖାହେଲେ ଏତେ ଶରଧା, ଘରକୁ ଗଲେ ପଦେ କଥା ନାହିଁ—ସ୍ଥାନ ବଦଳିବା ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ଆଚରଣ ବଦଳିଯାଉଛି। ଏହି ଓଲଟା ଦେଖାଇ “କଅଁଳକହୀ” ପ୍ରଶଂସାଟି କଟାକ୍ଷ ହୋଇଯାଏ। ସଂଯୁକ୍ତ ଅଭିଧାନ ଶବ୍ଦରେ ମନରେ କପଟ ରଖି ମିଠା କଥା କହିବାର ଅର୍ଥ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅଛି। ଦେଖାସାକ୍ଷାତରେ ଆଦର ଦେଖାଇ ପାଖକୁ ଆସିଲେ ମୁହଁ ଫେରାଇବାକୁ ଏହି କଥାରେ ଧରିହୁଏ। କିଏ ଘରକୁ ଗଲେ ବା ରାଧାଙ୍କ ସହ ତାଙ୍କର କି ସମ୍ପର୍କ, ପଦଟି ସେ କଥା କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A warm greeting in one setting rings hollow when it turns into silence in another.
entries.odia_summary: ବାଟର ଆଦର ଘରେ ନିରବତା ହେଲେ ମିଠା କଥାର ଅସଙ୍ଗତି ଧରାପଡ଼େ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A neighbour repeatedly welcomes someone warmly at the market and invites them to drop by. When the visitor arrives at the agreed time, the neighbour will not acknowledge them. Later, the visitor quotes the saying to a friend with a rueful laugh. This invented scene illustrates the contrast; it is not the source’s occasion.
entries.cultural_context: Radha is the name in the wording; no mythological identity, romance or biography is established. 8859 is lexical context only, not another full-saying witness. The visitor and relationship remain unspecified. Teasing force follows the source contrast and linked flattering-speech definition; contemporary situation is editorial.

entries.odia: ଦେଉଳ ତୋଳେଇଲେ ନାଁ ପଡ଼େ, ବାଟରେ ହଗିଲେ ନାଁ ପଡ଼େ
entries.title: A name for what?
entries.literal_meaning: Have a temple built and your name spreads; defecate on the road and your name spreads.
entries.explanation: The same phrase, “your name spreads”, carries two very different kinds of attention. Building a temple supplies the respectable image; fouling the road abruptly drags it down into coarse comedy. The dictionary places the saying under notoriety, after a separate sense for good reputation. Being talked about is therefore not enough to tell whether someone is admired or condemned. In an editorial everyday use, the line can puncture a boast about publicity by asking what earned it. Its shock is part of the contrast, not an instruction to humiliate a person or a claim about a particular temple builder.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦେଉଳ ତୋଳାଇଲେ ଲୋକେ ନାଁ କହନ୍ତି, ବାଟ ଅପରିଷ୍କାର କଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ନାଁ କହନ୍ତି—କିନ୍ତୁ ଦୁଇଥର କହିବାର ଅର୍ଥ ଏକ ନୁହେଁ। ସମ୍ମାନର ଚିତ୍ର ପଛକୁ ହଠାତ୍ ଏମିତି ଅଶୋଭନ କାମ ଆଣିବାରେ ଥଟ୍ଟାର ଝଟକା ଅଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ମଧ୍ୟ ସୁଖ୍ୟାତି ଓ ଅପଯଶକୁ ଅଲଗା ଅର୍ଥରେ ରଖିଛି। ତେଣୁ କେତେ ଲୋକ ମୋ କଥା କହୁଛନ୍ତି ବୋଲି ଗର୍ବ କରିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ କାହିଁକି କହୁଛନ୍ତି, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠେ। ନାଁ ହେବା ଓ ଭଲ ନାଁ ହେବାର ତଫାତକୁ ଏହି କଟାକ୍ଷ ମନେ ପକାଏ।
entries.english_summary: Attention alone cannot distinguish an admired reputation from notoriety.
entries.odia_summary: ନାଁ ହେବା ମାତ୍ରେ ସୁନାମ ହୁଏନାହିଁ; କେଉଁ କାମ ପାଇଁ ହେଲା, ସେଇଟି ଅସଲ କଥା।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After a noisy argument at a neighbourhood meeting, a participant boasts that everyone is talking about him. A friend quotes the saying and asks whether he wanted to be remembered for the quarrel or for helping solve the problem. No actual meeting or person is being described.
entries.cultural_context: The coarse bodily verb is retained in the exact quotation and literal translation. The example uses a non-bodily modern situation. The Radhanath quotation in the preceding dictionary sense is a separate named literary example and is not presented as the author of this saying.

entries.odia: ଖଣ୍ଡ଼ିଗଣିଆଁର ଦିଗୁଣ ସରେ
entries.title: Counting every piece, spending twice
entries.literal_meaning: The piece-counter uses up twice as much.
entries.explanation: The dictionary’s piece-counter is someone so miserly with food that each cut piece is counted before it is handed to the cook. The saying answers that anxious control with a reversal: the supposed saver ends up using twice as much. “Twice” gives the rebuke its bite; the source supplies no measured account or explanation of how the loss occurs. One editorial application is to a petty economy whose inconvenience creates more expense. The target is grasping control, not careful budgeting when resources are genuinely limited.
entries.meaning_odia: ରାନ୍ଧୁଣିଙ୍କୁ ଦେବା ଆଗରୁ ଖାଦ୍ୟର ପ୍ରତି ଖଣ୍ଡ ଗଣୁଥିବା କୃପଣଙ୍କୁ ଅଭିଧାନ “ଖଣ୍ଡ଼ିଗଣିଆଁ” କହିଛି। ଏତେ ହିସାବ ରଖି ମଧ୍ୟ ତାଙ୍କର ଦୁଇଗୁଣ ସରେ—ଏହି ଓଲଟା ଫଳରେ କଥାର ମଜା। କେମିତି ଦୁଇଗୁଣ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ହେଲା, ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ଘଟଣା ଦେଇନାହିଁ; ସଂଖ୍ୟାଟି କଟାକ୍ଷକୁ ଜୋର ଦିଏ। ଅଳ୍ପ ବଞ୍ଚାଇବାର ଜିଦ୍‌ରେ ଏମିତି ଅସୁବିଧା ତିଆରି ହୋଇପାରେ, ଯାହା ପାଇଁ ପରେ ଅଧିକ ଦେବାକୁ ପଡ଼େ। ଅଭାବରେ ସାବଧାନ ହୋଇ ଚଳିବାକୁ ନୁହେଁ, ଏଠାରେ ଅତି କୃପଣ ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରଣକୁ ହସରେ ଧରାଯାଇଛି।
entries.english_summary: A miser’s minute control is mocked as an economy that can cost more.
entries.odia_summary: ପ୍ରତି ଖଣ୍ଡ ବଞ୍ଚାଇବାର କୃପଣତା ଶେଷରେ ଅଧିକ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚର କାରଣ ହେବା ଉପରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: For a shared event, an organiser insists on buying too few paper cups to save a little. When they run out, a volunteer makes a second trip and pays more for a small packet. Someone quotes the saying about the piece-counter. The cups and extra trip are an invented illustration, not the dictionary’s story.
entries.cultural_context: The source explicitly defines food-related miserliness. The broader petty-economy application is editorial. No quantitative spending law, nutritional instruction or judgement of people living in poverty is implied.

entries.odia: କୋହଳ ପାଇଲେ ଦୋହଡ଼ ଚଷନ୍ତି
entries.title: Soft ground invites another pass
entries.literal_meaning: When they find it soft, they plough it a second time.
entries.explanation: The source places this line under “soft”, while the linked word dohada means a second tilling. That gives the saying a concrete repeated action: easy ground invites another pass of the plough. An editorial social reading hears a warning about someone taking further advantage when another person yields. It is a possible application of the image, not a separate traditional-use gloss supplied by this entry. The line need not make kindness a fault; the question is whether a concession is being treated as permission to keep pressing.
entries.meaning_odia: ନରମ ମିଳିଲେ ଆଉ ଥରେ ଚଷନ୍ତି—ଏଠାରେ ଏକ କାମ ସହଜ ହେବାରୁ ତାକୁ ପୁଣି କରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଅଛି। “ଦୋହଡ଼” ଅର୍ଥ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଥର ହଳ କରିବା ବୋଲି ସଂଯୁକ୍ତ ଅଭିଧାନ ଶବ୍ଦ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରେ। ଲୋକସମ୍ପର୍କରେ ଏହାକୁ ପଢ଼ିଲେ, ଜଣେ ଥରେ ଛାଡ଼ ଦେଲେ ଆଉ ଅଧିକ ଚାପ ଦେବାର କଥା ମନକୁ ଆସେ। ଏହା ଚିତ୍ରକୁ ଧରି ଆମର ପ୍ରୟୋଗମୂଳକ ପାଠ; ଉତ୍ସ ଅଲଗା ସାମାଜିକ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଦେଇନାହିଁ। ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରିବା ଭୁଲ ନୁହେଁ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଗୋଟିଏ ଛାଡ଼କୁ ସବୁବେଳର ଅଧିକାର କରିନେଲେ ସୀମା କେଉଁଠି ରହିବ?
entries.english_summary: In one social reading, an initial concession encourages someone to press for more.
entries.odia_summary: ଥରେ ଛାଡ଼ ପାଇ ଆଉ ଅଧିକ ଚାପ ଦେବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ପଢ଼ିହୁଏ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A colleague agrees to cover one shift. The same coworker then assumes they will cover the following weekend too, without asking. A friend quotes the saying, and the colleague clarifies that the first favour was for one day. This workplace use is editorial, not an attested origin.
entries.cultural_context: 199397 establishes second tilling only and is a context-only citation. The social application is explicitly editorial; no agricultural advice, rule about all generous people or documented origin is asserted.

entries.odia: କାକର ଧରି କି ଘଡ଼ା ଭର୍ତ୍ତି ହୁଏ
entries.title: Can dew fill the pot?
entries.literal_meaning: Can a pot be filled by collecting dew?
entries.explanation: The question sets tiny drops against a vessel that needs filling. The dictionary describes collecting dew and compares a Hindi proverb about licking dew not satisfying thirst. The force is a challenge to adequacy: is what is being gathered enough for the need at hand? In an editorial everyday use, it can question token help offered in place of a sufficient response. That does not make every small contribution useless; the mismatch between the amount and the particular need is what gives the question its point.
entries.meaning_odia: କାକରର ଛୋଟ ଛୋଟ ବିନ୍ଦୁ ଓ ଭରିବାକୁ ଥିବା ଘଡ଼ା—ଏହି ଦୁଇ ମାପକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରାଯାଇଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ କାକର ସଂଗ୍ରହର ଅର୍ଥ ଦେବା ସହ କାକର ଚାଟିଲେ ଶୋଷ ନମେଣ୍ଟିବା ବିଷୟରେ ହିନ୍ଦୀ ପ୍ରବଚନକୁ ତୁଳନା କରିଛି। ଯେତିକି ଦରକାର, ସେଥିପାଇଁ ମିଳୁଥିବା ଅଳ୍ପଟି ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ କି ନୁହେଁ—କଥାଟି ସେଇ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠାଏ। ବଡ଼ ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ଆଗରେ କେବଳ ନାମକୁ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଦେଲେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଛୋଟ ଅବଦାନକୁ ତୁଚ୍ଛ କରିବା ନୁହେଁ, ଆବଶ୍ୟକତାର ମାପ ସହ ତାହାକୁ ମିଳାଇ ଦେଖିବା ଏହି ପାଠର କଥା।
entries.english_summary: The question challenges a response too small for the need it is meant to meet.
entries.odia_summary: ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ତୁଳନାରେ ଉପାୟଟି ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ କି ନୁହେଁ, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A reading group needs enough notebooks for twenty children, but someone proposes bringing only two and calling the task finished. A volunteer quotes the dew-and-pot question, thanks them for the start, and asks how the remaining notebooks will be found. This is an invented use, not a source incident.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary itself offers a Hindi comparison; this is not evidence of borrowing direction or a shared origin. The image is not a technical claim that dew can never be harvested. The adequacy and token-help applications are editorial readings supported by the question and comparison.

entries.odia: ଥିଲାବେଳେ ଚିରାକନା ହଜିଗଲେ ମାଠ
entries.title: Fine cloth, once it is lost
entries.literal_meaning: While it was there, a rag; once lost, a fine cloth.
entries.explanation: The object changes in the speaker’s estimation after it disappears. What was dismissed as a torn rag suddenly becomes fine cloth worth lamenting. The joke catches the difference between the care something received and the value claimed for it afterwards. In an everyday application, it can tease exaggerated regret over an object or opportunity that was taken for granted. That application is our close reading of the contrast; the dictionary supplies the saying and the cloth vocabulary, not an account of its first use.
entries.meaning_odia: ପାଖରେ ଥିବାବେଳେ ଯାହାକୁ ଚିରାକନା କହି ତୁଚ୍ଛ କରାଯାଉଥିଲା, ହଜିଗଲା ପରେ ସେଇଟି ମାଠ ହୋଇଯାଉଛି। ବଦଳିଛି ଜିନିଷଟି ନୁହେଁ, ତାହାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ବିଷୟରେ କହୁଥିବା ମଣିଷର କଥା। ଥିବାବେଳେ ଆଦର ନ କରି ହରାଇବା ପରେ ବହୁତ ଆଦର ଦେଖାଇବାକୁ ଏହି ଓଲଟା ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଧରିହୁଏ। ଏଠାରେ ସେହି ହାଲୁକା କଟାକ୍ଷକୁ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ଅବହେଳା ଓ ଅନୁତାପର ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗରେ ପଢ଼ାଯାଇଛି।
entries.english_summary: Something dismissed while available becomes precious once it is lost.
entries.odia_summary: ପାଖରେ ଥିବାବେଳେ ଅବହେଳିତ ଜିନିଷ ହଜିଗଲେ ହଠାତ୍ ମୂଲ୍ୟବାନ ଲାଗେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A brother has called an old scarf useless for months. When he misplaces it, he calls it his finest scarf. His sister laughs and quotes the saying, reminding him how he spoke about it yesterday.

Retrospective valuation is editorial close reading. No origin or general rule about grief is claimed.

entries.odia: ମାଗଣୁ ମହର୍ଗ
entries.title: Calling a free thing costly
entries.literal_meaning: Free, yet costly.
entries.explanation: The dictionary gives a specific occasion for this short taunt: someone receives something without paying and still calls it expensive. The absurd price complaint does the work. A speaker can use it to prick dissatisfaction that forgets what was actually paid. It is not the different saying that a free offer always carries a hidden cost; neither does it settle whether the thing is useful or whether the recipient may refuse it. Its bite lies in this particular mismatch between receiving gratis and complaining about the price.
entries.meaning_odia: କିଛି ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନ ଦେଇ ଜିନିଷଟି ମିଳିଛି, ତଥାପି ତାହା ମହର୍ଗ ବୋଲି ଅଭିଯୋଗ ହେଉଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଅସଙ୍ଗତି ପାଇଁ କଥାଟି କୁହାଯାଏ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଇଛି। ଦୁଇ ପଦରେ ମିଳିଥିବା ସୁବିଧା ଓ ଅଭିଯୋଗର ହିସାବକୁ ସାମ୍ନାସାମ୍ନି ରଖିଦିଏ। ଜିନିଷଟି ଭଲ କି ଖରାପ, ସେ ବିଚାର ଅଲଗା; ଏଠାରେ କଟାକ୍ଷଟି ହେଉଛି ଟଙ୍କା ନ ଦେଇ ଦାମ ବିଷୟରେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିବା ଉପରେ।
entries.english_summary: The taunt targets someone who pays nothing but complains that the price is high.
entries.odia_summary: ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନ ଦେଇ ପାଇଥିବା ଜିନିଷର ଦାମକୁ ନେଇ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରିବାରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A club gives away its spare notebooks. Someone accepts one, then jokingly complains that it was too expensive. The organiser replies, “ମାଗଣୁ ମହର୍ଗ,” and both laugh at the impossible bill.
entries.cultural_context: The supplied gloss explicitly identifies the target. Do not recast it as a hidden-cost maxim or an instruction that recipients must be grateful for anything. Meaning is adapted from the dictionary gloss; example is original.

entries.odia: ରୋହଦ୍ର ଖରାରେ ଯେ ବସଇ ମୁହିଁ, ଆ ଛାଇକି ବୋଲି ବୋଲନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ
entries.title: No one calls me into the shade
entries.literal_meaning: I sit in the fierce sun; they do not say, “Come into the shade.”
entries.explanation: This voice complains of a small kindness withheld. The speaker is exposed to fierce heat, while the wished-for response is only an invitation into shade. The line makes neglect tangible without telling us who the others are or why they remain silent. Read conversationally, it can express the hurt of being overlooked when someone could easily acknowledge a difficulty. That broader use follows the image; it is not a documented original occasion or a claim that every unspoken offer is deliberate cruelty.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଚଣ୍ଡ ଖରାରେ ବସିଥିବା ମଣିଷଟି ଅନେକ କିଛି ମାଗୁନାହିଁ; ଛାଇକୁ ଆସ ବୋଲି ପଦେ ଡାକକୁ ଅପେକ୍ଷା କରୁଛି। ସେ ଡାକ ନ ମିଳିବାରେ ଅଭିମାନ ରହିଛି। ଦେଖିପାରୁଥିବା କଷ୍ଟ ପ୍ରତି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଧ୍ୟାନ ନ ଦେବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରେ। କିଏ ଡାକିଲେ ନାହିଁ ବା ସେମାନଙ୍କ ସହ କି ସମ୍ପର୍କ, ପଦଟି ନିଜେ ତାହା କହେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: The speaker feels overlooked when even a simple invitation to shelter is missing.
entries.odia_summary: କଷ୍ଟ ଦେଖି ମଧ୍ୟ ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଆଶ୍ରୟକୁ ଡାକ ନ ମିଳିବାର ଅଭିମାନ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After helping arrange an outdoor meeting, a volunteer remains in the sun while the others sit under the canopy. Later the volunteer quotes the line to a friend, describing the hurt of not being invited to join them.
entries.cultural_context: ରୋହଦ୍ର is explicitly glossed unbearably hot. Speaker, place and relationship are unnamed. Neglect is a reading of the direct complaint; no heat-safety instruction, biography or historical scene is inferred.

entries.odia: ଯଚ୍ନିୟା ମାଲର ରଙ୍ଗ ନାହିଁ
entries.title: When an unasked-for gift loses value
entries.literal_meaning: Unasked-for goods have no colour.
entries.explanation: The dictionary explains “no colour” here as a lack of value: an unsolicited thing is not valued. The line points to reception rather than a defect in the object. Something offered without being requested may be overlooked precisely because no effort was made to seek it. Our reading treats that as an observation about undervaluing what arrives easily, not proof that unsolicited help or gifts are worthless. It can sound rueful from the giver or self-mocking from someone who recognises their own neglect.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯାଚିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ମିଳିଥିବା ଜିନିଷର “ରଙ୍ଗ ନାହିଁ”—ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟାରେ ଏହାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ନ ହେବାର କଥା ଅଛି। ଜିନିଷଟିର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଗୁଣ ଠାରୁ ଏଠାରେ ତାହାକୁ କେମିତି ଗ୍ରହଣ କରାଯାଉଛି, ସେଇଟି ଆଗକୁ ଆସେ। ଖୋଜିବାକୁ ବା ମାଗିବାକୁ ନ ପଡ଼ିଲେ ମିଳିଥିବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟକୁ ହାଲୁକା ଭାବେ ନେବାରେ ଏହି କଥା ଲାଗିପାରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହା ସେହି ଅବହେଳାକୁ ଧରେ, ନ ମାଗି ମିଳିଥିବା ସବୁ ଜିନିଷ ମୂଲ୍ୟହୀନ ବୋଲି ରାୟ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: An unsolicited offering may receive less regard than something actively sought.
entries.odia_summary: ନ ମାଗି ମିଳିଥିବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ବା ଜିନିଷର ଆଦର କମିଯାଇପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A colleague sends useful notes before anyone asks. They remain unread until the team pays for similar guidance elsewhere. The colleague quotes the saying with a rueful smile about the notes that arrived too easily.

entries.odia: ଗାଡ଼ିଆରେ ହଜାଇ ପୋଖରୀରେ ଖୋଜିବା ନ୍ୟାୟ
entries.title: Searching the wrong pond
entries.literal_meaning: Like losing something in a small tank and searching for it in a pond.
entries.explanation: The search has moved away from the place of the loss. A larger or more noticeable place will not become the right one simply because it attracts attention. As an analogy, the image can question effort directed at the wrong location or cause. It asks the listener to connect the search with what actually happened before continuing. The source defines the small tank and labels the comparison; this explanation extends the spatial mismatch into an everyday use, without claiming a particular lost object or origin story.
entries.meaning_odia: ଜିନିଷଟି ହଜିଛି ଗାଡ଼ିଆରେ, ଖୋଜା ଚାଲିଛି ପୋଖରୀରେ। ଖୋଜିବାର ପରିଶ୍ରମ ଥିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ସ୍ଥାନର ମେଳ ନାହିଁ। କେଉଁଠି ଭୁଲ ହେଲା ନ ଦେଖି ଅନ୍ୟଠାରେ ଉତ୍ତର ଖୋଜିବାକୁ ଆମେ ଏହି ତୁଳନାରେ ବୁଝିପାରୁ। ଆଉ ଅଧିକ ଖୋଜିବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଖୋଜାର ଦିଗଟି ଠିକ୍ କି ନାହିଁ, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠେ।
entries.english_summary: Effort misses its mark when the search is detached from where the loss occurred.
entries.odia_summary: ଯେଉଁଠି ହଜିଛି ତାହା ଛାଡ଼ି ଅନ୍ୟଠାରେ ଖୋଜିଲେ ପରିଶ୍ରମ ଠିକ୍ ଦିଗରେ ଯାଏନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A team keeps checking the delivery van for a missing parcel, although its own register says the parcel never left the store. One member quotes the analogy and asks them to begin with the store records.
entries.cultural_context: The historical headword includes caste-ranked speech labels. Those labels are not adopted as facts about present communities. No animal, waterbody practice or actual loss event is reconstructed.

entries.odia: ଦିଆକୁ ଦିଆ, ଅଦିଆକୁ ଦୁଆର ଦିଆ
entries.title: Giving, and closing the door
entries.literal_meaning: Give to the giver; close the door to the non-giver.
entries.explanation: The repeated sound of “ଦିଆ” changes its force at the door: giving becomes shutting someone out. Read as a compact rule of reciprocity, the line divides people according to whether they give. It can expose the calculating side of an exchange in which welcome depends on a return. Our reading leaves room for a speaker to endorse that bargain or mock it; the short dictionary quotation supplies no performance setting. It should not be turned into a rule that someone unable to contribute deserves exclusion.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଥମେ “ଦିଆ”ରେ ଦେବାର କଥା, ଶେଷରେ “ଦୁଆର ଦିଆ”ରେ ବାଟ ବନ୍ଦ କରିବାର କଥା ଆସୁଛି। ଯିଏ ଦିଏ ତାକୁ ଦିଅ, ଯିଏ ଦିଏନାହିଁ ତାହା ପାଇଁ ଦୁଆର ବନ୍ଦ—ଏହି ହିସାବଟି କଥାରେ ଧରାପଡ଼େ। ଆଦର ଓ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ଯେତେବେଳେ କେବଳ ପ୍ରତିଦାନ ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କରେ, ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ତାହାର ସଂକୀର୍ଣ୍ଣତା ମଧ୍ୟ ଦିଶେ। ଏହାକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ କରି କୁହାଗଲା କି କଟାକ୍ଷରେ, ଅଭିଧାନର ଛୋଟ ଉଦାହରଣ ସେ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: The sound-play turns reciprocity into a door that opens or closes according to what someone gives.
entries.odia_summary: ଦେବାର ହିସାବରେ ଦୁଆର ଖୋଲିବା ବା ବନ୍ଦ ହେବାର ଶବ୍ଦଖେଳ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A committee suggests helping only members who donated last year. Another member quotes the saying critically, then asks what happens to neighbours who had nothing to give.
entries.cultural_context: ଦୁଆର ଦିଆ is explicitly glossed shutting the door against a person. Reciprocity and the critical example are editorial close reading, not a supplied moral gloss or universal custom.

entries.odia: ନାନା ମୁନିଙ୍କର ନାନା ମତ
entries.title: Even the wise differ
entries.literal_meaning: Different sages have different opinions.
entries.explanation: The repetition makes disagreement unsurprising: several thinkers need not arrive at one view. The line can loosen a conversation that has stalled because each side expects complete agreement. It does not tell us that all opinions are equally well supported, or that a decision can be avoided forever. Rather, in our reading, it creates a little room to hear why people differ before choosing what to do. The dictionary supplies “different opinions” and this example; it identifies no particular sages or dispute.
entries.meaning_odia: ମୁନି ଅନେକ ହେଲେ ମତ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅନେକ ହୋଇପାରେ। “ନାନା”ର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତିରେ ମତଭେଦକୁ ଆଶ୍ଚର୍ଯ୍ୟର କଥା ନ କରି ସହଜ ଭାବେ କୁହାଯାଏ। ସମସ୍ତେ ଏକ କଥା କହିବା ଦରକାର ବୋଲି ଜିଦ୍ ଧରିଥିବା ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ଏହା ଟିକିଏ ଅବକାଶ ଆଣିପାରେ। ତଥାପି କେଉଁ ମତ ପଛରେ କି ଯୁକ୍ତି ଅଛି, ସେହି ବିଚାର କରିବାର କାମ ରହିଯାଏ।
entries.english_summary: Disagreement can remain even among thoughtful people.
entries.odia_summary: ବିଚାରଶୀଳ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ମଧ୍ୟ ମତଭେଦ ରହିପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Three experienced readers propose different endings for a play. The director smiles, quotes the saying, and asks each to explain what their ending would achieve before the group chooses.
entries.cultural_context: No named sages, scriptural derivation or origin established. Acceptance of disagreement is an editorial application, not a claim that all claims are equally true.

entries.odia: ଢିଙ୍କି ପଡ଼େ ଧମଧମ, ସାହାବ ଚାକିରି ଭାରି କଠିଣ; ଝାଳ ବୁହେ ଗମଗମ
entries.title: The sound and sweat of work
entries.literal_meaning: The dheṅki falls thump-thump; service to the sahib is very hard; sweat streams.
entries.explanation: The heavy beat of the pounding implement is answered by the sound of streaming sweat. Between them comes the complaint that service to the sahib is hard. Sound makes the labour felt before any abstract judgment is offered. The line can be read as a rhythmic complaint about demanding work, but the quotation does not identify an employer, worker or event. A present-day speaker may borrow its exaggerated beat to describe a tiring task; that is a new use, not evidence of a particular historical labour arrangement.
entries.meaning_odia: ଢିଙ୍କିର “ଧମଧମ” ଶବ୍ଦ ପରେ ଝାଳର “ଗମଗମ” ଆସୁଛି। ମଝିରେ ସାହାବଙ୍କ ଚାକିରି କେତେ କଠିନ, ସେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ ରହିଛି। ଶବ୍ଦର ତାଳରେ କାମର ଭାର ଓ ଶରୀରର କ୍ଳାନ୍ତି ଏକାଠି ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଆଜି କେହି ନିଜର କଠିନ କାମକୁ ନେଇ ଏହା କହିଲେ ପୁରୁଣା ଚିତ୍ରଟି ନୂଆ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗକୁ ଆସେ; କିନ୍ତୁ ମୂଳ ପଦର କର୍ମୀ ବା ସାହାବଙ୍କ ପରିଚୟ ଆମ ପାଖରେ ନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Thumping sound and streaming sweat turn a complaint about hard service into a rhythmic line.
entries.odia_summary: ଢିଙ୍କିର ଶବ୍ଦ ଓ ଝାଳର ଚିତ୍ରରେ କଠିନ ଚାକିରିର ଅଭିଯୋଗ ତାଳ ପାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After repeatedly moving heavy boxes for a demanding organiser, a volunteer recites the line to a friend, tapping out “ଧମଧମ.” The friend hears both the joke and the complaint about the workload.
entries.cultural_context: Source label is Dhaga under an onomatopoeic word. The term sahib is retained as an unspecified form of address/status in the quotation; no colonial employer, date, caste or documented work scene is inferred. Not identical to048 compulsory work wherever one goes.

entries.odia: ଗଛରେ ଚଢ଼ିଛି ମରିବା ପାଇଁ ଜାମିନ ହୋଇଛି ଦେବା ପାଇଁ
entries.title: What a guarantee can ask of you
entries.literal_meaning: One has climbed the tree to die; one has stood surety to pay.
entries.explanation: The line states possible consequences with deliberately bleak certainty. Climbing brings the danger of a fall; standing surety can leave the guarantor having to pay. The dictionary defines the latter as undertaking responsibility for another person’s action. Our reading hears a warning against treating such an undertaking as empty words. It does not say that every climb is fatal or establish the legal effect of any present-day guarantee. The two compressed clauses make responsibility difficult to wave away.
entries.meaning_odia: ଗଛରେ ଚଢ଼ିବା ସହ ମୃତ୍ୟୁ, ଜାମିନ ହେବା ସହ ଟଙ୍କା ଦେବାକୁ ପଦଟି ସିଧା ଯୋଡ଼ିଦିଏ। ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପରିଣାମକୁ ଏତେ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ଭାବେ କହିବାରେ ସତର୍କ କରିବାର ଜୋର ଅଛି। ଅନ୍ୟର କାମର ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନେଲେ ସେ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନିଜ ପାଖକୁ ଫେରିଆସିପାରେ—ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହାହିଁ ମୁଖ୍ୟ କଥା। କେବଳ ପଦେ ହଁ କହିଦେବା ଓ ତାହାର ଭାର ବୋହିବା ଏକ କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A promise to answer for another person can bring a real burden back to the guarantor.
entries.odia_summary: ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନେବାର କଥା ନିଜ ଉପରେ ପ୍ରକୃତ ଭାର ଆଣିପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A friend agrees to cover a group’s equipment bill if the others cannot pay, calling it a mere formality. Another quotes the saying and asks whether the friend has considered actually meeting that bill.
entries.cultural_context: The stark death clause is rhetorical, not a prediction or safety instruction. Surety definition is historical lexical evidence; application is not current legal or financial advice. No actual contract is assessed.

entries.odia: ପେଟ ପୋଷ ନାହିଁ ଦୋଷ
entries.title: There is no shame in earning a living
entries.literal_meaning: Feed yourself; there is no fault.
entries.explanation: The rhyme answers an accusation before it grows: maintaining oneself is not in itself a fault. The dictionary explains “feeding the belly” as supporting one’s life. In an ordinary conversation, the line can defend necessary work against snobbery about its status. That reading concerns the dignity of earning a living, not permission to harm others for gain. The short source supplies no trade, worker or occasion, so a particular occupation belongs to an illustrative example rather than to the saying’s documented history.
entries.meaning_odia: ପେଟ ପୋଷିବାର ଅର୍ଥ ଅଭିଧାନରେ ନିଜର ଜୀବିକା ଚଳାଇବା। “ପୋଷ” ଓ “ଦୋଷ”ର ମେଳରେ ଜୀବିକାର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ପାଇଁ ଛୋଟ ଏକ ସମର୍ଥନ ମିଳେ। କାମଟିକୁ ହୀନ ଭାବି କେହି ହସିଲେ, ନିଜ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ନିଜେ ଚଳାଇବାରେ ଲାଜ କାହିଁକି ବୋଲି ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଆମର ଏହି ପଢ଼ା ଜୀବିକାର ସମ୍ମାନକୁ ନେଇ; ଲାଭ ପାଇଁ ଅନ୍ୟର କ୍ଷତି କରିବାକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Earning one’s living is not itself something to be ashamed of.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଜ ଜୀବିକା ଚଳାଇବାରେ ଲଜ୍ଜା ବା ଦୋଷ ନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A student is embarrassed that acquaintances have seen her selling repaired furniture to support her studies. Her aunt quotes the saying, affirming the work rather than measuring its social prestige.
entries.cultural_context: Livelihood is the explicit lexical sense. Dignity against occupational snobbery is editorial application, not a named movement, historical event or licence for wrongdoing.

entries.odia: ଗାଁଆଁ ପରିମଳ ଧୋବା ତୁଠରୁ ଜଣା
entries.title: The everyday edge tells a story
entries.literal_meaning: A village’s reputation is known from the washer’s bathing or washing place.
entries.explanation: The dictionary glosses the village’s “fragrance” as its greatness or reputation. The saying locates a clue to that reputation in an ordinary washing place rather than in a grand announcement. Our reading takes this as a contrast between what is claimed and what everyday surroundings reveal. It can encourage looking at a shared, practical corner before accepting a polished description. It does not supply a sanitary test or establish that the whole character of a community can be judged from one place.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଗାଁର “ପରିମଳ” ମାନେ ତାହାର ମାହାତ୍ମ୍ୟ ବା ସୁଖ୍ୟାତି। ସେହି ବଡ଼ ପରିଚୟକୁ ଏଠାରେ ଧୋବା ତୁଠ ପରି ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ସ୍ଥାନ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଦାବି କରାଯାଉଥିବା ଗୌରବ ଓ ସାଧାରଣ ବ୍ୟବହାରରେ ଦିଶୁଥିବା ଅବସ୍ଥାର ତୁଳନା ଆସେ। ଦୂରରୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସା ଶୁଣିବା ସହ ପାଖର ଛୋଟ କଥାକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଦେଖିବାର ଅବକାଶ ଏଥିରେ ଅଛି।
entries.english_summary: An ordinary shared place may reveal more than a grand claim of reputation.
entries.odia_summary: ବଡ଼ ପ୍ରଶଂସା ସହ ସାଧାରଣ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ସ୍ଥାନ ମଧ୍ୟ ପରିଚୟ ଦେଇପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A club advertises its excellent organisation, but leaves its shared workroom unusable. A member quotes the saying to suggest that the everyday space deserves attention before another publicity campaign.
entries.cultural_context: Historical occupational image is retained without making caste traits or purity claims. The headword supplies reputation; everyday-maintenance application is editorial. No measured sanitation, geography or community assessment is claimed.

entries.odia: ପଡ଼ିଲା ଉତ୍ତାରୁ ଯେ ମାରସି ଲାତ, ପୁଡ଼ିଯାଉ ସେ ଗୋଡ଼ହାତ
entries.title: Kicking someone who has fallen
entries.literal_meaning: Who kicks after someone has fallen—may those hands and feet burn.
entries.explanation: The anger is directed at the person who adds a kick after a fall. The curse gives the protest force: a moment of vulnerability has been used for further harm. We read the line as condemning that cruelty, while preserving its harsh words as the historical quotation rather than a wish to injure someone now. In conversation it can rebuke piling ridicule or blame onto a person already in difficulty. That nonviolent application is editorial; the source’s literal image remains a kick.
entries.meaning_odia: ପଡ଼ିଯାଇଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ କରିବା ବଦଳରେ ଯିଏ ପୁଣି ଗୋଇଠା ମାରେ, ତାହା ପ୍ରତି ଏହି ରାଗ। ଶେଷର ଅଭିଶାପରେ ପ୍ରତିବାଦର ତୀବ୍ରତା ଦିଶେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ କଥାଟି ଅସହାୟ ମୁହୂର୍ତ୍ତରେ ଆଉ ଆଘାତ ଯୋଡ଼ିବାକୁ ନିନ୍ଦା କରେ। ଆଜି କାହାର ଅସୁବିଧା ଦେଖି ଅଧିକ ଉପହାସ କରିବା ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗରେ ଏହାକୁ କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ; ଶରୀରର କ୍ଷତି କରିବାକୁ ଆମନ୍ତ୍ରଣ ଭାବେ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: The fierce protest condemns adding harm when someone is already vulnerable.
entries.odia_summary: ବିପଦରେ ପଡ଼ିଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଆଉ ଆଘାତ ଦେବା ବିରୋଧରେ ତୀବ୍ର ପ୍ରତିବାଦ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A team member makes a costly mistake and admits it. When others keep mocking him after the problem is resolved, a colleague quotes the saying to stop the piling-on, not to threaten anyone.
entries.cultural_context: The source labels the headword Sambalpur; this does not establish exclusive origin. Curse retained as quoted rhetoric, not endorsed retaliatory violence. No historical incident or speaker identified.

entries.odia: ଛେଛରି ଛତା, ହାଟ୍କେ ନେଲେ ପଇସା ହେତା
entries.title: Even the torn umbrella
entries.literal_meaning: A torn umbrella: taken to market, it could have brought money.
entries.explanation: The dictionary spells out the small possibility: the torn umbrella could be sold for money if taken to market. Damage has not automatically made it valueless. The conditional ending makes the value depend on taking it to market; it could sound practical or rueful, depending on the occasion. Our present-day reading asks whether something dismissed as useless still has an honest use or exchange value. It is not a guarantee that every broken object will sell, and the defect should not be hidden from a buyer.
entries.meaning_odia: ଛତାଟି ଚିରା, ତଥାପି ହାଟକୁ ନେଇ ବିକିଲେ ପଇସା ମିଳନ୍ତା ବୋଲି ଅଭିଧାନ ବୁଝାଇଛି। ଖରାପ ହୋଇଗଲା ମାତ୍ରେ ଜିନିଷଟିର ସବୁ ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଶେଷ ହୋଇନାହିଁ। “ହେତା”ରେ ହାଟକୁ ନେଇ ବିକିବାର ସର୍ତ୍ତ ସହ ପଇସା ମିଳିବାର ସମ୍ଭାବନା ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଫିଙ୍ଗିଦେବା ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଜିନିଷର ଅବଶିଷ୍ଟ କାମକୁ ଭାବିବାର ଅବକାଶ ଅଛି।
entries.english_summary: The damaged object may still bring money if taken to market.
entries.odia_summary: ଚିରା ଜିନିଷ ହାଟକୁ ନେଇ ବିକିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ପଇସା ମିଳିପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: During a clear-out, someone is about to discard an old umbrella whose frame can still be used. A friend quotes the line and suggests offering it openly as a damaged item to someone who repairs umbrellas.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary labels this a Sambalpur form and gives the selling gloss. No standardisation of ହାଟ୍କେ or ହେତା, no market-price claim or fraudulent-sale advice. Practical application is editorial.

entries.odia: ପୂରୂବ କହ୍ନେଇ କି? ଲହୁଣିଆଁ ମାଠ କାନ୍ଧରେ ପଡିଲେ, ମଣିଷ ଚିହ୍ନଇ କି?
entries.title: A fine shawl and forgotten faces
entries.literal_meaning: Is this the former Kahnei? With a fine soft shawl on the shoulder, does he recognise people?
entries.explanation: The question contrasts a remembered person with the way he now behaves. The fine shawl becomes the visible sign beside a failure to recognise others. Our reading hears a teasing accusation that improved appearance or standing has brought social distance. The line does not tell us that the cloth itself changes character, or that everyone whose circumstances improve becomes proud. Its force is directed at the particular person being addressed through this pointed question.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏ କି ସେଇ ପୂର୍ବର କହ୍ନେଇ—ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପୁରୁଣା ପରିଚୟ ଓ ଏବର ଆଚରଣ ମୁହାଁମୁହିଁ ହେଉଛି। କାନ୍ଧର ସରୁ କୋମଳ ଚାଦର ପାଖରେ ମଣିଷ ନ ଚିହ୍ନିବାର କଥା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ବେଶ ବା ସ୍ଥିତି ବଦଳିଲା ପରେ ପୁରୁଣା ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଅବହେଳା କରିବା ଉପରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ପୋଷାକଟି ନିଜେ ଦୋଷୀ ନୁହେଁ; ତାହା ପିନ୍ଧିଥିବା ଲୋକର ବ୍ୟବହାର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପଡ଼ୁଛି।
entries.english_summary: A changed appearance becomes an image for forgetting familiar people.
entries.odia_summary: ବେଶ ବଦଳିଲା ପରେ ପରିଚିତ ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ ଭୁଲିବାରେ କଟାକ୍ଷ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After a promotion, a friend stops greeting the people who used to share lunch with him. One of them quotes the saying in a private conversation, teasing the new distance rather than the friend’s clothes.
entries.cultural_context: The source labels the headword Jajpur; no exclusive origin follows. Kahnei remains the name in the quotation, not an identified deity or historical person. Fine soft cloth is explicit; fibre, cost and status-history are not established. Source spelling ପୂରୂବ retained.

entries.odia: ନିତି ମଳୁକୁ ଚାହାନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ
entries.title: When lasting illness becomes invisible
entries.literal_meaning: They do not look towards the chronically ill person.
entries.explanation: The dictionary defines the person in the line as chronically ill. The statement records a harsh lack of attention, but its brief quotation gives no speaker or occasion to tell us whether the neglect was being observed, lamented or defended. Our reading uses it critically: a difficulty that lasts can cease to attract the attention given to a new crisis. That is a way to question neglect, not a reason to accept it or a claim that every family behaves this way.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ “ନିତି ମଳୁ”ର ଅର୍ଥ ଦୀର୍ଘଦିନ ରୋଗରେ ପୀଡ଼ିତ ଲୋକ। ତାଙ୍କ ଆଡ଼କୁ ଚାହାନ୍ତି ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ପଦଟି କଠୋର ଏକ ଅବହେଳା କହେ। କିଏ କେଉଁ ଭାବରେ କହିଥିଲେ, ଛୋଟ ଉଦ୍ଧୃତିରୁ ତାହା ଜଣାଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଆମେ ଏହାକୁ ଅବହେଳାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରି ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ: କଷ୍ଟଟି ବହୁଦିନ ରହିଲା ବୋଲି ତାହା ପ୍ରତି ଧ୍ୟାନ ଶେଷ ହୋଇଯିବ କାହିଁକି?
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading questions attention fading while someone’s illness continues.
entries.odia_summary: ଦୀର୍ଘ କଷ୍ଟ ସହ ଧ୍ୟାନ ମଧ୍ୟ କାହିଁକି କମିଯାଏ—ଆମର ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପଢ଼ା।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Friends notice that they stopped calling someone whose illness has lasted many months. One quotes the line as an uncomfortable description of their own neglect and proposes asking what contact the person would welcome.
entries.cultural_context: Historical quotation is not endorsed as care advice. Critical application is explicitly editorial; source supplies chronic illness and lack of attention, not diagnosis, a universal family trait or evidence of the original speaker’s intention.

entries.odia: ଝିଅ ମଲେ ଜୋଇଁ କାହାର ଗୋତ?
entries.title: A relationship questioned after loss
entries.literal_meaning: When the daughter dies, whose relative is the son-in-law?
entries.explanation: The question presents a relationship as if it depends entirely on the woman through whom it was formed. Her death becomes the point at which the son-in-law’s place is questioned. The dictionary explains kinship vocabulary, but supplies no family story or evidence that the question describes a universal custom. Our reading approaches it critically: loss can expose how narrowly people define belonging. It need not settle the answer for a real bereaved family, whose affection and obligations cannot be reduced to this rhetorical line.
entries.meaning_odia: ଝିଅର ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ପରେ ଜୋଇଁ ଆଉ କାହାର ସମ୍ପର୍କୀୟ—ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଏକମାତ୍ର ସଂଯୋଗ ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କରାଉଛି। ଯେଉଁ ଝିଅ ଦୁଇ ପରିବାରକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ିଥିଲେ, ତାଙ୍କ ଅନୁପସ୍ଥିତିରେ ଜୋଇଁଙ୍କ ସ୍ଥାନ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପଡ଼ୁଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହା ସମ୍ପର୍କର ସଂକୀର୍ଣ୍ଣ ସୀମାକୁ ଭାବିବାର ଅବସର। ଶୋକରେ ଥିବା କୌଣସି ପରିବାର କାହାକୁ ନିଜର ମାନିବେ, ଏହି ପଦ ତାହାର ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading questions a narrow account of belonging after a family loss.
entries.odia_summary: ପରିବାରରେ ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ପରେ ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ସଂକୀର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଭାବେ ମାପିବାର ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: In a reading group, someone quotes the line while discussing how kinship is defined. Another reader challenges its implied exclusion, pointing out that shared care can outlast the person who first connected a family. This is an invented discussion, not advice delivered to a bereaved person.
entries.cultural_context: Critical interpretation only; no claim about contemporary marriage, inheritance law, a caste custom or every family’s conduct. The source does not establish whether the original use lamented or endorsed exclusion.

entries.odia: ଘୁ ଘୁ ଦେଖିଛି ଫାନ୍ଦ ଦେଖି ନାହିଁ
entries.title: The bird, but not the trap
entries.literal_meaning: Has seen the dove, but has not seen the trap.
entries.explanation: The two halves separate familiarity with an attractive or ordinary sight from knowledge of the danger connected with it. Seeing the bird does not mean seeing the trap. In our reading, the line can warn against mistaking partial experience for a full understanding of a situation. It may also sound like a taunt to someone who thinks they already know enough. The dictionary identifies the bird but gives no trapping story; the modern application and tone are editorial possibilities, not proof of an original event.
entries.meaning_odia: ପକ୍ଷୀଟିକୁ ଦେଖିଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ ଫାନ୍ଦକୁ ଦେଖିନାହିଁ—ଦୁଇ ପ୍ରକାର ଜାଣିବାର ତଫାତ ଏଠାରେ ଆସେ। ଚିହ୍ନା ଜିନିଷଟିକୁ ଜାଣିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ା ବିପଦ ଅଜଣା ରହିପାରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଅଳ୍ପ ଅନୁଭବକୁ ପୂରା ଜ୍ଞାନ ଭାବିବା ବେଳେ କଥାଟି ସତର୍କ କରେ। କହିବାର ସ୍ୱର ଅନୁସାରେ ଏହା ଚେତାବନୀ ବା ଟିକିଏ ତାଚ୍ଛଲ୍ୟ ମଧ୍ୟ ହୋଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: Familiarity with what is visible may leave its accompanying danger unseen.
entries.odia_summary: ଦିଶୁଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ଚିହ୍ନିଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ ତାହା ସହ ଥିବା ବିପଦ ଅଜଣା ରହିପାରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A new organiser knows how to book a hall and assumes the whole event will be easy. An experienced colleague quotes the line, then explains the overlooked cancellation conditions. The analogy concerns incomplete preparation, not an actual bird trap.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary labels the headword Medinipur; this does not establish birthplace or exclusive use. Bird identified generically as dove from source, no taxonomic or trapping instruction. Figurative application is our close reading; no supplied traditional moral gloss.

entries.odia: ଯତ୍ନ କଲେ ରତ୍ନ ମିଳେ
entries.title: Effort and the gem
entries.literal_meaning: If one makes an effort, one finds a gem.
entries.explanation: The small change from jatna, effort, to ratna, gem, gives the line its compact promise. The valuable result is pictured as something worth looking and working for. A speaker can use the conditional line to encourage another attempt when a task seems unrewarding. This encouraging use follows the wording and the dictionary definition of trying; it is not evidence that effort always succeeds. In our reading, the gem gives effort a direction without making failure a verdict on someone’s worth.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯତ୍ନରୁ ରତ୍ନ—ଧ୍ୱନିର ଛୋଟ ବଦଳରେ ଚେଷ୍ଟା ଓ ମୂଲ୍ୟବାନ ଫଳ ପାଖାପାଖି ଆସିଯାଏ। ଖୋଜିବା ଓ କାମ କରିବାର ଆଗ୍ରହକୁ ରତ୍ନର ଚିତ୍ର ଟାଣେ। କୌଣସି କାମରେ ଫଳ ନ ଦେଖି ମନ ଛାଡ଼ିଦେଉଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଆଉଥରେ ଚେଷ୍ଟା କରିବାକୁ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହା ଉତ୍ସାହର କଥା; ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ଚେଷ୍ଟାରେ ସଫଳତା ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ବା ଅସଫଳ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ କମ୍ ବୋଲି ବିଚାର ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: The rhyme encourages effort toward a worthwhile result, without guaranteeing success.
entries.odia_summary: ଯତ୍ନ ଓ ରତ୍ନର ମିଳ ମୂଲ୍ୟବାନ ଫଳ ପାଇଁ ଚେଷ୍ଟାର ଉତ୍ସାହ ଦିଏ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Two friends are trying to mend a loose chair. After the first adjustment fails, one says “ଯତ୍ନ କଲେ ରତ୍ନ ମିଳେ” and suggests checking the other joint. The line encourages a more careful second attempt rather than promising that the chair must be repairable.
entries.cultural_context: Source definesଯତ୍ନ କରିବା as trying/endeavouring and labels the lineଢଗ. Sound contrast and encouragement are editorial close reading, not a named author’s theory or origin account.

entries.odia: ପରଧନେ ଲହର ଫହର; ଛଡାଇ ନେଲେ ଲାଜେ ମର
entries.title: A flourish on someone else’s wealth
entries.literal_meaning: You move about in style on another’s wealth; when it is taken away, you die of shame.
entries.explanation: The first half gives someone room to move and make a show; the second suddenly takes that support away. The dictionary defines the headword as moving to and fro, while the verse puts that movement on another person’s wealth. Read as a taunt, it catches the embarrassment of displaying what one cannot claim as one’s own. The closing “die of shame” is exaggerated reproach, not a literal instruction. Our wider reading concerns borrowed display and insecure pretension, not the worth of people who receive help.
entries.meaning_odia: ପରର ଧନରେ ଚାଲିଛି ଲହର ଫହର; ସେ ଧନ ଫେରିଗଲେ ଦେଖାଣିର ଭିତ୍ତିଟି ମଧ୍ୟ ରହେନାହିଁ। ପ୍ରଥମ ଭାଗର ଆରାମ ଓ ଚଳପ୍ରଚଳକୁ ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଭାଗର ଲାଜ ହଠାତ୍ ଅଟକାଇଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ନିଜର ନୁହେଁ ଏମିତି ଜିନିଷକୁ ନିଜ ବଡ଼ପଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ କରି ଦେଖାଇବା ଏହି ଟାହିର ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ। “ଲାଜେ ମର” କଥାର ଅତିରଞ୍ଜନ; ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନେଉଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଛୋଟ କରିବା ଏଠାରେ ଆମର ପଢ଼ା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Borrowed display can become embarrassment when its support is withdrawn.
entries.odia_summary: ପରର ଧନରେ ନିଜ ବଡ଼ପଣ ଦେଖାଇଲେ, ତାହା ଫେରିଗଲେ ଲାଜରେ ପଡ଼ିବାର ଟାହି।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone poses with a friend’s expensive camera and lets others think it belongs to them. When the friend asks for it back, another friend quotes the saying softly. The joke concerns the false impression, not borrowing a camera.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary labels the headword Sambalpur; this is a source label, not proof of exclusive regional origin. The display reading is editorial close reading, not an independently supplied traditional-use gloss.

entries.odia: ଦଦରା ଡ଼ଙ୍ଗା, ମଝି ନଈରେ ଦେଲୁ ଦଗା
entries.title: The boat fails midstream
entries.literal_meaning: Worn-out boat, you betrayed me in the middle of the river.
entries.explanation: The boat is addressed as though it had broken a promise. Its failure comes in midstream, where the traveller is already relying on it and cannot simply step back onto the bank. That timing gives the short complaint its force. As an editorial application, it can describe an unreliable tool or arrangement failing at the moment it is most needed. The line supplies a vivid reproach; it does not establish a real accident or give instructions for crossing a river.
entries.meaning_odia: ଡ଼ଙ୍ଗାକୁ ମଣିଷ ପରି ଡାକି କୁହାଯାଉଛି—ତୁ ଠିକ୍ ମଝି ନଈରେ ଦଗା ଦେଲୁ। କୂଳରେ ଥିଲେ ପଛକୁ ଫେରିହେବ; ମଝିରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିଲା ପରେ ସେହି ଭରସା ଭାଙ୍ଗିବାର କଷ୍ଟ ଅଧିକ। ଦଦରା ଡ଼ଙ୍ଗା ଓ ଦଗାର ଧ୍ୱନିମିଳ ଅଭିଯୋଗକୁ ଆହୁରି ମନେ ରଖାଏ। ଆମର ଆଧୁନିକ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ, ଦରକାର ବେଳେ ଅଚଳ ହୋଇଯାଉଥିବା ଉପକରଣ ବା ଭରସାହୀନ ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ।

entries.title: Plenty for penalties, nothing for devotion
entries.literal_meaning: There are sixty kahans for penalties, but not a small cowrie amount for devotion to Hari.
entries.explanation: The verse sets a large expense beside a tiny amount refused. Its religious contrast is explicit: money can be found for a penalty or an expense one is forced to bear, yet none is available for devotion to Hari. The dictionary’s separate definition of taṇḍa includes fines and compelled expenditure; it does not tell us what offence, if any, lies behind this line. Our reading hears a reproach about priorities, made memorable by the unequal sums. That reading preserves the devotional voice without making spending on worship a test of anyone’s goodness.
entries.meaning_odia: ତଣ୍ଡ ପାଇଁ ବଡ଼ ଅଙ୍କର ଧନ ଅଛି, ହରିଙ୍କ ଭକ୍ତି ପାଇଁ ଅଳ୍ପଟିଏ ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଅସମାନ ତୁଳନାରେ କଥାର ଖୋଚା। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ତଣ୍ଡର ଅର୍ଥ ଜୋରିମାନାଠାରୁ ବାଧ୍ୟ ହୋଇ କରାଯାଉଥିବା ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟନ୍ତ ଅଛି; ଏଠାରେ କେଉଁ ଘଟଣାର ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ତାହା କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, କେଉଁ କାମ ପାଇଁ ଟଙ୍କା ମିଳେ ଓ କେଉଁ କାମ ବେଳେ ଅଭାବ ଦେଖାଯାଏ, ସେହି ବାଛବିଚାରକୁ ଏହା ପଚାରେ। ମୂଳ କଥାର ଭକ୍ତିଭାବ ରହିଥାଏ, କିନ୍ତୁ ପୂଜାରେ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ କରିବାକୁ ମଣିଷର ଭଲମନ୍ଦର ମାପ କରିବା ଆମର ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A devotional reproach contrasts large compelled expenses with a small amount withheld.
entries.odia_summary: ବାଧ୍ୟ ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚ ପାଇଁ ବହୁତ, ଭକ୍ତି ପାଇଁ ଅଳ୍ପଟିଏ ନାହିଁ—ଖର୍ଚ୍ଚର ବାଛବିଚାରକୁ ଏହି ଖୋଚା।

entries.odia: ମୁଁ ଖାଇ ନାହିଁ, ପାଟି ଖାଇଚି ନିୟାମ କରିବା ଆସ
entries.title: The mouth ate, not I
entries.literal_meaning: I have not eaten; my mouth has eaten. Come, let us take an oath.
entries.explanation: The speaker tries to separate the mouth from the person who used it. The invitation to swear then gives this flimsy distinction an exaggerated air of certainty. Read as a joke about evasion, the line exposes how changing the subject of a sentence can leave the action unchanged. The dictionary explains taking an oath and records the saying; the account of evasive reasoning is our close reading. Its comic force lies in the transparent excuse, not in proving that every denial is dishonest.
entries.meaning_odia: ଖାଇଛି ପାଟି, ମୁଁ ନୁହେଁ—ନିଜ ଅଙ୍ଗକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଦାୟ ଏଡ଼ାଇବାର ଅଦ୍ଭୁତ ଯୁକ୍ତି। ତାହା ପରେ ନିୟାମ କରିବାକୁ ଡାକିବାରେ ସେହି ଦୁର୍ବଳ ସଫେଇ ଆହୁରି ହାସ୍ୟକର ହୁଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, କଥାର କର୍ତ୍ତା ବଦଳାଇଦେଲେ ମଧ୍ୟ କାମଟି ବଦଳେନାହିଁ—ଏହା ସେହି ଫାଙ୍କିକୁ ଧରେ। ଯେଉଁଠି ସଫେଇଟି ନିଜେ ନିଜର ଅସଙ୍ଗତି ଦେଖାଇଦେଉଛି, ସେଠି ଏହି ରସ ଲାଗେ; ସବୁ ଅସ୍ୱୀକାରକୁ ମିଛ ଭାବିବାର କଥା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: An absurd division between a person and their mouth makes an evasive excuse visible.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଜ କାମର ଦାୟ ପାଟି ଉପରେ ପକାଇ ଏଡ଼ାଇବାର ହାସ୍ୟକର ସଫେଇ।

entries.odia: ଲଙ୍କା— ଗଡୁଁ ଯେତେକ ଜାତ, ସମସ୍ତେ ଅସୁରଙ୍କ ସୁତ
entries.title: One verdict for everyone
entries.literal_meaning: All who are born from Lanka’s fortress are sons of asuras.
entries.explanation: The force falls on “all”: a shared place becomes a single verdict about everyone born there. The dictionary supplies the totalizing word and quotation; its Lanka entry separately identifies the mythological capital. Our critical reading notices how quickly this image shuts out individual differences. It can help us examine a sweeping accusation, but birthplace or descent does not establish anyone’s character.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥାର ଜୋର “ସମସ୍ତେ” ଉପରେ—ଗୋଟିଏ ଜାଗାରେ ଜନ୍ମ ହେଲେ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ଏକ ରାୟରେ ବାନ୍ଧିଦିଆଯାଉଛି। ଅଭିଧାନର ଲଙ୍କା ଶବ୍ଦରେ ପୌରାଣିକ ରାଜଧାନୀର ଅର୍ଥ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅଛି। ଆମର ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ଦେଖାଏ କିପରି ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀର ନାମରେ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିର ଭିନ୍ନତା ଲୁଚିଯାଏ। ଜନ୍ମସ୍ଥାନ ବା ବଂଶରୁ ମଣିଷର ଚରିତ୍ର ସ୍ଥିର ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ଆମେ ଏହି ରାୟକୁ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରୁନାହୁଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading questions a single verdict imposed on a whole group.
entries.odia_summary: ଗୋଟିଏ ନାମରେ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷୀ ଭାବିବାର ରାୟକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପଚାରେ।

entries.odia: ଶତିକଈ ପୁରସ୍ତମ ଗଲା, ତୁଣ୍ଡ଼ କଥା କହି କହି ମଲା
entries.title: A taunt that follows the speaker
entries.literal_meaning: Shatikai went to Purastama and died talking and talking.
entries.explanation: The repeated talking carries the taunt to an exaggerated ending. The dictionary explicitly marks Shatikai as a satirical feminine term for a lying or talkative woman; this is an insult, not a neutral portrait. Our reading follows how the verse makes speech swallow the whole journey. Its verbal energy can be appreciated while questioning its gendered target and refusing to treat women’s speech as an inherent fault.
entries.meaning_odia: “କହି କହି”ର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତିରେ କଥା ଚାଲିଥାଏ, ଶେଷରେ ମରିବାର ଅତିରଞ୍ଜନ ଆସେ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଶତିକଈକୁ ମିଛ କହୁଥିବା ବା ବାଚାଳା ସ୍ତ୍ରୀ ପ୍ରତି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗଶବ୍ଦ ବୋଲି ଦେଇଛି; ଏହା ନିରପେକ୍ଷ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଯାତ୍ରାକୁ ପଛରେ ପକାଇ କଥା କହିବାଟି ସବୁକିଛି ହୋଇଯାଏ। ଧ୍ୱନିର ରସ ବୁଝିବା ସହିତ ନାରୀଙ୍କ କଥାକୁ ସ୍ୱଭାବଗତ ଦୋଷ କରୁଥିବା ଟାହିକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ପଚାରିହୁଏ।
entries.english_summary: A gendered taunt exaggerates relentless talking; our reading questions its target.

entries.odia: ଫୁଲର ଭାର ନ ସହନ୍ତି ରାଣୀ
entries.title: The weight of a flower
entries.category: dictionary-labelled proverbial saying; editorial close reading
entries.literal_meaning: The queen cannot bear the weight of a flower.
entries.explanation: The joke makes an almost weightless thing into a burden fit to overwhelm a queen. The dictionary defines the flower-weight expression as the weight of something very light; it does not identify a queen or describe an actual incident. Our reading hears exaggerated delicacy in the contrast. In a playful exchange, it could tease someone who makes a tiny agreed task sound immense. That use depends on knowing the situation: the line cannot tell us whether another person is in pain or what they can safely manage.
entries.meaning_odia: ଫୁଲ ପରି ହାଲୁକା ଜିନିଷର ଭାର ବି ରାଣୀ ସହିପାରୁନାହାନ୍ତି—ଏହି ବଢ଼ାଇ କହିବାରେ ହସ ଅଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ “ଫୁଲର ଭର”କୁ ଅତି ହାଲୁକା ବସ୍ତୁର ଭାର ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ; କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ରାଣୀଙ୍କ ଘଟଣା ଦିଏନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଅତି ସୁକୁମାର ଭାବ ଦେଖାଇବାର ଟାହି ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଆଗରୁ ରାଜି ହୋଇଥିବା ଛୋଟ କାମକୁ କେହି ବଡ଼ ବୋଝ କରି କହିଲେ, ସାଙ୍ଗମାନଙ୍କ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଏହା ହାଲୁକା ଥଟ୍ଟା ହୋଇପାରେ। କିନ୍ତୁ କାହାର କଷ୍ଟ ବା ସାମର୍ଥ୍ୟକୁ ଏହି କଥାରୁ ମାପିହେବ ନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A flower becomes an enormous burden in an exaggerated picture of delicacy.
entries.odia_summary: ଫୁଲର ହାଲୁକା ଭାରକୁ ଅସହ୍ୟ ବୋଝ କରି ଦେଖାଇବାରେ ଟାହି ଅଛି।

The other answers with the flower-and-queen line, and they laugh before starting. This harmless teasing scene is an editorial application, not a collected performance.
entries.cultural_context: The queen is the figure named in the saying, not proof of a historical royal custom or a trait of women. No medical judgment or obligation to ignore discomfort is implied. The source gloss defines light weight, not a complete social-use rule.

entries.odia: କୁକୁର୍କେ ଲାର୍ଡ କଲେ ମୁହେଁ ଚାଟ୍ସି
entries.title: Affection and familiarity
entries.category: dictionary-labelled proverbial saying; editorial close reading
entries.literal_meaning: If you lavish affection on the dog, it licks your face.
entries.explanation: The response is close and physical: affection is answered by a lick on the face. The headword gloss specifies excessive fondness, which gives the image its edge. Our reading follows the speaker’s complaint that encouraged familiarity has become more intimate than expected. The joke can also turn back on that speaker: what kind of response did the invitation encourage? Applying it to people is a sharp comparison, not a neutral description of their worth; boundaries can be discussed without treating anyone as inferior.
entries.meaning_odia: ଗେହ୍ଲା ପାଇ କୁକୁର ମୁହଁ ଚାଟୁଛି—ଉତ୍ତରଟି ଅତି ନିକଟର। ଅଭିଧାନର ଶବ୍ଦାର୍ଥରେ ଅତ୍ୟଧିକ ଗେହ୍ଲା କରିବା ବା ମୁହଁ ଦେବା ଅଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ନିଜେ ବଢ଼ାଇଥିବା ନିକଟତା ଆଶାଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ହେଲା ବୋଲି କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ହସଟି ତାଙ୍କ ଆଡ଼କୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଫେରିପାରେ: ସେ ନିଜେ କେମିତି ଉତ୍ତରକୁ ଉତ୍ସାହ ଦେଇଥିଲେ? ମଣିଷକୁ ଏହି ତୁଳନାରେ କହିବା ତୀକ୍ଷ୍ଣ ଟାହି; କାହାକୁ ହୀନ କରିବା ଛଡ଼ା ମଧ୍ୟ ନିଜର ସୀମା କହିହୁଏ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading notices how encouraged familiarity can exceed the inviter’s expectations.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଜେ ବଢ଼ାଇଥିବା ନିକଟତା ନିଜ ଆଶାଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ହେବାର ଟାହି ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଆସେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A club organizer tells friends to drop in whenever they like, then complains when they arrive during his quiet afternoon. He quotes the dog line about his own overgenerous invitation. A friend suggests stating visiting hours clearly instead of blaming the guests. The self-directed use is an editorial choice.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary marks the headword Sambalpur regional usage; that is not an exclusive origin claim. Quoted ଲାର୍ଡ is retained without silently changing it to the headword spelling ଲାଡ଼. This is a reading of a social comparison, not animal-care guidance or a rule that kindness produces ingratitude.
