entries.odia: ଡାହାଣୀ ହୋଇ ଲାଗିବା; ଗୁଣିଆ ହେଇ ଝାଡିବା
entries.title: Creating trouble, claiming the cure
entries.category: dictionary-labelled proverbial saying; editorial close reading
entries.literal_meaning: To afflict as a witch, then drive it out as the healer.
entries.explanation: Two roles face one another in a short, balanced line: the one associated with the affliction and the one who removes it. The headword explains possession in the language of a historical belief. Our close reading treats the paired roles as an image of someone creating trouble and then claiming credit for relief. The change of role, rather than a documented supernatural event, supplies the sting. A modern example can expose a manufactured problem without making accusations of witchcraft against any person.
entries.meaning_odia: ଛୋଟ କଥାଟିରେ ଦୁଇ ଭୂମିକା ମୁହାଁମୁହିଁ—ଲାଗିବା ଭୂମିକା ଓ ଝାଡ଼ିବା ଭୂମିକା। ଅଭିଧାନର ଶବ୍ଦାର୍ଥରେ ଅପଦେବତା ଆବିର୍ଭାବର ପୁରୁଣା ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହି ଯୋଡ଼ି ଭୂମିକା ନିଜେ ଅସୁବିଧା ତିଆରି କରି ପୁଣି ତାହା ଦୂର କରିବାର ଶ୍ରେୟ ନେବାର ଚିତ୍ର ହୁଏ। ଭୂମିକା ବଦଳରେ କଥାର ଦଂଶନ ଅଛି; ଏହା କୌଣସି ଅଲୌକିକ ଘଟଣାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ। ଆଜିର ଉଦାହରଣରେ କୃତ୍ରିମ ସମସ୍ୟାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିହୁଏ, କାହାକୁ ଡାହାଣୀ ବୋଲି ଅଭିଯୋଗ ନକରି।
entries.english_summary: Our reading sees the same person creating a problem and claiming credit for its remedy.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଜେ ସମସ୍ୟା କରି ତାହାର ସମାଧାନର ଶ୍ରେୟ ନେବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଆସେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: An organizer deliberately removes a useful instruction from a form, then presents restoring it as his special solution to everyone’s confusion. A colleague quotes the paired-role line while explaining what changed. The example criticizes the documented alteration, not anyone’s supposed supernatural powers.
entries.cultural_context: The supernatural vocabulary is historical source language, not an endorsed explanation of illness. The dictionary supplies the headword definition and saying, not an explicit figurative-use gloss; the manufactured-problem reading is editorial. No identified healer, ritual, community practice or origin is established.

entries.odia: ଯେସା ବୀଜ ତେସା ଅଙ୍କୁର
entries.title: Seed and sprout
entries.literal_meaning: As the seed, so the sprout.
entries.explanation: The repeated matching words make the beginning and its result answer one another. The dictionary explains ତେସା as “of that kind”; it supplies no social-use gloss. Our reading applies the image to work: what goes into a task can shape what comes out. This is a comparison to examine, not a guarantee of results or a judgment about inherited human worth.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯେମିତି ବୀଜ, ସେମିତି ଅଙ୍କୁର—ମେଳ ଖାଉଥିବା ଶବ୍ଦରେ ଆରମ୍ଭ ଓ ଫଳ ଯୋଡ଼ିହୁଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ତେସାର ଅର୍ଥ ସେହି ପ୍ରକାରର ବୋଲି ଦିଏ; ବ୍ୟବହାରର ପୂରା ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଦିଏନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ କାମର ଆରମ୍ଭରେ ଯାହା ରଖୁ, ଫଳରେ ତାହାର ଚିହ୍ନ ରହିପାରେ। ଏହା ଫଳର ନିଶ୍ଚୟତା ବା ମଣିଷର ବଂଶଗତ ମୂଲ୍ୟର ରାୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading connects a task’s starting material with its result.
entries.odia_summary: କାମର ଆରମ୍ଭ ଓ ଫଳର ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ଦେଖେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A team copies an unchecked list into its new catalogue, then finds the same mistakes there. A colleague quotes the seed-and-sprout line and suggests checking the original list before copying it again. This application concerns a process, not anyone’s parentage.
entries.cultural_context: The headword is labelled adapted from Hindi; this does not establish the saying’s origin or route of borrowing. No caste, family or community trait is inferred.

entries.title: Adding to a hurt
entries.literal_meaning: Smear mustard paste on a cut wound.
entries.explanation: The short phrase puts a deliberate action against an existing hurt. The dictionary glosses ଛାପ୍ୱା as smearing and repeats the expression with ମଡ଼ାଇବା. Our figurative reading hears an added injury: a taunt or needless reproach when someone is already upset. The wound is the image carrying that reading, not a treatment instruction.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆଗରୁ କଟା ଘା ଅଛି, ତାହା ଉପରେ ପୁଣି ବେଶର ବୋଳାଯାଉଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ଛାପ୍ୱାକୁ ବୋଳିବା ବା ମଡ଼ାଇବା ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଆମ ରୂପକ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଆଗରୁ ଦୁଃଖିତ ଲୋକକୁ ଟାହି ବା ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ଭର୍ତ୍ସନାରେ ଆହୁରି କଷ୍ଟ ଦେବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଆସେ। ଏହି ଘାର ଚିତ୍ର କଥାର ଦଂଶନ ବୁଝାଏ, ଚିକିତ୍ସାର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading hears a further hurt added to one already felt.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଗରୁ ଥିବା କଷ୍ଟକୁ ଆହୁରି ବଢ଼ାଇବାର ଚିତ୍ର।

entries.title: Drop after drop
entries.category: descriptive rhythmic formula; dictionary-labelled Dhaga, not a moral proverb
entries.literal_meaning: Juice drips—drop, drop.
entries.explanation: The repeated ending lets the ear follow separate drops. Unlike a moral saying, this short formula describes an action through sound. The source explicitly glosses juice falling drop by drop. Our reading enjoys the playful rhythm without adding a lesson about people or claiming a particular performance tradition.
entries.meaning_odia: ଥପଂ ଥପଂର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତିରେ ଟୋପା ପରେ ଟୋପା ପଡ଼ିବାର ଲୟ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ମଧ୍ୟ କୌଣସି ଦ୍ରବ୍ୟରୁ ଟୋପା ଟୋପା ରସ ଗଳିବା ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଏଠି ଶବ୍ଦର ଖେଳ ଗୋଟିଏ କ୍ରିୟାକୁ ଶୁଣାଏ; ମଣିଷ ପାଇଁ ନୀତିବାକ୍ୟ ତିଆରି କରେନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହି ଛୋଟ ଲୟର ରସଟି ମୁଖ୍ୟ।
entries.english_summary: A descriptive sound-play formula follows juice falling drop by drop.
entries.odia_summary: ଟୋପା ଟୋପା ରସ ଗଳିବାକୁ ଶବ୍ଦର ଲୟ ଅନୁସରେ।

entries.title: Every role in the same hands
entries.literal_meaning: Father is the deity’s servant, son the priest; body and head are all yours.
entries.explanation: The father-and-son pairing gathers the roles into one circle. The dictionary explicitly explains the saying as “you have become all-in-all here.” Our reading follows the teasing accusation of concentrated control: who is left to question a decision? The image does not establish wrongdoing by a family or religious occupation. Its application to a modern committee is our own.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାପ ଓ ପୁଅଙ୍କ ଭୂମିକାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ି ସବୁକିଛି ଗୋଟିଏ ପରିସରରେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରେ—ତୁମ୍ଭେ ଏଠାରେ ସର୍ବେସର୍ବା ହୋଇଛ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ କ୍ଷମତା ଏକାଠି ହୋଇଯିବାର ଟାହି ଅଛି: ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତିକୁ ପଚାରିବାକୁ ଆଉ କିଏ ରହିଲା? ଏହା କୌଣସି ପରିବାର ବା ଧାର୍ମିକ ବୃତ୍ତିର ଦୋଷର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ। ଆଜିର ସମିତି ସହ ତୁଳନା ଆମର ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ।
entries.english_summary: The source’s all-in-all gloss gives a teasing picture of concentrated authority.
entries.odia_summary: ସର୍ବେସର୍ବା ହୋଇ ବସିବାର ଟାହି ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଆସେ।

entries.title: Asking the way home
entries.literal_meaning: You will ask the way to your father’s home; do not set your mind on Ayodhya as well.
entries.explanation: The line contrasts asking directions to a familiar home with wishing for another destination. The dictionary defines the father’s home in a bride’s context but gives no figurative-use gloss. Our reading hears a sharp challenge to an ambition: first consider the knowledge needed for the journey. That challenge can itself be questioned; needing directions does not prove someone incapable of learning or travelling.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାପଘରର ପଥ ପଚାରିବା ସହ ଅଯୋଧ୍ୟାକୁ ମନ କରିବାର ବିରୋଧ ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ବାପଘରକୁ ବଧୂର ପିତୃଗୃହ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ, ରୂପକ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଦିଏନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଆକାଂକ୍ଷା ପ୍ରତି ଏକ ତୀକ୍ଷ୍ଣ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଅଛି—ଯାତ୍ରା ପାଇଁ କଣ ଜାଣିବା ଦରକାର? କିନ୍ତୁ ପଥ ପଚାରିବାରୁ କେହି ଶିଖିବା ବା ଯାତ୍ରା କରିବାକୁ ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ସ୍ଥିର ହୁଏନାହିଁ।

entries.title: When a skill becomes a verdict
entries.literal_meaning: If, being a girl, she is not fit for kitchen work, her birth is wasted.
entries.explanation: The conditional turns a cooking expectation into a verdict on a girl’s entire life. The dictionary places this line under the act of cooking. Our critical reading questions that leap: a useful skill becomes a measure of human worth, imposed by gender. The source preserves the harsh judgment; it does not supply our rejection of it.
entries.meaning_odia: ରୋଷେଇର ଯୋଗ୍ୟତାକୁ ଏଠି ଝିଅର ସମଗ୍ର ଜୀବନର ରାୟ କରାଯାଇଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ପାକକର୍ମ ଅର୍ଥରେ ଏହି କଥା ଦିଏ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ସେହି ଡେଇଁବାକୁ ପଚାରେ: ଗୋଟିଏ ଦରକାରୀ କୌଶଳ କିପରି ଲିଙ୍ଗ ଆଧାରରେ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ମାପେ? କଠୋର ରାୟଟି ଉତ୍ସରେ ଅଛି; ତାହାକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବା ଆମର ପଢ଼ା।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading questions measuring a girl’s worth by cooking ability.

entries.title: Leaving nothing unfinished
entries.literal_meaning: A remnant of debt, a remnant of illness—never leave a trace of either.
entries.explanation: The paired remnants give the instruction its insistence: a problem left over still demands attention. This is the saying’s absolute rhetoric, not a promise that illness or debt can always be eliminated. Our transfer to unfinished paperwork draws on that insistence without turning the line into medical or financial advice.
entries.meaning_odia: ଋଣ ଓ ରୋଗର ଅବଶେଷକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ି କଥାଟି ଜୋର ଦେଉଛି—ରହିଯାଇଥିବା ସମସ୍ୟା ପୁଣି ଧ୍ୟାନ ମାଗେ। ଏହା କଥାର ନିରଙ୍କୁଶ ଆଦେଶ, ସବୁ ରୋଗ ବା ଋଣ ନିଶ୍ଚୟ ଦୂର ହେବାର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ନୁହେଁ। ଅଧାରହିଥିବା କାଗଜକାମରେ ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ସେହି ଜୋରକୁ ନେଉଛି; ଚିକିତ୍ସା ବା ଆର୍ଥିକ ପରାମର୍ଶ ଦେଉନାହିଁ।

entries.cultural_context: The headword means complete cure. The verse gives an absolute exhortation; it does not establish causes of illness or blame people with continuing difficulties.

entries.title: Start again for the headman
entries.literal_meaning: When the headman arrives, sing from the beginning.
entries.explanation: In our reading, a late arrival changes where the song must begin. Placed under “village headman,” the line brings authority into that restart. Our reading hears a teasing complaint: everyone else has already listened, but the important newcomer gets the beginning again. The dictionary supplies the role, not a documented performance custom or this modern meeting application.

entries.english_summary: Our reading hears a teasing restart for someone with authority.

entries.title: Trouble where I sought refuge
entries.literal_meaning: I fled into my aunt’s house; my aunt struck me at a bad time.
entries.explanation: The first-person speaker runs towards a relative and meets another blow. Our reading follows that reversal: the hoped-for refuge adds to the trouble. The quotation follows the headword’s “bad time” sense; its other senses are noon and midnight, so a precise clock time is not established here. The line gives one sharp scene, not a verdict on aunts.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥକ ପଳାଇ ସମ୍ପର୍କୀୟଙ୍କ ଘରେ ପଶିଲେ, ସେଠି ପୁଣି ମାଡ଼ ଖାଇଲେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଆଶ୍ରୟର ଆଶା ଓ ନୂଆ ବିପଦର ଓଲଟା ଚିତ୍ର ଅଛି। ଉଦ୍ଧୃତିଟି ଅଭିଧାନର ଅସମୟ ଅର୍ଥ ପରେ ଆସିଛି; ଅନ୍ୟ ଅର୍ଥ ମଧ୍ୟାହ୍ନ ଓ ଅର୍ଦ୍ଧରାତ୍ର। ତେଣୁ ଏଠି ଘଣ୍ଟାର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ସମୟ ଧରାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଗୋଟିଏ ତୀକ୍ଷ୍ଣ ଘଟଣା ସବୁ ମାଉସୀଙ୍କ ବିଚାର ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading follows refuge turning into further trouble.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଶ୍ରୟ ଖୋଜି ଆଉ ଦୁଃଖ ପାଇବାର ଓଲଟା ଚିତ୍ର।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After a difficult committee meeting, someone asks a friend for help drafting a reply. The friend begins another scolding. “ପଳେଇ ପଶିଲି ମାଉସୀ ଘରେ…” the visitor says ruefully. Here the added blow is criticism; that nonliteral setting is our invention.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary’s placement guides this translation without erasing its multiple time senses. The example transfers physical violence into verbal disappointment; it does not approve either.

entries.title: Resolve and a neighbourhood’s stigma
entries.literal_meaning: If the mind is firm, then a home even in the sex workers’ quarter.
entries.explanation: The contrast makes firmness of mind stand against a stigmatized address. The source defines the quarter but gives no account of its residents’ conduct. Our critical reading separates personal resolve from that inherited suspicion: where someone lives cannot establish their worth. This challenge to the stigma is our response, not a counter-moral supplied by the saying.
entries.meaning_odia: ମନର ଦୃଢ଼ତା ସାମ୍ନାରେ ଏଠି ଏକ କଳଙ୍କିତ କରାଯାଇଥିବା ଠିକଣା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଉତ୍ସ ସାହିର ଅର୍ଥ ଦିଏ, ବାସିନ୍ଦାଙ୍କ ଆଚରଣର ବିବରଣୀ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ମନର ଦୃଢ଼ତାକୁ ସେହି ସନ୍ଦେହଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ: ଠିକଣାରୁ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଜଣାଯାଏନାହିଁ। କଳଙ୍କକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବା ଆମର ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା, କଥାଟି ଦେଇଥିବା ଓଲଟା ନୀତି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading distinguishes resolve from prejudice about an address.
entries.odia_summary: ମନର ଦୃଢ଼ତାକୁ ଠିକଣାର ପୂର୍ବଧାରଣାଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରିବା।

They discuss the contrast without judging its residents. This is an invented critical conversation, not collected traditional usage.
entries.cultural_context: Historical derogatory naming remains in the exact witness. No named neighbourhood, universal community trait, documented incident or contemporary sex-work condition is inferred.

entries.odia: ନିତି ମାଗନ୍ତାକୁ ଦିଅନ୍ତା ନାହିଁ
entries.title: Asking every day
entries.literal_meaning: For the person who asks every day, there is no giver.
entries.explanation: The daily asking meets an absolute “no giver” in the answering half. The dictionary defines the daily asker; it does not explain why help is needed or absent. Our reading considers the impatience that repetition can provoke, while questioning whether repeated need makes someone undeserving. Deliberate refusal is a possible interpretation, not an action established by the wording.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରତିଦିନ ମାଗିବାର ଉତ୍ତରରେ କଥାଟି ଦେବାଲୋକର ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଅଭାବ ରଖେ। ଅଭିଧାନ ନିତି ମାଗିବାକୁ ଆସୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିକୁ ବୁଝାଏ; ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ନ ମିଳିବାର କାରଣ ଦିଏନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ବାରମ୍ବାର ଅନୁରୋଧରୁ ଜନ୍ମିପାରୁଥିବା ବିରକ୍ତିକୁ ବିଚାର କରେ। ପୁଣି ମାଗିଲେ ବୋଲି କେହି ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟ ହୁଏ କି? ଜାଣିଶୁଣି ମନା କରିବା ଏକ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ପଢ଼ା, ଶବ୍ଦରୁ ସ୍ଥିର ହୋଇଥିବା କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Daily asking meets no giver; our reading considers impatience without assuming its cause.
entries.odia_summary: ନିତି ମାଗିଲେ ଦେବାଲୋକ ନାହିଁ; ତାହାର କାରଣ ନ ଧରି ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ବିରକ୍ତିକୁ ବିଚାର କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A neighbour repeatedly borrows a chair for evening lessons. Someone quotes the saying in irritation. Another asks whether they could agree on a regular arrangement instead. The invented reply questions the refusal; it does not establish a traditional answer.
entries.cultural_context: The source names no class or community. Its categorical wording is not evidence that people in continuing need are unworthy or that assistance is always refused.

entries.odia: କାହାର କି ଚିନ୍ତା, ବାଇଣ୍ଟି ପୋଇଲିର ଘଇତା ଚିନ୍ତା
entries.title: Everyone has a concern
entries.literal_meaning: Whatever others worry about, the girl addressed with this taunt worries about a husband.
entries.explanation: The opening leaves everyone else’s concerns unspecified, then singles out a girl’s interest in a husband for teasing. The dictionary calls the address mild abuse used by mothers towards young girls. Our critical reading notices the unequal permission to have a concern: her interest becomes the joke. It does not turn the insult into an affectionate nickname or establish what any girl actually wants.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆରମ୍ଭରେ ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କ ଚିନ୍ତା ଅନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ; ଶେଷରେ ଝିଅର ସ୍ୱାମୀଚିନ୍ତାକୁ ଟାହି କରାଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ସମ୍ବୋଧନକୁ ମାଆମାନେ ଟୋକୀ ଝିଅଙ୍କୁ ଦେଉଥିବା ଗାଳି ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ଦେଖେ—ନିଜ ଚିନ୍ତା ରଖିବାର ସୁଯୋଗ ସମାନ ନୁହେଁ, ତାହାର ଆଗ୍ରହ ହସର କଥା ହୁଏ। ଗାଳିକୁ ସ୍ନେହନାମ କରାଯାଉନାହିଁ, କୌଣସି ଝିଅର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଇଚ୍ଛା ମଧ୍ୟ ଧରାଯାଉନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: The taunt singles out a girl’s concern; our critical reading questions that scrutiny.
entries.odia_summary: ଝିଅର ଆଗ୍ରହକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଟାହି କରିବାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପଚାରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A reading group compares how different people’s interests become jokes. One reader quotes the line; another asks why the girl’s interest is singled out while everyone else’s remains unnamed. This is a present-day invented discussion, not a collected family conversation.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary marks Ganjam usage, not an exclusive origin or a practice of every family. The abusive expression remains in the exact witness; no community or gender trait is inferred.

entries.title: The world in two colours
entries.literal_meaning: The world is two-coloured.
entries.explanation: This brief expression offers a contrast without naming its two sides. The dictionary explains the headword through opposite colours or different pictures. Our reading treats the world’s changing appearance as an invitation to compare experiences, not proof that everyone is deceitful. A cheerful public occasion and difficult work behind it are one editorial application, not the source’s prescribed pair.
entries.meaning_odia: ଛୋଟ କଥାଟି ଦୁଇ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱର ନାମ ନ ଦେଇ ବିରୋଧର ଚିତ୍ର ରଖେ। ଅଭିଧାନ ବିପରୀତ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣ ବା ଭିନ୍ନ ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଶବ୍ଦଟିକୁ ବୁଝାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଦୁନିଆର ଭିନ୍ନ ଦେଖା ଅଭିଜ୍ଞତାକୁ ମେଳାଇ ଦେଖିବାକୁ କୁହେ; ସବୁ ଲୋକ ଛଳନାକାରୀ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରମାଣ ଦିଏନାହିଁ। ଆନନ୍ଦମୟ ଅନୁଷ୍ଠାନ ଓ ପଛର କଠିନ କାମ ଆମର ପ୍ରୟୋଗ, ଉତ୍ସ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ କରିଥିବା ଯୋଡ଼ି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A short image of contrast leaves its two sides open; our example supplies one pair.
entries.odia_summary: ବିରୋଧର ଛୋଟ ଚିତ୍ର; ଦୁଇ ପାର୍ଶ୍ୱକୁ ଆମ ଉଦାହରଣ ପୂରଣ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: After a neighbourhood celebration, two volunteers see the bright photographs and the pile of chairs still to be stacked. One recalls the two-coloured-world expression. They mean the contrast between the public occasion and its remaining work, not dishonesty by the guests.
entries.cultural_context: A short dictionary-labelled aphoristic expression, not a recovered longer proverb. No fixed moral, traditional performance setting or universal human trait is supplied.

entries.title: A fever with pointed timing
entries.literal_meaning: Fever came at paddy-pounding time; fever left at rice-boiling time.
entries.explanation: The paired arrivals make the timing conspicuous: illness accompanies one stage of food preparation and disappears at another. Our reading hears a possible teasing suspicion about avoiding the harder work. The source does not prove that anyone pretended to be ill, and boiling rice is not yet eating it. The contrast can carry an accusation without making that accusation true.
entries.meaning_odia: ଖାଦ୍ୟ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତିର ଗୋଟିଏ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟରେ ଜର ଆସେ, ଅନ୍ୟ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟରେ ଛାଡ଼େ—ଦୁଇ ସମୟକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ି କଥାଟି ନଜର ଟାଣେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ କଠିନ କାମ ଏଡ଼ାଇବା ପ୍ରତି ଟାହିମିଶା ସନ୍ଦେହ ଶୁଣାଯାଇପାରେ। କେହି ମିଛରେ ଅସୁସ୍ଥ ହୋଇଥିଲେ ବୋଲି ଉତ୍ସ ପ୍ରମାଣ ଦିଏନାହିଁ; ଭାତ ଫୁଟିବା ମଧ୍ୟ ଖାଇବା ନୁହେଁ। ବିରୋଧରେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଆସିପାରେ, ତାହା ସତ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading notices suspicious timing without treating it as proof of pretence.
entries.odia_summary: ସମୟର ମେଳରେ ସନ୍ଦେହ ଉଠିପାରେ, ଛଳନାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: In a reading discussion, someone quotes the two timings and laughs at the apparent convenience. Another points out that illness can change and asks what the line actually establishes. This imagined exchange separates a joke from evidence about a sick person.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary defines fever abatement. No medical explanation, diagnosis, work instruction or documented household incident is established; the teasing inference is editorial.

entries.odia: ଆଶା ଲୁବଧରେ ପୂରିଲା କାଳ, ଷଣ୍ଢ ପଛେଧାଇଁ ମଲା ଶିଆଳ
entries.title: Following an expectation too far
entries.literal_meaning: Life ran out in hope and greed; the fox died chasing after the bull.
entries.explanation: The first clause names hope and greed; the second gives them a fatal pursuit. The dictionary places the quotation under avarice. Our reading follows the cost of staying with an expectation until nothing is left for anything else. The line does not say what the fox hoped to obtain or how it died; no remembered fable is supplied to fill those gaps.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଥମ ଖଣ୍ଡ ଆଶା ଓ ଲୋଭ କହେ, ଦ୍ୱିତୀୟ ଖଣ୍ଡ ସେଥିରେ ମରଣାନ୍ତକ ପିଛାକରିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଦିଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଉଦ୍ଧୃତିକୁ ଲୋଭ ଅର୍ଥରେ ରଖିଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଆଶା ପଛରେ ଲାଗି ଅନ୍ୟ ସବୁ ପାଇଁ ସମୟ ସରିଯିବାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଦେଖାଯାଏ। ଶିଆଳ କଣ ପାଇବାକୁ ଚାହୁଁଥିଲା ବା କିପରି ମଲା, କଥାଟି କହେନାହିଁ। ମନେଥିବା କୌଣସି କାହାଣୀରେ ସେହି ଫାଙ୍କ ପୂରଣ କରାଯାଇନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Hope and greed become a fatal pursuit; its precise object remains unnamed.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଶା ଓ ଲୋଭର ପିଛାରେ ଜୀବନ ସରେ; ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟବସ୍ତୁ ଅନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: A hobby club keeps postponing its modest exhibition while waiting for an unconfirmed grand venue. A member quotes the fox-and-bull line and suggests deciding what can actually be arranged. The invented application concerns time spent chasing a possibility, not a prediction of disaster.
entries.cultural_context: The separate Jagannath–Bhagabata example illustrates the earlier poetic adjective; it is not credited as author of this saying. Animal imagery is literary, not zoological evidence.

entries.title: My meal, your troubled face
entries.literal_meaning: I am eating my own rice; why is your hand on your cheek?
entries.explanation: The speaker sets their own meal against someone else’s troubled pose. The dictionary explains that pose through distress. Our reading hears a pointed question about another person’s reaction: why should my ordinary act trouble you? It may sound teasing or defensive, but the line does not establish envy or explain the observer’s concern. That unanswered reason gives the exchange its edge.
entries.meaning_odia: କଥକ ନିଜ ଭାତ ଖାଇବା ସାମ୍ନାରେ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଦୁଃଖୀ ଭଙ୍ଗୀ ରଖନ୍ତି। ଅଭିଧାନ ଗାଲରେ ହାତ ଦେବାକୁ ଦୁଃଖରେ ବୁଝାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ତୀକ୍ଷ୍ଣ—ମୋର ସାଧାରଣ କାମ ତୁମକୁ କାହିଁକି ବ୍ୟଥିତ କରୁଛି? ଏଥିରେ ଟାହି ବା ନିଜକୁ ସମର୍ଥନ କରିବାର ସ୍ୱର ଥାଇପାରେ। କିନ୍ତୁ ଈର୍ଷା ସ୍ଥିର ହୁଏନାହିଁ, ଦେଖୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ଚିନ୍ତାର କାରଣ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅକୁହା। ସେହି ଅକୁହା କାରଣରେ କଥାର ଧାର ରହେ।
entries.english_summary: A pointed question contrasts one person’s meal with another’s distress; the cause is unstated.
entries.odia_summary: ଜଣଙ୍କ ଭାତ ଓ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଦୁଃଖର ବିରୋଧ; କାରଣ ଅକୁହା।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: At lunch, one friend eats while another rests a cheek in a hand. The eater playfully quotes the line. The friend replies that they are thinking about an unfinished letter. This invented reply shows why a troubled expression need not be envy.
entries.cultural_context: The source explains a gesture of affliction, not a universal body-language rule. No actual speaker, household incident or motive is documented.

entries.title: A verdict made from age
entries.literal_meaning: Wherever there are old people, there are fools.
entries.explanation: The repeated “wherever…there” makes age stand in for judgment. Our critical reading questions that shortcut: a person’s age cannot tell us whether a particular remark is foolish. The source preserves the insult, not this objection to it. Its sweeping rhythm can make the verdict sound settled before any individual has been heard.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯେଉଁଠି ସେଇଠିର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତି ବୟସକୁ ବିଚାରର ସ୍ଥାନରେ ବସାଏ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ଏହି ସହଜ ରାୟକୁ ପଚାରେ—ବୟସରୁ କାହାର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ କଥା ନିର୍ବୋଧ କି ନୁହେଁ ଜଣାଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଉତ୍ସ ଅପମାନଟି ରଖିଛି, ତାହା ପ୍ରତି ଆମର ଆପତ୍ତି ନୁହେଁ। ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ କଥା ଶୁଣିବା ଆଗରୁ ହିଁ ଛନ୍ଦର ଜୋର ରାୟକୁ ସ୍ଥିର ଭଳି ଶୁଣାଇପାରେ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading challenges a sweeping insult that substitutes age for judgment.
entries.odia_summary: ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ କଥା ବଦଳରେ ବୟସରେ ରାୟ ଦେବାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପଚାରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: In a reading group, someone quotes the line after discussing a disagreement between generations. Another asks them to examine the disputed suggestion itself rather than the speaker’s age. This imagined response challenges the generalization; it is not a traditional reply supplied by the source.
entries.cultural_context: A documented age-directed taunt, not evidence about cognition or the beliefs of every community. Our rejection of its blanket judgment is explicitly editorial.

entries.title: A face praised, a body judged
entries.literal_meaning: The face is beautiful; the body is ugly.
entries.explanation: The parallel halves divide one person into a praised face and a disparaged body. The dictionary places the last word under “ugly,” not its other senses of a lump or something flat. Our critical reading asks what this splitting does to the person being described. The source supplies the appearance judgment; our objection to reducing someone to it is editorial.

entries.title: An invitation to make trouble
entries.literal_meaning: If you have no quarrel, take two wives; if the rice does not run out, keep two residences.
entries.explanation: The paired invitations offer ways to acquire trouble or use up provisions. Our reading hears irony rather than practical instruction. It also questions the first half’s gendered assumption: conflict is assigned to a marriage arrangement without hearing the people involved. The second half turns to the cost of maintaining two places. Neither household outcome is demonstrated by the saying.

entries.english_summary: Our reading hears ironic invitations to trouble while questioning the gendered premise.

That application is editorial, not evidence of an actual bodily practice or a judgment about anyone’s worth.

entries.title: A headache without a head
entries.literal_meaning: There is no head, yet it has a headache.
entries.explanation: The line removes the head and keeps its ache: an impossible complaint compressed into a joke. The entry separately gives a figurative sense of deep anxiety. Our reading transfers the paradox to worry about a responsibility that does not exist; the source supplies no particular occasion for that use. It does not establish that anyone’s actual pain is false.
entries.meaning_odia: ମୁଣ୍ଡକୁ ବାଦ ଦେଇ ତାହାର ବଥାକୁ ରଖାଯାଇଛି—ଅସମ୍ଭବ ଅଭିଯୋଗଟି ହିଁ ପରିହାସ। ଏହି ଶବ୍ଦର ଅଲଗା ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥରେ ଗଭୀର ଚିନ୍ତା ଦିଆଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ନଥିବା ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ନେଇ ଚିନ୍ତାକୁ ଏହି ବିରୋଧାଭାସରେ ଦେଖାଯାଏ; ସେ ପ୍ରୟୋଗର କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଅବସର ଉତ୍ସ ଦିଏନାହିଁ। କାହାର ପ୍ରକୃତ ଯନ୍ତ୍ରଣା ମିଛ ବୋଲି ଏଥିରୁ ପ୍ରମାଣ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।

entries.odia_summary: ଅସମ୍ଭବ ମୁଣ୍ଡବଥାରେ ନଥିବା ଦାୟିତ୍ୱର ଚିନ୍ତାକୁ ନେଇ ଆମର ପରିହାସ।

entries.title: A fitting pair
entries.literal_meaning: Whatever suits each: soak black gram and rice.
entries.explanation: The entry defines the opening as what is appropriate to a person or thing. Its answer brings black gram and rice together in the action of soaking. Our reading follows the pairing: usefulness can depend on what accompanies something. The quotation names no finished dish, proportion or rule for sorting people into groups.
entries.meaning_odia: ଆରମ୍ଭର କଥାକୁ ଅଭିଧାନ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ବା ବସ୍ତୁ ପ୍ରତି ଯାହା ଉପଯୁକ୍ତ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଉତ୍ତରରେ ବିରି ଓ ଚାଉଳ ତିନ୍ତେଇବାର କାମ ଆସେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମେଳଟି ମୁଖ୍ୟ—ଗୋଟିଏ ଜିନିଷ ସହ କଣ ରହୁଛି, ତାହା ତାର ଉପଯୋଗକୁ ବଦଳାଇପାରେ। ଢଗଟି କୌଣସି ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତ ଖାଦ୍ୟର ନାମ, ପରିମାଣ ବା ମଣିଷକୁ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀରେ ବାଣ୍ଟିବାର ନିୟମ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।

entries.title: Fire from home
entries.literal_meaning: To tuck fire into the fold at one’s waist because it is the household’s fire.
entries.explanation: The reason offered is familiarity: the fire belongs to the house. The imagined act brings it against the body. Our reading questions treating something harmful as harmless merely because it is one’s own. The wording itself contains no explicit prohibition; this warning is our interpretation of the image.
entries.meaning_odia: କାରଣଟି ହେଉଛି ନିଜରପଣ—ନିଆଁଟି ଘରର। କିନ୍ତୁ ତାକୁ ଅଣ୍ଟିରେ ପୂରାଇବାର କଳ୍ପନା ଦେହ ପାଖକୁ ଆଣେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ନିଜର ବୋଲି କ୍ଷତିକାରକ ଜିନିଷକୁ ନିରାପଦ ଭାବିବା ନେଇ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଅଛି। ମୂଳ କଥାରେ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନିଷେଧ ନାହିଁ; ସତର୍କତାଟି ଏହି ଛବିରୁ ଆମର ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା।

entries.title: One goes round, one stays put
entries.literal_meaning: Milk goes from neighbourhood to neighbourhood; liquor is sold while sitting.
entries.explanation: Movement belongs to the milk; sitting belongs to the liquor sale. The contrast makes unequal selling effort visible. Our reading uses that imbalance to ask why one offering must seek attention while another receives it. The source does not explain the difference or supply evidence about actual demand.
entries.meaning_odia: ବୁଲିବାଟି ଗୋରସ ସହ, ବସି ବିକିବାଟି ମଦ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ବିକ୍ରିର ଦୁଇ ଭିନ୍ନ ପରିଶ୍ରମ ଏହି ବିରୋଧରେ ଦିଶେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠେ—ଗୋଟିଏ ଜିନିଷକୁ ଧ୍ୟାନ ପାଇବାକୁ ଖୋଜି ବୁଲିବାକୁ ପଡ଼ୁଛି, ଅନ୍ୟଟି ପାଖକୁ ଲୋକ ଆସୁଛନ୍ତି କାହିଁକି? ଏହି କାରଣ ବା ପ୍ରକୃତ ଚାହିଦାର ତଥ୍ୟ ଉତ୍ସ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।

entries.title: What has flowed, what remains
entries.literal_meaning: Let the water that has flowed away go that way; let the dammed water remain held.
entries.explanation: The two wishes face different water: what has already gone and what can remain contained. Our reading turns attention from recovering every loss to keeping what is still available. This is an editorial application of the contrast, not a promise that every loss can be repaired by restraint.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୁଇଟି ଇଚ୍ଛା ଦୁଇ ଅବସ୍ଥାର ପାଣିକୁ ନେଇ—ଯାହା ବୋହିଗଲା ଓ ଯାହା ଅଟକି ରହିଛି। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ ହରାଇଥିବା ଜିନିଷ ଫେରାଇବାଠାରୁ ଧ୍ୟାନ ଏବେ ଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ରଖିବା ଆଡ଼କୁ ଫେରେ। ଏହା ବିରୋଧଟିର ଆମର ପ୍ରୟୋଗ; ସଂଯମରେ ସବୁ କ୍ଷତି ଭରଣା ହେବ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading distinguishes a past loss from what can still be kept.
entries.odia_summary: ବିତିଥିବା କ୍ଷତି ଓ ରଖିପାରିବା ଜିନିଷ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଆମ ପଢ଼ାର ତଫାତ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ବର୍ଷାରେ ପଢ଼ାଚକ୍ରର ଗୋଟିଏ ଦିନ ବାତିଲ ହେଲା। ଆୟୋଜକ ସେଦିନକୁ ନେଇ ଅନୁତାପ କରୁଥିବାବେଳେ ସାଙ୍ଗ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ଆସନ୍ତା ଦୁଇଦିନର ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା କରିବା।” / Rain cancels one day of a reading programme. While an organiser regrets it, a friend recalls the saying: “Let us arrange the two days still ahead.” This application is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The verb’s dam-building sense supports the water image. No particular river, engineering method, conservation custom or practical water-management instruction is documented here.

entries.odia: ଛୋଟ ମୁହଁରେ ବଡ଼ କଥା, ଶୁଣିଲା ଲୋକର ମନ ବ୍ୟଥା
entries.title: Whose words cause offence?
entries.literal_meaning: Big words from a small mouth: the listener’s mind is hurt.
entries.explanation: The dictionary’s “small” marks a person treated as low or insignificant. The line places the listener’s hurt beside that person’s speech. Our critical reading asks whether the offence comes from the words or from refusing the speaker standing. That question challenges the hierarchy; it is not a tolerant moral supplied by the saying.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ “ଛୋଟ” କଥାଟି ନୀଚ ବା ନଗଣ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ଧରାଯାଇଥିବା ମଣିଷକୁ ସୂଚାଏ। ସେ ମଣିଷର କଥା ପାଖରେ ଶ୍ରୋତାର ମନବ୍ୟଥା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମର ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ—କଥାଟି ବାଧିଲା, ନା କହୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦା ଦେବାର ଅନିଚ୍ଛା? ଏହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଚ୍ଚନୀଚ ବିଚାର ଉପରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠାଏ; ଢଗଟି ନିଜେ ସହନଶୀଳତାର ନୀତି ଶିଖାଉଛି ବୋଲି କୁହାଯାଉନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading separates a speaker’s standing from the worth of the words.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ାରେ ବକ୍ତାର ସ୍ଥାନ ଓ କଥାର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ଅଲଗା।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ନୂଆ ସଦସ୍ୟ ହିସାବର ଏକ ଭୁଲ ଦେଖାଇଲେ। ଜଣେ ଢଗଟି କହି ତାଙ୍କୁ ଚୁପ୍ କରାଇବାକୁ ଚାହିଁଲେ। ସଭାପତି କହିଲେ, “ସେ କେତେଦିନର ସଦସ୍ୟ, ତାହା ନୁହେଁ; ହିସାବଟି ମେଳୁଛି କି ଦେଖିବା।” / A newcomer points out an accounting error. Someone invokes the saying to silence them. The chair replies, “Their membership is recent; let us still check the figures.” This critical exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: Historical rank language is retained as source evidence, not a judgment of anyone’s worth. The source identifies no caste, age, gender or particular speaker in the quotation.

entries.odia: ମଉନମୁହୀଁର ଅପାର ଗୁଣ
entries.title: So many fine qualities
entries.literal_meaning: The quiet one has boundless qualities.
entries.explanation: The praise turns on the dictionary’s explicitly ironic definition: apparently quiet, yet scheming. “Qualities” therefore carries a sting rather than straightforward admiration. Our critical reading keeps that insinuation audible while questioning it: silence alone cannot establish deceit. This response is ours, not a tolerant lesson hidden in the source.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନର ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ୍ୟ ଅର୍ଥ—ବାହାରକୁ ଚୁପ୍, ଭିତରେ କପଟ—ପ୍ରଶଂସାର ସ୍ୱରକୁ ଓଲଟାଇ ଦିଏ। ତେଣୁ “ଗୁଣ” କଥାରେ ସରଳ ପ୍ରଶଂସା ବଦଳେ ଖୋଚା ରହେ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ସେ ଇଙ୍ଗିତକୁ ରଖି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ: କେବଳ ଚୁପ୍ ରହିବା କପଟର ପ୍ରମାଣ ହୋଇପାରେନାହିଁ। ଏହି ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା ଆମର; ଉତ୍ସର ଗୁପ୍ତ ସହନଶୀଳ ଶିକ୍ଷା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Ironic praise conceals an accusation that our reading questions.
entries.odia_summary: ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ୍ୟ ପ୍ରଶଂସାର ଅଭିଯୋଗକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ବୈଠକରେ ଜଣେ ସଦସ୍ୟ କମ୍ କଥା କହିଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ଢଗଟି ଉଠାଇଲେ। ସଭାପତି କହିଲେ, “ଚୁପ୍ ଥିଲେ ବୋଲି ସନ୍ଦେହ କରିବା କାହିଁକି? ତାଙ୍କ ମତ ଶୁଣିବା।” / A member speaks little at a meeting. Someone invokes the line. The chair replies, “Why suspect them for being quiet? Let us hear their view.” This exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The head lists a feminine form matching the quotation. Its broad claim about quiet people is a historical dictionary judgment, not evidence about a gender or personality type.

entries.odia: ଧର୍ମ ଡଙ୍ଗା ସୁଖରେ ଯାଏ
entries.title: The boat of dharma
entries.literal_meaning: The boat of dharma travels happily.
entries.explanation: The entry places the line under following the religious path, then gives the literal boat sense. Its note records a belief that dharma keeps boats afloat. Read as an image of faith, the journey offers reassurance. Our interpretation preserves that confidence as a belief, without turning it into a physical promise of safety.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନ ଧର୍ମପଥ ଅନୁସରଣ ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଢଗଟି ରଖି ପରେ ପ୍ରକୃତ ନୌକାର ଅର୍ଥ ଦିଏ। ଟୀକାରେ ଧର୍ମ ଥିବାରୁ ଡଙ୍ଗା ଭାସୁଛି ବୋଲି ଏକ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ଲିପିବଦ୍ଧ। ଆସ୍ଥାର ଛବି ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ିଲେ ଯାତ୍ରାଟି ଆଶ୍ୱାସ ଦିଏ। ଆମ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ସେ ଭରସାକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱାସ ଭାବେ ରଖେ, ପ୍ରକୃତ ଯାତ୍ରାର ନିରାପତ୍ତା ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A boat image expresses religious confidence, not a safety guarantee.
entries.odia_summary: ଡଙ୍ଗାର ଛବିରେ ଧାର୍ମିକ ଭରସା, ନିରାପତ୍ତାର ନିଶ୍ଚୟତା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପଢ଼ାଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ ଢଗଟିକୁ ନିଜ ଆସ୍ଥାର କଥା ଭାବେ କହିଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଏଠି ଡଙ୍ଗାଟି ତୁମ ପାଇଁ କଣ?” ସେ କହିଲେ, “କଠିନ କାମରେ ଭରସା ରଖିବାର ଛବି।” / In a reading group, someone uses the saying to express faith. Asked what the boat means to them, they answer, “An image of keeping confidence through difficult work.” The exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The recorded belief is attributed to this dictionary witness; its prevalence, present practice and theological reach were not independently established. No navigation instruction or claim that faith prevents drowning follows.

entries.odia: ଆଗେରେ କାଳିଆ ! ନାହିଁ କରୁଥିଲୁ ସିଘାଂଣି ନାକକୁ ଦେଖି, ଏବେରେ କାଳିଆ ! ଝୁରି ମରୁଅଛୁ ଥନ ଯଉବନ ଦେଖି
entries.title: Your gaze has changed
entries.literal_meaning: Earlier, Kāḷiā, you refused on seeing the runny nose; now, Kāḷiā, you pine away on seeing breasts and youth.
entries.explanation: The same addressee is called twice, first for rejection and then for longing. The bodily contrast exposes a change in response. Our reading asks what such a reversal reveals about the observer’s standards, rather than treating a person’s worth as dependent on youthful appearance. The source does not identify the speaker, exact ages or relationship.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏକା ଲୋକକୁ ଦୁଇଥର ଡକାଯାଇଛି—ଆଗେ ନାହିଁ କରିବା ପାଇଁ, ଏବେ ଝୁରିବା ପାଇଁ। ଦେହକୁ ନେଇ ବିରୋଧଟି ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟାର ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନ ଦେଖାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଏହି ଓଲଟାଣି ଦେଖୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ମାନଦଣ୍ଡ ନେଇ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠାଏ; ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟକୁ ଯୌବନର ଦେଖାଶୁଣା ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କରାଏନାହିଁ। ବକ୍ତା, ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ବୟସ ବା ସମ୍ପର୍କ ଉତ୍ସ ଚିହ୍ନାଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A changed bodily response prompts our question about the observer’s standards.
entries.odia_summary: ଦେହ ଦେଖି ବଦଳିଥିବା ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟାରେ ଦର୍ଶକର ମାନଦଣ୍ଡକୁ ନେଇ ଆମ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଏକ ପାଠ ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ଏଠି ବଦଳିଥିବା ଦେହଠାରୁ ମୋତେ ଦେଖୁଥିବା ଲୋକର ବଦଳିଥିବା ବ୍ୟବହାର ବେଶି ବାଧୁଛି।” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ଢଗଟିକୁ ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନରେ ପୁଣି ପଢ଼ିଲେ। / In a reading discussion, someone says, “What troubles me more than the bodily change is the observer’s changed treatment.” Another rereads the saying through that question. This critical exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The name Kāḷiā is retained without identifying a deity or historical person. The bodily language remains explicit; no life story, universal attraction or documented courtship custom is inferred.

entries.odia: ମନର ଗୁଣେ ଫଳ ଫଳେ
entries.title: Fruit and the mind
entries.literal_meaning: Fruit grows according to the mind.
entries.explanation: The entry explains the opening as according to one’s mental state or thought. Fruit supplies an image of an outcome. Our reading asks how an attitude shapes the way someone approaches work; it does not claim that thoughts alone control events. Neither success nor suffering can be diagnosed from this short line.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନ ଆରମ୍ଭର କଥାକୁ ନିଜ ମନ ବା ଚିନ୍ତା ଅନୁସାରେ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଫଳ ଏଠି ପରିଣାମର ଛବି ଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମନୋଭାବ କାମକୁ କିପରି ଆଗେଇ ନିଏ, ସେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଅଛି; କେବଳ ଚିନ୍ତାରେ ଘଟଣା ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରିତ ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ଦାବି ନାହିଁ। ଏତିକି କଥାରୁ କାହାର ସଫଳତା ବା କଷ୍ଟର କାରଣ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading links outlook with approach, without promising control over results.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମନୋଭାବ ଓ କାମର ଧାରାର ସମ୍ପର୍କ, ଫଳ ନିୟନ୍ତ୍ରଣର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ନୁହେଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରର କାମ ଆରମ୍ଭ ପୂର୍ବରୁ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ଏଥିରେ କିଛି ହେବନି।” ସାଙ୍ଗ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ଫଳ କଣ ହେବ ଜାଣିନି; କିନ୍ତୁ ଚେଷ୍ଟାଟି ମନ ଦେଇ କରିବା।” / Before a reading-group project begins, someone dismisses it. A friend recalls the saying: “I cannot promise the outcome, but let us make a thoughtful attempt.” This exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The following Jagannath Bhagabata verse is a separate literary illustration, not evidence that Jagannath authored this saying. No psychological law, guaranteed reward or blame for hardship is inferred.

entries.odia: କହୁଛି ମତେ ରଗାନା, ମୋ ସାଙ୍ଗରେ ତୁ ଲାଗନା
entries.title: Do not provoke me
entries.literal_meaning: I am telling you: do not anger me; do not get into it with me.
entries.explanation: The speaker addresses “you” directly, repeating a demand to stop provoking them. The paired endings give the warning its rhythm. Our reading hears a boundary being voiced, without knowing whether the occasion was playful or tense. The source names no quarrel, threat or outcome.
entries.meaning_odia: ବକ୍ତା ସିଧା “ତୁ”କୁ କହି ବିରକ୍ତ କରିବା ବନ୍ଦ କରିବାକୁ ପୁଣି ଦାବି କରୁଛନ୍ତି। ଦୁଇ ଖଣ୍ଡର ମେଳ ଚେତାବନୀକୁ ଛନ୍ଦ ଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଜଣେ ନିଜ ସୀମା କହୁଥିବା ଶୁଣାଯାଏ; ଅବସରଟି ଥଟ୍ଟାର ଥିଲା କି ଉତ୍ତେଜନାର, ଜଣାଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ଝଗଡ଼ା, ଧମକ ବା ପରିଣାମ ଚିହ୍ନାଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: A rhythmic direct warning becomes our reading of a spoken boundary.
entries.odia_summary: ସିଧା ଛନ୍ଦମୟ ଚେତାବନୀରେ ନିଜ ସୀମା କହିବାର ଆମ ପଢ଼ା।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଜଣେ ସାଙ୍ଗ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଥଟ୍ଟା କଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ଢଗଟି କହି ଯୋଡ଼ିଲେ, “ମୋତେ ଏହା ଭଲ ଲାଗୁନି; ଏବେ ଛାଡ଼।” ସାଙ୍ଗ କଥାଟି ବନ୍ଦ କଲେ। / A friend repeats a joke. The other invokes the line and adds, “I do not like this; please stop now.” The friend stops. This peaceful outcome is invented, not supplied by the saying.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary labels the quotation Dhaga under causing anger. A voiced warning is retained as its genre; no settled traditional moral or universal rule for resolving conflict is claimed.

entries.odia: ପୀଢ଼ା ଫାଟେ ନାହି ଲେଉଟେ ତେବେ ସେ ବ୍ରାହ୍ମଣ ଠାଆରୁ ଉଠ
entries.title: A meal stretched into a taunt
entries.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: The stool cracks, the navel turns out—only then, Brahmin, rise from your place.
entries.explanation: Cracking furniture and the protruding navel exaggerate a meal into a caste-directed taunt. The final “rise” is retained as an apparent command, rather than silently made a report of what someone did. Our critical reading notices how bodily excess is attached to a named group; it rejects that attachment as evidence of the group’s conduct.
entries.meaning_odia: ଫାଟୁଥିବା ପୀଢ଼ା ଓ ବାହାରୁଥିବା ନାହି ଭୋଜନକୁ ବଢ଼ାଇ ଏକ ଜାତି ଉଦ୍ଦେଶ୍ୟରେ ଖୋଚା କରେ। ଶେଷର “ଉଠ”କୁ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ ଆଦେଶ ଭାବେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି; କିଏ କଣ କଲା ବୋଲି ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନାକୁ ବଦଳାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ଦେଖେ କିପରି ଦେହର ଅତିଶୟତା ଏକ ନାମିତ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଏ; ଏହାକୁ ସେ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀର ଆଚରଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ ମାନେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading questions a caste stereotype carried by exaggerated eating.
entries.odia_summary: ଅତିଶୟ ଭୋଜନର ଛବିରେ ଜାତିଗତ ଧାରଣାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠ ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ଜଣେ ପୀଢ଼ା ଫାଟିବାର ଛବିରେ ହସିଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଅତିଶୟତାରେ ହସିବା ଓ ଗୋଟିଏ ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀକୁ ସେପରି ଭାବିବା ଏକା କଥା କି?” / In a reading discussion, someone laughs at the cracking stool. Another asks, “Is laughing at an exaggeration the same as believing it about a whole group?” This critical exchange is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The source’s bodily gloss explains the image, not a diagnosis. Exact ending syntax remains elliptical; no historical meal, actual person, dietary instruction or customary group behaviour is established.

entries.odia: ଜାଣିଥିଲିକି? କିଏ ସୂନା କିଏ ପିତଳ ବୋଲି ନିକିତି ପକେଇ ତୁଳି ଥିଲିକି?
entries.title: Had I weighed them?
entries.literal_meaning: Did I know? Had I put them on a balance and weighed who was gold and who was brass?
entries.explanation: Two questions resist the expectation of prior knowledge. Gold and brass give the contrast a material image, while the balance suggests examination. Our reading hears someone explaining a mistaken judgment: they had not tested what they were asked to recognise. The source supplies no particular deception, person or transaction.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦୁଇଟି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିଥିବାର ଆଶାକୁ ଅଟକାଏ। ସୁନା ଓ ପିତଳ ବିରୋଧକୁ ବସ୍ତୁର ଛବି ଦିଏ, ନିକିତି ପରଖିବାକୁ ମନେ ପକାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଭୁଲ ବିଚାରର ସଫେଇ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ—ଯାହାକୁ ଚିହ୍ନିବା ଆଶା କରାଗଲା, ତାକୁ ପରଖାଯାଇନଥିଲା। ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଠକାମି, ମଣିଷ ବା କାରବାର ଦିଏନାହିଁ।

entries.title: The scrupulous woman
entries.literal_meaning: The scrupulous elder sister is applying cow-dung water to her body.
entries.explanation: The dictionary explicitly calls the address ironic and describes excessive observance of purity. The bodily action gives that irony a concrete image. Our reading asks how a claim to scrupulousness can become an object of ridicule, without accepting the ridicule as evidence about women or a whole tradition.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନ ସମ୍ବୋଧନଟିକୁ ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ୍ୟ ବୋଲି କହି ଅତିରିକ୍ତ ଆଚାରନିଷ୍ଠାର ଅର୍ଥ ଦିଏ। ଦେହରେ ଲଗାଇବାର କାମ ସେ ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ୍ୟକୁ ଏକ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ଛବି ଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଉଠେ—ଅତି ସତର୍କ ଆଚାରର ଦାବି କିପରି ପରିହାସର ବିଷୟ ହୁଏ? ସେ ପରିହାସକୁ ନାରୀ ବା ସମଗ୍ର ପରମ୍ପରା ବିଷୟରେ ପ୍ରମାଣ କରାଯାଇନାହିଁ।

entries.title: Expecting kindness from the cat
entries.literal_meaning: The tomcat eating its own young: an analogy.
entries.explanation: The dictionary explains the analogy as vainly expecting kindness toward another’s young from a cat that eats its own. The contrast concerns what one expects after the conduct already imagined. Our reading asks what grounds there are for trust; the premise is retained as the source’s analogy, not offered as a general fact about cats or a rule that people cannot change.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନ ଉପମାଟିକୁ ଏପରି ବୁଝାଏ—ନିଜ ଛୁଆ ଖାଉଥିବା ଭୁଆଠାରୁ ପର ଛୁଆ ପ୍ରତି ମମତା ଆଶା କରିବା ଦୁରାଶା। କଳ୍ପିତ ଆଚରଣଟି ଦେଖିସାରି କଣ ଆଶା କରାଯାଉଛି, ସେହି ବିରୋଧ ମୁଖ୍ୟ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଭରସାର ଆଧାର ନେଇ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଅଛି। ମୂଳ ଧାରଣାଟି ଉତ୍ସର ଉପମା ଭାବେ ରହେ, ବିରାଡ଼ି ବିଷୟରେ ସାଧାରଣ ତଥ୍ୟ ବା ମଣିଷ ବଦଳିପାରେନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ନିୟମ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading asks what supports an expectation of kindness.

Someone recalls the analogy: “Let us look for evidence that it has changed.” The application is invented and does not declare change impossible.

entries.title: Who is listening?
entries.literal_meaning: A Purana gathering in a deaf village: those who hear will be astonished.
entries.explanation: The line places a listening gathering in a village called deaf, then turns to those who hear. That tension carries the joke. Our critical reading asks about the assumed audience and the means of participation, rather than treating deafness as a lack of intelligence or interest. The source supplies no actual village or performance.
entries.meaning_odia: ଶୁଣିବାର ସଭାକୁ କାଲ ବୋଲି କୁହାଯାଇଥିବା ଗାଁରେ ରଖି, କଥାଟି ପୁଣି ଶୁଣିଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଆଡ଼କୁ ଫେରେ। ଏହି ଟାଣାପଡ଼ାରେ ପରିହାସ ରହେ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ଧରିନିଆଯାଇଥିବା ଶ୍ରୋତା ଓ ଭାଗ ନେବାର ଉପାୟକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ; ବଧିରତାକୁ ବୁଦ୍ଧି ବା ଆଗ୍ରହର ଅଭାବ ମାନେନାହିଁ। ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ପ୍ରକୃତ ଗାଁ ବା ପ୍ରଦର୍ଶନ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading questions the audience assumed by the joke.

entries.title: For this belly
entries.literal_meaning: This belly! For this belly, the road to Bengal.
entries.explanation: The repeated belly gives a bodily reason for the journey. The dictionary explains the phrase through Puri panda agents travelling to Bengal to gather pilgrims. Our reading hears livelihood behind the repeated exclamation: a route is taken because someone must eat. The source supplies no named traveller, dated journey or testimony.
entries.meaning_odia: ପେଟର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତି ଯାତ୍ରାର ଏକ ଦେହସମ୍ବନ୍ଧୀୟ କାରଣ ଦିଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହି ପଦକୁ ପୁରୀର ପଣ୍ଡା ଗୁମାସ୍ତାମାନେ ଯାତ୍ରୀ ସଂଗ୍ରହ ପାଇଁ ବଙ୍ଗଦେଶକୁ ଯିବା ସହ ବୁଝାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ପୁନରୁକ୍ତ ଡାକ ପଛରେ ଜୀବିକା ଶୁଣାଯାଏ—ଖାଇବାର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତା ପାଇଁ ବାଟ ଧରାଯାଏ। କୌଣସି ନାମିତ ଯାତ୍ରୀ, ତାରିଖ ଥିବା ଯାତ୍ରା ବା ସାକ୍ଷ୍ୟ ଉତ୍ସ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading hears the need for livelihood behind a named route.
entries.odia_summary: ନାମିତ ବାଟ ପଛରେ ଜୀବିକାର ଆବଶ୍ୟକତାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ଶୁଣେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଦୂରକୁ କାମ ପାଇଁ ଯାଉଥିବା ଜଣେ ସାଙ୍ଗ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ମୋ ବାଟ ବଙ୍ଗଳାକୁ ନୁହେଁ, କିନ୍ତୁ ପେଟର କଥାଟି ବୁଝୁଛି।” / A friend leaving for work far away recalls the saying: “My route is not to Bengal, but I understand the part about earning a meal.” This modern use is invented, not a documented pilgrimage account.
entries.cultural_context: The Puri label and agent explanation belong to this dictionary witness. They do not establish the saying’s origin, current recruitment practice or a motive shared by every practitioner.

entries.title: Onion and interest
entries.literal_meaning: Hindus do not eat onions; Pathans do not eat interest.
entries.explanation: The rhyme pairs eating onions with “eating” interest, giving two prohibitions the same verbal shape. The dictionary glosses biaja as loan interest and adds a religious explanation. Our critical reading notices how the line turns named communities into categorical statements. We retain those words as historical rhetoric, not as evidence of everyone’s diet, conduct or beliefs.
entries.meaning_odia: ପିଆଜ ଖାଇବା ସହ ସୁଧ “ଖାଇବା”କୁ ମେଳ ଦେଇ ଦୁଇ ନିଷେଧକୁ ଏକା ବାକ୍ୟଛାଞ୍ଚରେ ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଅଭିଧାନ ବିଆଜର ଅର୍ଥ ଋଣର ସୁଧ ଦିଏ ଓ ଧାର୍ମିକ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ା ଦେଖେ କିପରି ନାମିତ ସମୁଦାୟକୁ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ଏକାଭଳି ଦାବିରେ ବଦଳାଯାଏ। ଏହି ଶବ୍ଦକୁ ଐତିହାସିକ କଥନ ଭାବେ ରଖୁଛୁ, ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ଖାଦ୍ୟ, ଆଚରଣ ବା ବିଶ୍ୱାସର ପ୍ରମାଣ ଭାବେ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A rhyme makes categorical community claims that our reading questions.
entries.odia_summary: ଛନ୍ଦରେ ଗଢ଼ା ସମୁଦାୟର ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ବିଷୟରେ ଦାବିକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।

entries.title: A lament against the times
entries.literal_meaning: Let the ways of this age burn: while the grandfather is still alive, the grandson dies.
entries.explanation: The curse against the age is followed by a death that reverses the expected generational order. Our reading hears grief protesting that reversal. The line names no cause or particular family, and its anger at “the times” is not evidence that an era caused the death.
entries.meaning_odia: ଯୁଗକୁ ଅଭିଶାପ ଦେବା ପରେ ଏମିତି ମୃତ୍ୟୁ ଆସେ ଯାହା ପିଢ଼ିର ଆଶାକରା କ୍ରମକୁ ଓଲଟାଇ ଦିଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଶୋକ ସେ ଓଲଟାଣିକୁ ପ୍ରତିବାଦ କରୁଥିବା ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। କଥାଟି କୌଣସି କାରଣ ବା ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ପରିବାରର ନାମ ଦିଏନାହିଁ; “ଯୁଗ” ପ୍ରତି ରାଗ ମୃତ୍ୟୁର କାରଣ ଯୁଗ ଥିଲା ବୋଲି ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading hears grief resisting an expected order overturned.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଶାକରା କ୍ରମ ଓଲଟିଗଲେ ଶୋକର ପ୍ରତିବାଦକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ଶୁଣେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଏକ ପାଠ ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ଜଣେ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଯୁଗକୁ କାହିଁକି ଦୋଷ ଦିଆଯାଉଛି?” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ କହିଲେ, “ହୁଏତ କାରଣ ବୁଝାଇବାଠାରୁ ଦୁଃଖକୁ କହିବା ଏଠି ମୁଖ୍ୟ।” / A reading group asks why the age is blamed. Someone suggests that expressing grief may matter more here than explaining a cause. This discussion is invented, not testimony from a bereaved family.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary supplies the phrase “spirit of the age.” No historical mortality pattern, named death or literal call to burn anything is established.

entries.title: An alliance regretted
entries.literal_meaning: Seeing a great household, I made a kinship alliance; I took my daughter and gave her to Yama.
entries.explanation: The dictionary defines the great household by wealth and standing. The speaker’s first-person account turns that attraction into the terrible image of giving a daughter to Yama. Our reading hears regret over judging an alliance by status. The image does not establish an actual death, a particular form of harm or a story about every wealthy family.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନ “ବଡ଼ ଘର”କୁ ଧନ ଓ ପ୍ରତିଷ୍ଠାରେ ଚିହ୍ନାଏ। ବକ୍ତାର ନିଜ କଥାରେ ସେ ଆକର୍ଷଣ ଝିଅକୁ ଯମ ହାତରେ ଦେବାର ଭୟଙ୍କର ଛବିକୁ ଫେରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦା ଦେଖି ବନ୍ଧୁତା ବିଚାର କରିଥିବାର ଅନୁତାପ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଏହି ଛବି ପ୍ରକୃତ ମୃତ୍ୟୁ, ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ କ୍ଷତି ବା ସବୁ ଧନୀ ପରିବାରର କାହାଣୀ ସ୍ଥାପନ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading hears regret when family prestige becomes the basis of an alliance.
entries.odia_summary: ପରିବାରର ପ୍ରତିଷ୍ଠାକୁ ବନ୍ଧୁତାର ଆଧାର କରିବାର ଅନୁତାପ ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପଢ଼ାଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ଏହାକୁ ଧନୀ ଘର ଖରାପ ବୋଲି ପଢ଼ିବା?” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ କହିଲେ, “ମୁଁ ବରଂ କେବଳ ପ୍ରତିଷ୍ଠା ଦେଖି ବିଚାର କରିବାର ଅନୁତାପ ପଢ଼ୁଛି।” / A reader asks whether the line condemns wealthy households. Another replies, “I read regret about judging by prestige alone.” This critical discussion is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The daughter and kinship language suggest a marriage alliance; no marriage event, dowry account or abuse history is supplied. Yama is retained as the source’s death image.

entries.title: Something to console the mind
entries.literal_meaning: Nothing but nothing: mere kanji water to console the mind.
entries.explanation: The repeated dismissal makes the consolation sound slight. The dictionary explains the headword as an act that satisfies expectations left unmet. Our reading stays with that small substitute: it may soothe disappointment without becoming the thing originally hoped for. The source supplies no actual meal or measure of the food’s value.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାରମ୍ବାର ତୁଚ୍ଛ କହିବାରେ ସାନ୍ତ୍ୱନାଟି ସାମାନ୍ୟ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଅଭିଧାନ ମନମୁରୁଛାକୁ ଅପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଆଶାରେ ମନକୁ ବୁଝାଇବାର କାମ ବୋଲି ବୁଝାଏ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ସେହି ଛୋଟ ବଦଳି ଜିନିଷ ପାଖରେ ରହେ—ନିରାଶାକୁ କିଛି ଶାନ୍ତ କରିପାରେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ପ୍ରଥମେ ଚାହିଁଥିବା ଜିନିଷ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଉତ୍ସ କୌଣସି ପ୍ରକୃତ ଭୋଜନ ବା ଖାଦ୍ୟର ମୂଲ୍ୟ ମାପ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading distinguishes a small consolation from a fulfilled wish.
entries.odia_summary: ଛୋଟ ସାନ୍ତ୍ୱନା ଓ ପୂରଣ ହୋଇଥିବା ଆଶାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ଅଲଗା କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ବଡ଼ ନାଟକ ଦେଖିବାର ଯୋଜନା ବାତିଲ ହେଲା। ସାଙ୍ଗମାନେ ଘରେ ଏକ ଦୃଶ୍ୟ ପଢ଼ିଲେ। ଜଣେ ଢଗଟି ମନେ ପକାଇ କହିଲେ, “ସମାନ ନୁହେଁ, ତଥାପି ମନକୁ କିଛି ବୁଝାଇଲା।” / A planned theatre visit is cancelled. Friends read one scene together at home. Recalling the saying, someone remarks, “It is not the same, but it is some consolation.” This use is invented.
entries.cultural_context: Kanji water is retained as the food expression; the record establishes neither a recipe nor nutritional inferiority. The dismissive valuation belongs to the line’s rhetoric.

entries.title: Borrowing and answering for another
entries.literal_meaning: I would borrow, but would not become surety for someone else.
entries.explanation: The dictionary’s inline explanation distinguishes taking a loan from guaranteeing another person. The first-person voice accepts one involvement and refuses the other. Our reading hears a boundary between bearing one’s own obligation and answering for someone else; it does not turn that preference into a rule everyone should follow.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନର ସଂଲଗ୍ନ ବ୍ୟାଖ୍ୟା ଋଣ ନେବା ଓ ଅନ୍ୟ ପାଇଁ ଜାମିନ ହେବାକୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ। ବକ୍ତା ଗୋଟିଏ ସମ୍ପର୍କରେ ପଶିବାକୁ ମାନେ, ଅନ୍ୟଟିକୁ ମନା କରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ନିଜ ଦାୟ ନେବା ଓ ପର ପାଇଁ ଉତ୍ତରଦାୟୀ ହେବା ମଧ୍ୟରେ ସୀମା ଶୁଣାଯାଏ; ସେ ପସନ୍ଦ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ପାଇଁ ନିୟମ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading hears a speaker distinguishing two kinds of obligation.
entries.odia_summary: ଦୁଇ ପ୍ରକାର ଦାୟକୁ ଅଲଗା କରୁଥିବା ବକ୍ତାକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ଶୁଣେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “କଥାଟିରେ ଋଣଠାରୁ ଅଧିକ ଦାୟର ଭେଦ ମୋତେ ଶୁଣାଯାଉଛି।” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ନିଜ ପାଇଁ କହିବା ଓ ପର ପାଇଁ କଥା ଦେବା କି ଏକା?” / A reading group discusses the difference between speaking for oneself and giving one’s word for someone else. This discussion is invented, not borrowing advice.
entries.cultural_context: Sambalpur labels the dictionary’s verb, not a proven saying origin. The gloss supplies surety; this historical wording offers no present financial or legal guidance.

entries.title: Who will listen?
entries.literal_meaning: To whom shall I speak; who will listen? The master does not understand and will strike.
entries.explanation: The question about a listener is followed by the speaker’s expectation of a blow. Our reading hears the difficulty of speaking when the person with authority seems unwilling to understand. The line voices an expectation; it does not document an assault or establish how every master behaves.
entries.meaning_odia: ଶୁଣିବା ଲୋକ କିଏ ବୋଲି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ପରେ ବକ୍ତା ମାଡ଼ ଆଶଙ୍କା କରେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ କ୍ଷମତା ଥିବା ଲୋକ ବୁଝିବାକୁ ରାଜି ନଥିବା ମନେହେଲେ କଥା କହିବାର ଅସୁବିଧା ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। କଥାଟି ଆଶଙ୍କା ପ୍ରକାଶ କରେ; ପ୍ରକୃତ ଆକ୍ରମଣର ବିବରଣୀ ବା ସବୁ ସାଆନ୍ତଙ୍କ ବ୍ୟବହାରର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading hears an anxious search for someone willing to listen.
entries.odia_summary: ଶୁଣିବାକୁ ରାଜି ଲୋକଟିଏ ଖୋଜିବାର ଉଦ୍ବେଗ ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ଶୁଣାଯାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଏକ ଗଳ୍ପ ଆଲୋଚନାରେ ଜଣେ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ବକ୍ତାକୁ କିଏ ଶୁଣିପାରିବ?” ଦଳଟି ଏମିତି ଏକ ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ ଦୃଶ୍ୟ କଳ୍ପନା କଲା ଯେଉଁଠି କେହି କଥା ନକାଟି ଶୁଣେ। / Discussing a story, readers ask who could hear the speaker out. They imagine a following scene in which someone listens without interruption. This peaceful continuation is invented, not part of the source.
entries.cultural_context: The source illustrates an emphatic particle. Its neighbouring literary quotations do not identify this saying’s author. The authority-and-listening application is editorial, not a supplied historical incident.

entries.title: Land and a meal from elsewhere
entries.literal_meaning: The woman with sixty bāṭi of land asks for food at another’s yard or veranda.
entries.explanation: The dictionary defines a woman with extensive landholdings. The quotation sets that description beside asking and eating elsewhere. Our reading notices a gap between an imposing description of possessions and the immediate means of obtaining a meal. It leaves the reason open rather than declaring the woman dishonest or undeserving.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ବହୁ ଜମିର ଅଧିକାରିଣୀ ସ୍ତ୍ରୀଙ୍କୁ ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି। ଉଦ୍ଧୃତି ସେହି ପରିଚୟ ପାଖରେ ପରଘରେ ମାଗି ଖାଇବାକୁ ରଖେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ ସମ୍ପତ୍ତିର ବଡ଼ ପରିଚୟ ଓ ସେହି ବେଳର ଖାଇବା ଯୋଗାଡ଼ ମଧ୍ୟରେ ଫରକ ଦିଶେ। ଏହାର କାରଣ ଖୋଲା ରହେ; ସ୍ତ୍ରୀଜଣକ ଠକ ବା ସାହାଯ୍ୟର ଅଯୋଗ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ଆମେ ରାୟ ଦେଉନାହୁଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading distinguishes possessions from the meal immediately available.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ସମ୍ପତ୍ତି ଓ ସେହି ବେଳର ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଯୋଗାଡ଼କୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: କଥାଟି ପଢ଼ି ଜଣେ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଜମି ଅଛି ବୋଲି ସେହି ବେଳେ ଖାଇବା ଅଛି କି?” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ କହିଲେ, “ଏଠି କାରଣଟା ଲେଖାନାହିଁ।” / Two readers distinguish owning land from having a meal available and leave the missing explanation unresolved. Their discussion is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The female landowner is the source’s subject. Bāṭi is retained without conversion; the line establishes neither a historical person nor a cause of her request.

entries.title: The director behind the action
entries.category: dictionary-labelled Dhaga headword idiom; source-informed editorial reading
entries.literal_meaning: Gobardhan Das, the master of the play.
entries.explanation: The dictionary defines a concealed controller: others visibly act, while this person directs them. The theatrical wording identifies the person behind the action, not a documented theatre practitioner. Our application asks who actually makes a decision when somebody else announces it; hidden direction need not be guessed from appearances alone.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଏମିତି ଜଣେ ସୂତ୍ରଧରଙ୍କୁ ବୁଝାଏ, ଯିଏ ନିଜେ ଚିହ୍ନା ନପଡ଼ି ଅନ୍ୟମାନଙ୍କ କାମକୁ ଚଳାନ୍ତି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ହେଉଛି—ଖବର ଦେଉଥିବା ଲୋକ ଓ ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତି ନେଉଥିବା ଲୋକ କିଏ? କେବଳ ଚେହେରା ଦେଖି ଲୁଚା ସୂତ୍ରଧର ଥିବାର ଅନୁମାନ କରିବା ଠିକ୍ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: A named theatrical idiom points to concealed direction behind visible action.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଗରେ କାମ କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କ ପଛରେ ଥିବା ସୂତ୍ରଧରକୁ ଏହି ପଦଟି ବୁଝାଏ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ମୀନା ସଭାରେ ନୂଆ ସମୟ ଘୋଷଣା କଲେ। ରବି ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଏହି ସମୟ କିଏ ଠିକ୍ କଲା?” ମୀନା ନିଷ୍ପତ୍ତିର ଚିଠି ଦେଖାଇଲେ। / Meena announced a new meeting time. Ravi asked who had chosen it, and she showed him the decision letter. This invented scene explores responsibility; it does not establish a secret plot.
entries.cultural_context: The source labels the whole headword Dhaga and supplies its figurative meaning. Gobardhan Das remains part of the expression; this page does not identify a historical individual, author or origin. Bengali and Hindi equivalents are listed, not evidence of transmission direction.

entries.odia: ବୁଢ଼ା ଚୋରକୁ ଚୋରି ଶିଖଉଛି !
entries.title: Teaching the practised thief
entries.literal_meaning: Teaching an old hand at theft how to steal!
entries.explanation: The dictionary places this exclamation under a thief practised in the activity, separately from an elderly thief. Its joke makes the lesson unnecessary because the learner already knows the craft. Our everyday application questions instruction offered without first finding out what someone knows; it neither praises theft nor says experienced people cannot learn.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନର ଏହି ଅର୍ଥରେ ଚୋରଟି ଚୋରିରେ ପାରଙ୍ଗମ; କେବଳ ବୟସରେ ବୁଢ଼ା ନୁହେଁ। ଯିଏ କାମଟି ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣେ, ତାକୁ ସେହି କାମ ଶିଖାଇବାରେ କଥାର ମଜା। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ଶିଖାଇବା ଆଗରୁ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ କେତେ ଜାଣନ୍ତି, ତାହା ବୁଝିବା ଦରକାର। ଏହା ଚୋରିର ପ୍ରଶଂସା ବା ଅଭିଜ୍ଞ ଲୋକଙ୍କ ଆଉ ଶିଖିବାର ନାହିଁ ବୋଲି ରାୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: An unnecessary lesson becomes the joke; our application asks about prior experience.
entries.odia_summary: ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିଥିବା କାମ ଶିଖାଇବାକୁ ନେଇ ମଜା; ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ପୂର୍ବ ଅଭିଜ୍ଞତାକୁ ଜାଣିବା ଜରୁରୀ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ନୂଆ ସହକର୍ମୀ ଫାଇଲ ସଜାଇବା ଶିଖାଇବାକୁ ଯାଉଥିଲେ। ରୀତା କହିଲେ, “ଏହି ପଦ୍ଧତିଟା ମୁଁ ତିଆରି କରିଥିଲି; ତୁମ ପାଖରେ କିଛି ନୂଆ ଉପାୟ ଅଛି କି?” / A colleague begins explaining a filing method to its creator, who remains open to improvements. This scene is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The saying accompanies sense1, proficiency through practice. Sense2 separately describes an elderly thief. Neither establishes a real offender or an age-group trait.

entries.odia: ଯାହା ଘରେ ରହେ ଯୁବା ଝିଅ, ବିନା ନିଆଁରେ ପୋଡ଼େ ତା ଦିହ
entries.title: Burning without fire
entries.literal_meaning: Provisional reading: Whoever has a grown daughter at home burns in body without fire.
entries.explanation: The line makes a grown daughter’s presence the occasion for burning without flame. It does not state marriage, dowry, a cause of distress or an actual injury. Our critical response refuses to turn that charged comparison into a verdict that daughters are burdens. Asking whose worry is being voiced leaves the young woman’s own perspective open.
entries.meaning_odia: ବଢ଼ିଲା ଝିଅ ଘରେ ଥିବା ସହିତ ନିଆଁ ବିନା ଦେହ ପୋଡ଼ିବାର ତୀବ୍ର ଛବି ଯୋଡ଼ାଯାଇଛି। ଏଠି ବିବାହ, ଯୌତୁକ, ଦୁଃଖର କାରଣ ବା ପ୍ରକୃତ ଆଘାତ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପାଠ ଏହାକୁ ଝିଅମାନେ ବୋଝ ବୋଲି ରାୟ କରେନାହିଁ। କାହାର ଚିନ୍ତା ଏଠି କୁହାଯାଉଛି ବୋଲି ପଚାରିଲେ ଝିଅଟିର ନିଜ ଦୃଷ୍ଟିଭଙ୍ଗୀ ପାଇଁ ମଧ୍ୟ ଜାଗା ରହେ। ଦେହଟି କାହାର, ଉତ୍ସ ତାହା ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ କରେନାହିଁ; ଏହି ପାଠ ସମ୍ଭାବ୍ୟ, ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ଅର୍ଥ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical response questions the burden implied by the fireless-burning image.
entries.odia_summary: ନିଆଁ ବିନା ପୋଡ଼ିବାର ଛବିରେ ଥିବା ବୋଝର ଇଙ୍ଗିତକୁ ଆମ ପାଠ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ ପଚାରିଲେ, “ଏଠି କାହାର ଚିନ୍ତା?” ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ କହିଲେ, “ଝିଅଟି ନିଜେ କଣ କହିବ, ସେଥି ବି ଶୁଣିବା ଦରକାର।” / Readers ask whose anxiety the line expresses and leave room for the daughter’s voice. Their discussion is invented, not a collected traditional explanation.
entries.cultural_context: The dictionary defines a daughter who has reached puberty. The pronoun’s bodily subject is not further explained; the literal reading remains provisional. No present-day family or community trait is established.

entries.title: Near enough to attend to
entries.literal_meaning: Cultivation where it can be regularly seen; dwellings close together.
entries.explanation: The accompanying adjective means something that can often be seen or attended to. The line pairs that accessibility in cultivation with proximity in living. Our reading asks what distance permits us to notice and care for; it does not prescribe settlement density or promise better harvests.
entries.meaning_odia: ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ବିଶେଷଣର ଅର୍ଥ—ଯାହାକୁ ବାରମ୍ବାର ଦେଖି ବା ତାହାର ତତ୍ତ୍ୱ ନେଇହେବ। ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଚାଷରେ ସେହି ସୁବିଧା ସହିତ ଲଗାଲଗି ରହିବାକୁ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଆମ ପାଠ ପଚାରେ, ଦୂରତା କେଉଁ କାମର ତତ୍ତ୍ୱ ନେବାରେ ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ବା ବାଧା ଦିଏ। ଏହା ଘରବସତିର ନିୟମ ବା ଭଲ ଫସଲର ନିଶ୍ଚୟତା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading connects proximity with the possibility of regular attention.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ପାଖରେ ଥିବାକୁ ବାରମ୍ବାର ତତ୍ତ୍ୱ ନେବାର ସୁବିଧା ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠାଗାରର ମରାମତି ଖାତାଟି ଦୂର ଆଲମାରିରେ ରହୁଥିଲା। ସ୍ୱେଚ୍ଛାସେବୀମାନେ ତାହାକୁ କାମର ଟେବୁଲ ପାଖରେ ରଖିଲେ, ଯେପରି ରୋଜ ଦେଖିପାରିବେ। / Volunteers move a repair log near their worktable so they can check it daily. This practical analogy is invented.
entries.cultural_context: This is the adjective-sense example, separate from the earlier river/kinship saying and later named literary line. No agricultural trial or universal village pattern is established.

entries.title: You turned away from me
entries.literal_meaning: Newness lasts how many days? Seeing the new, you forgot the old and turned your back on me.
entries.explanation: The speaker protests being forgotten when something new appears. The source places the saying under neglect, but identifies neither the relationship nor the new attraction. Our reading attends to the person left out of another’s enthusiasm, without making every change a betrayal.
entries.meaning_odia: ନୂଆ କିଛି ଦେଖି ପୁରୁଣାକୁ ଭୁଲିଯିବାରେ ବକ୍ତା ନିଜ ପ୍ରତି ଅବହେଳାର କଥା କହୁଛନ୍ତି। ଅଭିଧାନ ଏହାକୁ ଅନାସ୍ଥା ଅର୍ଥରେ ଦେଇଛି; ସମ୍ପର୍କଟି କଣ ବା ନୂଆ ଆକର୍ଷଣଟି କଣ, କହିନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କ ଉତ୍ସାହ ଭିତରେ ବାଦ୍ ପଡ଼ିଥିବା ଲୋକର ସ୍ୱର ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ସବୁ ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱାସଘାତ କୁହାଯାଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: An unnamed speaker protests neglect after a new attraction appears.
entries.odia_summary: ନୂଆ ଆକର୍ଷଣ ଆସିବା ପରେ ଅବହେଳା ପାଇଥିବା ଜଣଙ୍କର ପ୍ରତିବାଦ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ନୂଆ ପ୍ରକଳ୍ପରେ ସମସ୍ତେ ବ୍ୟସ୍ତ ଥିଲେ। ପୁରୁଣା ଦଳର ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ଆମ କାମର ଖବର ବି ନିଅ।” ସେମାନେ ଦୁଇ ଦଳର ଆଲୋଚନା ପାଇଁ ସମୟ ରଖିଲେ। / An established team asks not to be forgotten during a new project. The shared meeting is an invented continuation.
entries.cultural_context: The exact source does not identify lovers, spouses, friends or a historical occasion. The opening question and addressed protest are retained without supplying those roles.

entries.title: An unexpected claimant
entries.literal_meaning: Even when there is no rival, an unexpected claimant appears.
entries.explanation: The headword defines an unexpected rival, enemy or claimant to a share. The saying contrasts apparent absence with sudden arrival. Our application notices how a settled expectation can be interrupted; it does not prove that the newcomer’s claim is false or that every undertaking must meet opposition.
entries.meaning_odia: ଅଭିଧାନରେ ହଠାତ୍ ଆସୁଥିବା ପ୍ରତିଦ୍ୱନ୍ଦ୍ୱୀ, ଶତ୍ରୁ ବା ଭାଗ ଦାବି କରୁଥିବା ଲୋକକୁ ବୁଝାଯାଇଛି। କେହି ନଥିବା କଥା ପାଖରେ ହଠାତ୍ କେହି ବାହାରିବା ରଖାଯାଇଛି। ଆମ ପ୍ରୟୋଗରେ ଧରିନିଆ କଥା କିପରି ବଦଳିପାରେ, ତାହା ଦିଶେ। ନୂଆ ଲୋକର ଦାବି ମିଛ ବା ପ୍ରତ୍ୟେକ କାମରେ ବିରୋଧୀ ଆସିବେ ବୋଲି ଏହା ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading notices an unexpected challenge without judging its legitimacy.
entries.odia_summary: ଅପେକ୍ଷା ବାହାରର ଦାବିକୁ ଆମ ପାଠ ଦେଖେ; ତାହାର ଯଥାର୍ଥତା ଉପରେ ରାୟ ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଘରଟି ଖାଲି ବୋଲି ଦଳ ଭାବିଥିଲା। ଅନ୍ୟ ଦଳ ଆସି ନିଜ ବୁକିଂ ଦେଖାଇଲା। ସେମାନେ ଖାତା ମିଳାଇ ଦେଖିଲେ। / Another group arrives with a booking for a room thought to be free; both check the register. The scene is invented, not a property dispute report.
entries.cultural_context: The supplied gloss governs the compound here; no journey, festival, property law or named dispute is reconstructed from its parts.

entries.title: A ring does not change the blow
entries.literal_meaning: A slap from a gold-ringed hand brings the benefit of bathing in the Ganga.
entries.explanation: The saying gives a blow from an adorned hand the value of a sacred bath. Our critical reading questions that elevation: an ornament does not make harm deserved or beneficial. This is our response to the line, not a supplied traditional counter-moral or a claim of ritual efficacy.
entries.meaning_odia: ସୁନାମୁଦି ପିନ୍ଧା ହାତର ଚାପୁଡ଼ାକୁ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଗଙ୍ଗାସ୍ନାନର ଫଳ ସହିତ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପାଠ ସେହି ମୂଲ୍ୟଦାନକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରେ—ଅଳଙ୍କାର ଥିବାରୁ ଆଘାତ ଯୋଗ୍ୟ ବା ଉପକାରୀ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ଏହା ଆମ ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା; ଉତ୍ସରେ ଦିଆଯାଇଥିବା ପାରମ୍ପରିକ ବିପରୀତ ଉପଦେଶ ବା ଧାର୍ମିକ ଫଳର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical response separates an adorned hand from any justification for its blow.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପ୍ରତିକ୍ରିୟା ଅଳଙ୍କାରକୁ ଆଘାତର ଯଥାର୍ଥତାଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ହାତରେ ଦାମୀ ଜିନିଷ ଥିଲେ ଆଘାତ ବଦଳିଯାଏ କି?” ଅନ୍ୟମାନେ ଅଳଙ୍କାର ଓ ବ୍ୟବହାରକୁ ଅଲଗା କରି ଆଲୋଚନା କଲେ। / Readers distinguish adornment from conduct. This discussion is invented; no assault is depicted or reported.
entries.cultural_context: The first duplicated headword block supplies this wording. A second repeats altered spellings; neither is silently repaired. The earlier Krishna Singh Mahabharata illustration is separate, not this saying’s authorship.

entries.title: Concealing it from the skilled observer
entries.literal_meaning: Like hiding one’s belly from the midwife.
entries.explanation: The example follows the definition of a skilled midwife. Our reading takes the contrast as attempted concealment from someone familiar with the matter. It is an analogy about expertise, not proof that any practitioner knows everything or a demand to disclose intimate information.
entries.meaning_odia: ଦକ୍ଷ ପ୍ରସବସହାୟିକାର ସଂଜ୍ଞା ପରେ ଏହି ତୁଳନା ଆସିଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ, ଯିଏ ବିଷୟଟି ଜାଣନ୍ତି ତାଙ୍କଠାରୁ ସେହି କଥା ଲୁଚାଇବାର ଚେଷ୍ଟା ଏଠି ଦିଶେ। ଏହା ଦକ୍ଷତାକୁ ନେଇ ଉପମା; କେହି ସବୁ ଜାଣନ୍ତି ବା ନିଜର ଗୋପନ କଥା କହିବାକୁ ବାଧ୍ୟ ବୋଲି ନିୟମ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading concerns attempted concealment from someone with relevant experience.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ସମ୍ପୃକ୍ତ ଅଭିଜ୍ଞତା ଥିବା ଲୋକଙ୍କଠାରୁ କଥା ଲୁଚାଇବାର ଚେଷ୍ଟାକୁ ଦେଖେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଭଙ୍ଗା କବାଟର ଖରାପ କବଜାଟିକୁ ରଙ୍ଗରେ ଢାଙ୍କିଦିଆଗଲା। ମରାମତି କାରିଗର କବାଟ ଖୋଲି ସେହି ତ୍ରୁଟି ଦେଖିଲେ। / A repairer notices a faulty hinge beneath fresh paint. This invented analogy is not a medical encounter.
entries.cultural_context: The source labels this a Dhaga comparison under midwife, distinct from the earlier wet-nurse sense. No diagnosis, historical incident or customary disclosure rule is established.

entries.title: A household’s changing circumstances
entries.literal_meaning: At times, a home with two wives; at times, blow and blow at the hearth until you die.
entries.explanation: The repeated “at times” turns a household image into an exhausting cooking complaint. The source gives no cause for the change. Our critical reading notices that the contrast relies on an expectation of women’s kitchen labour; describing that expectation does not make cooking their obligation.
entries.meaning_odia: ବାରମ୍ବାର ଆସୁଥିବା “କେତେବେଳେ” ଘରର ଚିତ୍ରକୁ ରାନ୍ଧି ରାନ୍ଧି ହାଲିଆ ହେବାର ଅଭିଯୋଗ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଏହି ବଦଳର କାରଣ ଉତ୍ସ କହେନାହିଁ। ଆମ ସମାଲୋଚନାମୂଳକ ପାଠରେ ଏଠି ନାରୀଙ୍କ ରୋଷେଇ ଶ୍ରମ ଉପରେ ଆଶା ରଖାଯାଇଛି; ସେହି ଆଶାକୁ ବୁଝିବା ଅର୍ଥ ରୋଷେଇ କେବଳ ତାଙ୍କ ଦାୟିତ୍ୱ ବୋଲି ମାନିବା ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our critical reading distinguishes a household complaint from an obligation imposed on women.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଘରର ଅଭିଯୋଗକୁ ନାରୀଙ୍କ ଉପରେ ଥୋପାଯାଇଥିବା ଦାୟିତ୍ୱଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ପଢ଼ି ସମସ୍ତେ ରୋଷେଇ କାମ କିଏ କରେ ବୋଲି ଆଲୋଚନା କଲେ। ନିଜ ସଭାର ଭୋଜନ ପାଇଁ ସେମାନେ କାମ ବାଣ୍ଟିନେଲେ। / Readers discuss the complaint and share the work of preparing their meeting’s meal. This response is invented, not the saying’s traditional moral.
entries.cultural_context: The quotation follows the figurative cooking sense. Its death wording is rhetorical here, not an established death event; no marriage history or reason for absence is supplied.

entries.title: Grain ripens, an elder dances
entries.literal_meaning: Gulji suan ripened; the Kharia elder danced.
entries.explanation: The line joins ripening grain to one elder’s dance. The dictionary’s note describes gathering and cooking this grain. Our reading attends to the connection between available food and delight, without making the named figure stand for everyone in a community or turning the dance into a documented ritual.
entries.meaning_odia: ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଶସ୍ୟ ପାଚିବା ସହ ଜଣେ ବୃଦ୍ଧଙ୍କ ନାଚକୁ ଯୋଡ଼େ। ଅଭିଧାନର ଟୀକାରେ ଏହି ଶସ୍ୟ ସଂଗ୍ରହ କରି ରାନ୍ଧିବା କଥା ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ମିଳିବା ଓ ଆନନ୍ଦର ସମ୍ପର୍କକୁ ଦେଖେ; ଜଣେ ପାତ୍ରକୁ ପୂରା ସମୁଦାୟର ସ୍ୱଭାବ ବା ନାଚକୁ ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ପର୍ବ ବୋଲି ଧରେନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading follows the verse’s food-and-delight connection without generalising a community.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଓ ଆନନ୍ଦର ଯୋଗକୁ ଦେଖେ, ସମୁଦାୟ ବିଷୟରେ ସାଧାରଣ ନିୟମ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ କହିଲେ, “ଏହି ଲୋକଟିର ଆନନ୍ଦକୁ ଦେଖିବା, ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କ ସ୍ୱଭାବ ବୋଲି କହିବା ନାହିଁ।” / A reader asks the group to attend to the individual’s delight rather than make a community stereotype. This discussion is invented.
entries.cultural_context: Sambalpur labels the headword, not a proven saying origin. The historical note’s community and poverty classifications remain attributed source language, not present-day ethnography or botanical identification.

entries.odia: ଧନ୍ୟ ସେ ପ୍ରଜାପତି, ବରକୁ କନ୍ୟା ଘଟାଘଟି
entries.title: A fitting pair
entries.literal_meaning: Blessed is that Prajapati: bride and groom suit each other.
entries.explanation: The headword here means suiting one another. The line praises a pairing through an invocation of Prajapati, whose precise referent is not explained here. Our reading attends to mutual fit rather than judging either person alone. Whether a particular use is sincere or ironic would depend on its setting.
entries.meaning_odia: ଏଠି ଘଟାଘଟିର ଅର୍ଥ ପରସ୍ପରକୁ ମାନିବା ବା ଉପଯୋଗୀ ହେବା। ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ପ୍ରଜାପତିଙ୍କୁ ଧନ୍ୟ କହି ଯୋଡ଼ିର ମେଳକୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସା କରେ; ପ୍ରଜାପତି କାହାକୁ ବୁଝାଏ ଏଠି ସ୍ପଷ୍ଟ ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠ ଜଣକୁ ଅଲଗା ବିଚାରିବା ବଦଳେ ପରସ୍ପରର ମେଳକୁ ଦେଖେ। କଥାଟି ସରଳ ପ୍ରଶଂସା କି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗ, ତାହା ପ୍ରୟୋଗର ପରିସ୍ଥିତି ଉପରେ ନିର୍ଭର କରିବ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading follows the source’s mutual-fit gloss without fixing the speaker’s tone.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ପରସ୍ପରର ମେଳକୁ ଦେଖେ, ବକ୍ତାଙ୍କ ସ୍ୱରକୁ ନିଶ୍ଚିତ କରେନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଜଣେ ପାଠକ ଦୁଇ ଚରିତ୍ରର ଯୋଡ଼ିକୁ ପ୍ରଶଂସା କଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ପଚାରିଲେ, “କେଉଁ କଥାରେ ସେମାନେ ପରସ୍ପରକୁ ମାନନ୍ତି?” / Readers discuss why two fictional characters make a fitting pair. This scene is invented, not a marriage custom or compatibility test.
entries.cultural_context: Adjective sense4 supplies the gloss; intervening dying/critical-moment senses do not apply. No marriage arrangement, mythic incident or independently verified compatibility is asserted.

entries.title: Will this fill the belly?
entries.literal_meaning: Cane berries full of bones—will eating them fill the belly?
entries.explanation: The question sets the berry’s apparent bulk against what it offers to eat. The dictionary describes a layer around the seed, which helps us read the bone image. Our editorial application asks whether something supplies enough usable substance for its purpose; it is not a nutritional verdict about the fruit.
entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ଫଳର ଆକାର ସହ ତାହାର ଖାଇବା ଅଂଶକୁ ତୁଳନା କରେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ମଞ୍ଜି ଉପରେ ଏକ ସ୍ତର ଥିବା କଥା ଅଛି; ସେଥିରୁ ହାଡ଼ର ଚିତ୍ରଟି ବୁଝିହୁଏ। ଆମ ସମ୍ପାଦକୀୟ ପ୍ରୟୋଗ ପଚାରେ, କୌଣସି ଜିନିଷରେ କାମ ପାଇଁ ଯଥେଷ୍ଟ ସାର ଅଛି କି। ଏହା ଫଳର ପୋଷଣ ବିଷୟରେ ରାୟ ନୁହେଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our application asks about usable substance, not the fruit’s measured food value.

entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଏକ ପୁସ୍ତିକାରେ ଅନେକ ସଜାଯାଇଥିବା ପୃଷ୍ଠା ଥିଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ କାମଟି କରିବାର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ଅଳ୍ପ। ପାଠକମାନେ ଦରକାରୀ ପଦକ୍ଷେପ ଯୋଡ଼ିବାକୁ କହିଲେ। / Readers ask for practical steps in a booklet with many decorated pages but little guidance. This comparison is invented.

entries.title: An insult and a plea
entries.literal_meaning: You call me a loose woman; do not go to live elsewhere.
entries.explanation: The reply places a plea not to leave beside a degrading name. Its position follows the dictionary’s pejorative sense, not its separate slender-body senses. Our critical reading keeps the speaker’s request distinct from accepting the insult. The source does not identify the relationship or explain why the speaker asks the other person not to leave.

entries.explanation: The line calls a statement true while registering a failure of belief. The headword’s second sense supplies that reading of the shortened ending. Our interpretation attends to the gap between asserting truth and finding something convincing; the line itself does not establish whether an unnamed statement is actually true.

entries.title: The nearby voice
entries.literal_meaning: The one who sleeps nearby speaks into the ear—can their words be distrusted?
entries.explanation: The question gives a nearby voice an apparent advantage. The dictionary places it under backbiting, making access to the listener part of the image. entries.meaning_odia: ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଟି ପାଖରେ ଥିବା ସ୍ୱରକୁ ଏକ ସୁବିଧା ଦେଉଥିବା ପରି ଲାଗେ। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଏହା ଚୁଗୁଲି କହିବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ନିକଟତାକୁ ବିଶ୍ୱସନୀୟତାଠାରୁ ଅଲଗା କରେ—ଏକାନ୍ତରେ ଶୁଣିଲେ ବୋଲି କଥାଟି ସତ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। ବକ୍ତା ପତି ବା ପତ୍ନୀ, କେଉଁ ଲିଙ୍ଗର ବା କେଉଁ ଅଭିଯୋଗ କରୁଛନ୍ତି, ଉତ୍ସ ତାହା କହେନାହିଁ।

entries.title: The fish advertises its worth
entries.literal_meaning: The bhakuda fish said: I am king among fish; make broth from my head and see how enjoyable it is.
entries.explanation: The talking fish supports its royal claim with an offer of its own head for cooking. Our reading follows that odd self-advertisement: praise of its worth comes through what someone else might enjoy. This is a playful reading of the boast, not a supplied moral about sacrifice or a tested cooking recommendation.

entries.title: Someone else wears the blame
entries.literal_meaning: The villagers ate the jackfruit; they smeared its sticky substance on Bhandari’s head.
entries.explanation: The eaters and the person marked by the sticky residue are different. The headword explicitly explains laying blame or stigma on someone. Our reading follows that transfer: the visible mark is made to point away from those who acted. It is a way to question an accusation, not evidence about any community’s conduct.
entries.meaning_odia: ପଣସ ଖାଇଥିବା ଲୋକ ଓ ମୁଣ୍ଡରେ ଅଠା ବୋଳାଯାଇଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତି ଅଲଗା। ଶବ୍ଦର ଅର୍ଥରେ କାହା ଉପରେ ଦୋଷ ବା କଳଙ୍କ ଦେବା କଥା ଅଛି। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଦାଗଟି ପ୍ରକୃତ କାର୍ଯ୍ୟକାରୀଙ୍କ ବଦଳରେ ଅନ୍ୟଜଣଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷୀ ଦେଖାଉଛି। ଏହା ଅଭିଯୋଗକୁ ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ କରିବାର ପାଠ, କୌଣସି ସମୁଦାୟର ଆଚରଣର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।

entries.title: A hard division between working and asking
entries.literal_meaning: Whoever works does not eat by asking; whoever eats by asking does not earn food through work.
entries.explanation: The paired clauses draw an absolute line between labour and asking for food. The headword supplies earning a livelihood through work. Our critical response questions the absolute division: the saying does not establish why anyone needs help or whether their work meets their needs. That response is editorial, not a counter-moral supplied by the dictionary.

entries.title: Let the hair fall
entries.literal_meaning: Let the hair loose, let it fall to the waist; let a hundred thousand champa flowers fall.
entries.explanation: The invitation to loosen the hair opens into an extravagant fall of flowers. The headword’s second sense supports letting hair loose. We read the line as a lyrical image, allowing its abundance to remain playful rather than supplying a practical lesson. The source labels it Dhaga but provides no occasion or explanation of the flower image.

entries.title: Was the remark meant for you?
entries.literal_meaning: You are not the one; why are you taking it personally?
entries.explanation: The speaker denies that the listener is the target, then questions the listener’s hurt. The dictionary places the line under taking something personally, not accepting responsibility. Our reading asks how the intended target and the felt effect may differ. The speaker’s denial does not prove that the listener has no reason to be hurt.

entries.title: The wedding is tomorrow

entries.explanation: The line puts a question beside an approaching event: today, then tomorrow. The headword explains mangana through the eve of a marriage. entries.odia: ହରି ନାମକୁ ବାନ୍ଧିଥିବୁ ଭେଳା
entries.title: A raft made of Hari’s name
entries.literal_meaning: Keep Hari’s name bound as a raft.
entries.explanation: The divine name becomes the material of an imagined raft. The dictionary places this line under using a means to accomplish something, after the literal raft-making sense. Our reading keeps that devotional metaphor without supplying an unnamed destination or guaranteed result. The source does not describe a particular crossing or establish the practice’s efficacy.
entries.meaning_odia: ହରିନାମ ଏଠାରେ କଳ୍ପିତ ଭେଳାର ଉପାଦାନ ହେଉଛି। ଅଭିଧାନରେ ଧାଡ଼ିଟି କାର୍ଯ୍ୟ ସାଧନ ପାଇଁ ଉପାୟ ଅବଲମ୍ବନ କରିବା ଅର୍ଥ ତଳେ ଅଛି; ତାପୂର୍ବରୁ ପ୍ରକୃତ ଭେଳା ତିଆରି କରିବା ଅର୍ଥ ରହିଛି। ଆମ ପାଠ ଭକ୍ତିମୂଳକ ରୂପକକୁ ରଖେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଅକୁହା ଗନ୍ତବ୍ୟ ବା ନିଶ୍ଚିତ ଫଳ ଯୋଡ଼େନାହିଁ। କୌଣସି ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ପାରିହେବା ଘଟଣା ବା ସାଧନାର ସଫଳତା ଏଥିରୁ ପ୍ରମାଣିତ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading preserves the devotional means-image without promising its outcome.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଭକ୍ତିର ଉପାୟ-ଚିତ୍ରକୁ ରଖେ, ଫଳର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ଦିଏନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ଜଣେ ପାଠକ ନାମରୁ ଭେଳା ହେବାର ରୂପକ ଆଲୋଚନା କଲେ। ସେ ଏହାକୁ ପ୍ରକୃତ ନୌକାର ସୁରକ୍ଷା ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ଭାବେ ପଢ଼ିଲେ ନାହିଁ। / A reader discusses the metaphor rather than treating it as boating advice. This discussion is invented.
entries.cultural_context: No sect, author, salvation guarantee or life-ocean setting is supplied. Earlier B31 religious-boat wording shares imagery but is not certified as the same saying.

entries.odia: ଚୋରି କରିବ, ମହତ ଲୋକର ହାବୁଡ଼େ ପଡ଼ିବ
entries.title: Wrongdoing meets magnanimity
entries.literal_meaning: You will steal; you will encounter a magnanimous person.
entries.explanation: The line brings theft and an encounter with a magnanimous person together. The first dictionary sense supplies generosity of character, not merely wealth or rank. Our reading attends to the tension between the act and the person encountered. It leaves the encounter’s result open: the source promises neither pardon nor reform and is not a recommendation to steal.
entries.meaning_odia: ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଚୋରି ଓ ଜଣେ ଉଦାରମନା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ସହ ଭେଟକୁ ପାଖାପାଖି ରଖେ। ଅଭିଧାନର ପ୍ରଥମ ଅର୍ଥରେ ଉଦାରତା ଅଛି, କେବଳ ଧନ ବା ପଦମର୍ଯ୍ୟାଦା ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପାଠ କାମଟି ଓ ଭେଟୁଥିବା ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିଙ୍କ ଗୁଣ ମଧ୍ୟର ଟାଣକୁ ଦେଖେ। ଭେଟର ଫଳ ଅକୁହା ରହେ—କ୍ଷମା ବା ଚରିତ୍ର ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନର ପ୍ରତିଶ୍ରୁତି ନାହିଁ। ଏହାକୁ ଚୋରି କରିବାର ପରାମର୍ଶ ଭାବେ ନିଆଯାଉନାହିଁ।
entries.english_summary: Our reading keeps the encounter unresolved instead of inventing forgiveness.
entries.odia_summary: ଆମ ପାଠ ଭେଟର ଫଳକୁ ଅକୁହା ରଖେ, କ୍ଷମାର ଘଟଣା ଯୋଡ଼େନାହିଁ।
entries.usage_example: Original imagined example: ପାଠଚକ୍ରରେ ଜଣେ ଶେଷରେ କ୍ଷମା ମିଳିବ ବୋଲି ଭାବିଲେ। ଅନ୍ୟଜଣ ମନେ ପକାଇଲେ, ଧାଡ଼ିରେ ଫଳ କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ। / Readers distinguish their expected ending from what is actually stated. This discussion is invented.
entries.cultural_context: The quotation follows magnanimous sense1, not the later saintly sense3. No historical incident, immunity, compulsory mercy or fixed traditional moral is established.
